````markdown
## §6 discipline: fable R1-B3, codex B03, B04, B05, muse B5 — resolved

At `0164b5a` the codex job had already fixed the round-1 witnesses except one:
codex B03(b), `h t; h t; d = qcopy t; quncopy t d`, was rejected because the
closed-window set was permanent. A window now opens at its computation:
`Discipline::closed` counts window-closing events per wire and each `Creation`
snapshots the counts of its dependencies (`window_closed`).

The council asked for a sound checker, so I added a differential test that
does not depend on anyone's reading: `tests/r1_fuzz_discipline.rs` generates
random actions (compute, middle and possibly mutated uncompute sequences, qif,
qloop, nested predicates, local regions, qload/qstore) and requires every
statically accepted one to run exactly clean on all basis inputs and on a
superposed input, forward and adjoint, using the exact simulator (B15). It
found four unsound accepts, all also accepted at `0164b5a`:

1. `h d0; ccx d0 p d1; cx d1 t; ccx d0 p d1; h d0` released d0 entangled with
   t: recorded reads were not transitive. `note_reads` now records the
   transitive dependency set.
2. The same through a predicate: `change` rebuilt each operation key by
   splitting its version at `":context"`, which also occurs inside nested
   snapshots, so the key was wrong and the recorded reads silently fell back to
   direct reads. The key is now taken before formatting.
3. A diagonal phase on a perm value that depends on an `other` value kicks back
   onto it (`h d0; cx d0 d1; cz d1 t; cx d0 d1; h d0`): outstanding diagonal
   phases are now tracked (`Discipline::phases`) and block the adjoint of the
   `other` values they depend on.
4. Gate operation identities used predicate names, not versions, for `other`
   targets (the fable R1-B3 class): versions now include every control and
   effective-control wire's version.

The ignored 200,000-program sweep then accepts 82,797 programs and every one
runs clean (`PROGRESS.md`).

Tests (`tests/r1_discipline.rs`): `fable_r1_b3_predicate_flip_closes_the_window`
(both witnesses and both positive controls),
`codex_b03_predicate_versions_and_windows_start_at_the_computation`,
`codex_b04_qif_arms_are_complementary_and_loops_compose`,
`codex_b05_quantum_memory_cleanup_and_restoration`,
`codex_b05_child_call_advances_loaded_cells`,
`muse_b5_loop_bodies_are_validated_per_iteration`,
`fuzz_witnesses_of_entangling_reads_are_rejected`; each accepted positive is
also executed. RED: codex B03(b) and the fuzz witnesses FAIL; the others pass
(fixed by the codex job after `3dea965`).

SPEC-QUESTIONS 25: the literal §6.2 sentence "other values are released only by
the adjoint of the sequence that produced them" admits witness 1; the crate
implements the stronger reading T5 needs, with a proposed 0.9 wording.

`src/schema.rs` `validate_call_graph` builds the graph from structured region
calls, `lift.oracle_call`/`lift.oracle_uncall`/`lift.perm_call`, `qinplace`
pairs and `lift.call`, finds strongly connected components, and rejects any
component containing an edge other than `lift.call` (§5.1 "recursion exists
only through lift.call"). Test: `tests/r1_rules.rs`
`b02_region_recursion_through_lifted_calls_is_rejected` (the self-calling
oracle and the action → oracle → lift.perm_call cycle rejected; `sum_db` still
parses). RED: FAIL.

## codex B06 — local qregion as a call operand — resolved (at 0164b5a)

Fixed by the codex job after `3dea965`. Pinned by `tests/r1_rules.rs`
`b06_local_qregion_passed_to_a_child_action`: parent `qregion r 3 1 @img`
passes `r` to a child that loads cell p, XORs it into t and unloads; for all
p ∈ 0..8 and t ∈ {0, 1}, t ends as t ⊕ bit p of 0xa5, p is unchanged, and the
adjoint restores the state exactly.

## codex B07 — qinplace — resolved

At load (`validation.rs`, `qinplace` arm) @g and @ginv must be oracles mapping
one wire[n] input to a wire[n] target with no mem and no args and one fault
width (the §4.5 expansion names none). At execution (`action.rs`
`verify_inverse_pair`), before any state change, both oracles run on every
n-bit input under the actual token: FAULT_NONE everywhere and
g∘ginv = ginv∘g = id, else a §4.5 error. Tests (`tests/r1_qinplace.rs`):
`b07_zero_zero_pair_is_rejected_before_mutation` (B = 1 and B = 2, both t,
state unchanged), `b07_not_not_pair_executes_controlled_and_adjoint` (fails at
B = 2, inverts at B = 3, controlled on c, adjoint), and
`b07_interfaces_are_checked_at_load`. RED: 3 FAIL. qinplace had no test at
all before. SPEC-QUESTIONS 26.

## codex B08 — matched oracle uncall — resolved

`src/call_discipline.rs` `validate_matched_oracle_calls` is now a forward
dataflow over the row CFG: each `lift.oracle_uncall` must have an outstanding
`lift.oracle_call` with identical operands on every incoming path (multisets
meet by pointwise minimum), consuming one. An outstanding call is invalidated
by any write to its ins, tgt or fr other than oracle XOR delivery (which
commutes) and by a possible write to a supplied cell: a store whose address is
a known `lift.addr` constant outside the region does not invalidate; an
unknown address, a perm call with a mut region, or a `lift.call` whose closure
stores does. Tests (`tests/r1_rules.rs`):
`b08_two_calls_then_two_matched_uncalls` (input 8, tk = (3,0,0,0), B = 5:
(0, 0, 5); a third uncall is rejected), `b08_disjoint_global_store_between_a_matched_pair`
(store to global g at 32, region db at 16: accepted and run to (0, 0, 6);
store through `lift.addr @db`: rejected). RED: both FAIL.

## codex B09 — whole-run reversal — resolved

`src/classical.rs` `reverse`: history traversal undoes frame effects and skips
reversed frames and uncall markers (§7.4); afterwards the run's administrative
control (activation stack, next instance id, fault/finished/pending) is the
control recorded before the first frame, so a run whose first frame opens a
later-cancelled segment ends at its entry. Test: `b09_whole_run_reversal_after_an_initial_cancelled_segment`
(`main: call @f; uncall @f () (); ret`, `f: ret`; run(4) and reversal twice).
RED: FAIL.

## codex B10 — ptr arguments — resolved

`src/oracle.rs` `check_argument` is the one §3.3 classical-argument check for
oracles, actions and CC region calls (ptr included). Test:
`b10_pointer_arguments_reach_permutation_actions` (B = 2: (1, 0, 2), machine
agrees and reverses; p = 2^32 rejected). RED: FAIL.

## codex B11 — block order — resolved

`src/validation.rs` `validate_classical` types definitions to a fixpoint
(`classical_instruction`), independent of block text order. Reading a name
with no instance on the executed path is FAULT_UB_TRAP. Test:
`b11_classical_definitions_need_not_precede_uses_in_text` (run(4) = 7,
reversal restores entry). RED: FAIL. SPEC-QUESTIONS 24.

## codex B13 — malformed callees — resolved

`src/schema.rs` `validate_local_schemas` checks the §4.8 operand schema of every
structured and classical instruction before any pass reads callee bodies.
Test: `b13_malformed_callee_is_a_diagnostic_never_a_panic` (`Object::parse`
returns a §4.8 error; the CLI exits 1 citing §4.8). RED: FAIL (panic at
`call_discipline.rs:81`).

## codex B14, muse B6 — borrow frames — resolved

`src/borrow.rs` decides P_F = P′ ⊗ I_B exactly: every wire's final value is an
algebraic-normal-form polynomial over the frame's inputs (canonical, so the
decision covers the full domain); loops are composed by repeated squaring;
permutation actions are inlined; quantum memory is multiplexed exactly;
black-box oracle and qinplace calls are canonical symbols when their inputs do
not depend on borrowed wires. The 16-wire cap and the 10^6 loop cap are gone.
The translation lemma remains the structural route. A frame the decision
cannot settle is admitted only through verified certificate `borrow_frames`
claims (`claims.rs` `borrow_frames_certified`), the "library certificate"
route. `Object::verify_certificate` re-executes claims and rejects altered and
incomplete ones.

Tests (`tests/r1_borrow.rs`): `codex_b14_seventeen_wire_swap_identity_frame`
(512 samples, plus the ignored exhaustive 2^17 run),
`muse_b6_eighteen_wire_paired_cx_frame_and_its_dependent_variant`,
`borrow_frames_inside_bounded_loops_are_composed_not_unrolled` (X^(2^40)
accepted and executed; an odd count rejected; the order-3 map cubed accepted,
squared rejected). `tests/r1_certificates.rs`
`b14_checked_borrow_claim_and_altered_or_incomplete_claims` (a proof against an
identity program and against a full table; one wrong table row rejected; a
domain short of D is evidence and is rejected as a borrow_frames proof; a claim
without the borrowed bundle is rejected) and the ignored 17-wire claim. While
running the 2^40-iteration loop I found the executor ran it literally; it now
skips whole periods once its exact state returns to the loop-entry value.
RED: 3 FAIL; the claim tests had no API at `0164b5a`. SPEC-QUESTIONS 20, 21.

## codex B15 — exact cleanliness — resolved

`src/exact.rs`: every amplitude reachable by §4.4 gates lies in
Q(√2, i)[z, 1/z] with dyadic coefficients and z = e^{i·2^−1075}, because every
finite binary64 angle is an integer multiple of 2^−1074; z is transcendental
(Lindemann–Weierstrass), so a Laurent polynomial is zero iff its coefficients
are. `src/quantum.rs` carries this exact shadow beside the binary64 amplitudes
(which now serve only Born probabilities) and decides release, basis reads and
state equality exactly. The superposition form is sparse over arbitrary-width
basis keys, so the fixed 24-wire limit is gone too. Tests (`tests/r1_exact.rs`):
`b15_tiny_rotation_is_not_clean_and_release_changes_nothing` (ry(1e-13) and
rx(1e-300)), `b15_exact_adjoints_release_cleanly`,
`b15_cc_free_of_an_almost_clean_register_traps` (fault 4, handle still live; the
adjoint pair frees cleanly and reverses), `superpositions_have_no_wire_limit`
(a 200-wire GHZ state). RED: 3 FAIL.

## codex B16, muse B7 — metadata and claims — resolved (variant enum declined in part)

At `0164b5a` the codex job had already added typed recursive schemas: the
council's schedule witnesses (boolean, null and negative budgets, phase
"garbage", malformed paths, negative start time) and certificate witnesses
(`versions:false`, false bindings, false composition fields, `{"bogus":1}`
claims, unknown fields) were rejected there; `tests/r1_certificates.rs`
`b16_schedule_values_are_typed` and
`b16_muse_b7_certificate_values_and_claims_are_typed` pin them. Added now:
variants contain no `:` (keys are `<variant>:<controls>`), domain bounds are
exact at any width (`Json::uint_text`), and claims are checked, not just
parsed (`src/claims.rs`, B14). Declined in part: codex objects to
`variant: "banana"`. The specification never lists variant names (§6.4, §11,
§12 only use "variant" as a key component), so rejecting a name would invent
an enum; SPEC-QUESTIONS 11 proposes 0.9 wording.

## codex B17 — certificate composition — resolved

`src/identity.rs`: closure hashes over pinned imports use the pin (§9.3 makes
the linked closure equal it), so a client's closure hash, and its certificate
region, exist before linking. `src/linking.rs` `compose_certificates` unites
region records and multiplicities (equal where they meet), rebinds every hash
including `<hash>:<variant>:<c>` keys and changed schedule hashes (a rebinding
collision is an error, never an overwrite), requires equal versions, dialect
mapping and target bindings, and recomputes `epsilon_total` exactly
(`exact::Decimal`). Tests (`tests/r1_linking.rs`):
`b17_certified_client_and_callee_link_and_compose` (both regions retained,
bindings re-validated by the re-parse, epsilon_total = 3 × 0.25 × 2 + 0.1 =
1.6, client(8) with tk = 3 → (9, 0, 2)), `b17_incompatible_certificates_are_link_errors`,
`interface_region_names_cannot_alias_symbols` (fable's §9.2 suggestion). RED:
3 FAIL. SPEC-QUESTIONS 22.

## codex B18 — fixture audit — resolved

`tests/r1_fixtures.rs` enumerates `tests/fixtures/*.bisa`
(`b18_every_bisa_file_is_audited_and_has_a_comments_file`), shows a corrupted

and checks the inc8 and sum_db fixtures byte-for-byte against the §16.3 text

At `0164b5a` the hand list happened to be complete; at `3dea965` it omitted

## codex B19 — target, launch, schedule and interval-checker modules — partial

Not built in this milestone. `PROGRESS.md` stages them as deliverables 8–11
(launch ABI §10 / suite G; target descriptions §8 / suite E; schedule consumer

## codex B20 — call tiers — resolved

`validation.rs` `classical_instruction`: an R function calls only R functions
and Q regions; a CC function calls CC or R functions; `uncall` follows the same
graph, and a CC segment containing `measure` traps when uncalled (§7.4). The

## muse B3 — effect table at load — resolved

`validation.rs` `validate_effect` checks every §7.3 device operation's name,
operand count and ptr/integer types, and requires the model to be declared;

## muse B4 — `in` wire as a qstore value — declined

§4.6 defines `qstore name a v` as "for each i: under `a == i`, `qxor v
cell_i`", and §5.1 admits `in` wires "as `qcopy`/`qxor` sources": the stored
value is a qxor source and is never modified. `qexchm` exchanges its value
into a cell, so an `in` value there is rejected. Test:
`muse_b4_qstore_value_is_a_qxor_source_and_may_be_in`. SPEC-QUESTIONS 23
proposes adding "qstore values" to the §5.1 list.
````

````markdown
restoration of every returned wire and independence of every other live

spanning a loop remain in its map and are checked only at their actual return.

allocation preceding Borrow is known clean if freed before Return.
````

## `isa_check.py` (549 lines)

````python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pre-flight check for spec/Bennett-ISA-Spec.md (seed of the reference interpreter): the example objects must parse,
their hashes must follow the spec's own envelope rule, and their stated
semantics must hold on a reference interpreter. Run before every council
round (council.py prepare --precheck "python3 tools/isa_check.py").

What it implements (from the spec text; version-pinned by the header line):
  - §16  canonical text: header, section order, data lines, function blocks
  - §9.2 semantic envelope + SCC hashing (Tarjan over @symbol references)
  - §14.1 reference interpreter for the lifted subset the examples use:
         lift.const.iN lift.add lift.sub lift.icmp.* lift.zext.iM lift.mov
         lift.addr lift.boundscheck lift.load.iN lift.call lift.ret
         lift.retval qjump qbranch, with activation records, alloctab
         pre-entries, budgets (steps/depth) and fault codes
Exit 1 on any mismatch; prints what differed.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SPEC = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "spec" / "Bennett-ISA-Spec.md"
SECTION_ORDER = ["symbols", "imports", "functions", "data", "devices", "layout",
                 "schedule", "certificate", "coverage"]
FAULT = {"NONE": 0, "STEPS": 1, "HEAP": 2, "DEPTH": 3, "TRAP": 4, "DIV0": 5,
         "SDIV": 6, "MEMFAULT": 7, "EFFECT": 8, "CALLEE": 9}


def jcs(o):
    return json.dumps(o, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)


def sha(b):
    return hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- parsing

def extract_examples(text):
    """Code blocks that start with 'bennett-object' are example objects."""
    blocks = re.findall(r"```\n(bennett-object[^\n]*\n.*?)```", text, re.S)
    return [b.rstrip("\n") + "\n" for b in blocks]


def parse_object(obj):
    lines = obj.rstrip("\n").split("\n")
    assert lines[0].startswith("bennett-object "), "missing header"
    hdr = dict(kv.split("=") for kv in lines[0].split(" ")[1:])
    sections, cur, order = {}, None, []
    i = 1
    while i < len(lines):
        ln = lines[i]
        if ln == "":
            assert i + 1 < len(lines) and lines[i + 1].startswith("section "), \
                f"blank line not followed by section at line {i}"
            i += 1
            continue
        if ln.startswith("section "):
            cur = ln.split(" ", 1)[1]
            assert cur in SECTION_ORDER, f"unknown section {cur}"
            assert cur not in sections, f"duplicate section {cur}"
            order.append(cur)
            sections[cur] = []
            i += 1
            continue
        assert cur is not None, "content before any section"
        sections[cur].append(ln)
        i += 1
    assert order == [s for s in SECTION_ORDER if s in order], f"section order {order}"
    for s in order:
        if s not in ("functions", "data"):
            assert len(sections[s]) == 1, f"section {s} must be one JSON line"
            sections[s] = json.loads(sections[s][0])
            raw = lines[[k for k, l in enumerate(lines) if l == "section " + s][0] + 1]
            assert jcs(sections[s]) == raw, f"section {s} is not JCS-canonical"
    return hdr, sections


def parse_functions(lines):
    """Split the functions section into functions; each: header, regs, blocks."""
    fns, cur = [], None
    for ln in lines:
        if re.match(r"^(fn (cc|r)|oracle|action|perm_action|lproc) @", ln):
            cur = {"head": ln, "regs": None, "blocks": [], "lines": [ln]}
            m = re.match(r"^(?:fn (?:cc|r)|oracle|action|perm_action|lproc) @([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*) (.*)$", ln)
            cur["kind"] = ln.split(" ")[0] if not ln.startswith("fn") else ln.split(" ")[1]
            cur["name"] = m.group(1)
            # five parenthesised lists
            cur["plists"] = re.findall(r"\(([^()]*)\)", m.group(2))
            fns.append(cur)
        elif ln.startswith("regs "):
            cur["regs"] = ln
            cur["lines"].append(ln)
        elif ln.startswith("^"):
            m = re.match(r"^\^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*)\((.*)\):$", ln)
            cur["blocks"].append({"name": m.group(1), "instrs": []})
            cur["lines"].append(ln)
        else:
            assert cur and cur["blocks"], f"instruction outside a block: {ln}"
            cur["blocks"][-1]["instrs"].append(ln)
            cur["lines"].append(ln)
    return fns


def parse_params(pl):
    out = []
    for p in [x for x in pl.split(", ") if x]:
        name, rest = p.split(":", 1)
        parts = rest.split(" ")
        out.append((name, parts[0], parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else None))
    return out


def parse_regs(regs_line):
    m = re.match(r"^regs \{ (.*) \}", regs_line)
    body = m.group(1).strip()
    d = {}
    for p in [x for x in body.split(", ") if x]:
        n, t = p.split(":")
        d[n] = int(re.match(r"reg\[(\d+)\]", t).group(1))
    return d


def parse_instr(ln):
    lhs, rhs = (ln.split(" = ", 1) if " = " in ln else (None, ln))
    toks = re.findall(r"\([^()]*\)|\S+", rhs)
    op, ops = toks[0], toks[1:]
    return lhs, op, ops


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- hashing

def symbol_refs(fn_lines):
    """References in the body; the header line's own name is a definition."""
    return [m for m in re.findall(r"@([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*)", "\n".join(fn_lines[1:]))]


def layout_leaves(layout):
    leaves = {}
    for k, v in layout.items():
        if k in ("globals", "interface_regions"):
            for n, e in v.items():
                if k == "globals":
                    leaves[f"globals.{n}"] = e
                else:
                    for r, ee in e.items():
                        leaves[f"interface_regions.{n}.{r}"] = ee
        else:
            leaves[k] = v
    return leaves


def closure_set(sym, fn, sections):
    """(data entries, layout leaves) in the symbol's closure set per §9.2."""
    layout = sections.get("layout", {})
    leaves = layout_leaves(layout)
    data = dict(l.split(" ") for l in sections.get("data", []))
    if sym["kind"] == "oracle":
        sel = {k: v for k, v in leaves.items()
               if not (k.startswith("interface_regions.") and not k.startswith(f"interface_regions.{sym['name']}."))}
        imgs = {k: data[k] for k in [v.get("image") for v in sel.values() if isinstance(v, dict)] if k}
        return imgs, sel
    if sym["kind"] == "lproc":
        names = re.findall(r"lift\.addr @([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*)", "\n".join(fn["lines"]))
        sel = {f"globals.{n}": leaves[f"globals.{n}"] for n in names if f"globals.{n}" in leaves}
        imgs = {v["image"]: data[v["image"]] for v in sel.values()}
        return imgs, sel
    return {}, {}


def envelope(version, ptr_width, sig, body_lines, data, leaves, refs):
    parts = [f"isa={version}", f"ptr_width={ptr_width}", jcs(sig)] + body_lines
    parts += [f"data {n} {h}" for n, h in sorted(data.items())]
    parts += [f"layout {k} {jcs(v) if not isinstance(v, int) else v}" for k, v in sorted(leaves.items())]
    parts += list(refs)
    return ("\n".join(parts) + "\n").encode()


def compute_hashes(hdr, sections):
    symbols = {v["name"]: dict(v, index=k) for k, v in sections["symbols"].items()}
    fns = {f["name"]: f for f in parse_functions(sections.get("functions", []))}
    data_lines = dict(l.split(" ") for l in sections.get("data", []))
    names = list(symbols)
    # reference graph over symbols (interface-region names are not symbols)
    graph = {}
    for n in names:
        if n in fns:
            graph[n] = [r for r in symbol_refs(fns[n]["lines"]) if r in symbols]
        else:
            graph[n] = []
    # Tarjan SCC
    index, low, stack, on, sccs, counter = {}, {}, [], set(), [], [0]

    def strong(v):
        index[v] = low[v] = counter[0]; counter[0] += 1
        stack.append(v); on.add(v)
        for w in graph[v]:
            if w not in index:
                strong(w); low[v] = min(low[v], low[w])
            elif w in on:
                low[v] = min(low[v], index[w])
        if low[v] == index[v]:
            comp = []
            while True:
                w = stack.pop(); on.discard(w); comp.append(w)
                if w == v:
                    break
            sccs.append(sorted(comp))
    for v in names:
        if v not in index:
            strong(v)
    scc_of = {v: c for c in sccs for v in c}
    hashes = {}

    def hash_scc(comp):
        # dependencies outside the SCC first
        for v in comp:
            for w in graph[v]:
                if w not in comp and w not in hashes:
                    hash_scc(scc_of[w])
        envs = []
        for v in comp:
            sym = symbols[v]
            if v in fns:
                fn = fns[v]
                body = list(fn["lines"])
                refs = []
                def repl(m):
                    w = m.group(1)
                    if w in comp:
                        return "@$" + str(comp.index(w))
                    if w in symbols:
                        if hashes[w] not in refs:
                            refs.append(hashes[w])
                        return "@" + hashes[w]
                    return m.group(0)
                body = [body[0]] + [re.sub(r"@([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*)", repl, l) for l in body[1:]]
                data, leaves = closure_set(sym, fn, sections)
                envs.append(envelope(hdr["isa"], hdr["ptr_width"], sym["signature"], body, data, leaves, refs))
            else:  # data symbol
                envs.append(envelope(hdr["isa"], hdr["ptr_width"], sym["signature"], [f"{v} {data_lines[v]}"], {}, {}, []))
        if len(comp) == 1 and comp[0] not in graph[comp[0]]:
            hashes[comp[0]] = sha(envs[0])
        else:
            scc_hash = sha(b"".join(envs))
            for i, v in enumerate(comp):
                hashes[v] = sha(f"{scc_hash}:{i}".encode())
    for comp in sccs:
        if comp[0] not in hashes:
            hash_scc(comp)
    return hashes, symbols


# ------------------------------------------------------ reference interpreter

class Fault(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code):
        self.code = code


class Budget(Exception):
    pass


def frame_cells(fn):
    """R_f per §3.7: 3 record cells + |L_f|; L_f = params, result name, regs."""
    nparams = len(parse_params(fn["plists"][0]))
    nresult = len(parse_params(fn["plists"][1]))
    nregs = len(parse_regs(fn["regs"])) if fn["regs"] else 0
    return 3 + nparams + nresult + nregs


def run_oracle(hdr, sections, name, ins, regions, B, depth_limit=64, stack_limit=None):
    fns = {f["name"]: f for f in parse_functions(sections["functions"])}
    oracle = fns[name]
    layout = sections.get("layout", {})
    if stack_limit is None:
        stack_limit = 2 ** layout.get("S_cells", 0)
    leaves = layout_leaves(layout)
    data = dict(l.split(" ") for l in sections.get("data", []))
    # memory + alloctab pre-entries: globals (layout order) then interface regions
    mem, alloctab = {}, []
    for gname, g in layout.get("globals", {}).items():
        img = bytes.fromhex(data[g["image"]])
        for i, b in enumerate(img):
            mem[g["base"] + i] = b
        alloctab.append([g["base"], g["size"], 1, 1])
    irs = layout.get("interface_regions", {}).get(name, {})
    mem_params = parse_params(oracle["plists"][3])
    for (rname, rtype, role) in mem_params:
        A, W = map(int, re.match(r"region\[(\d+),(\d+)\]", rtype).groups())
        base = irs[rname]["base"]
        for i, b in enumerate(regions[rname]):
            mem[base + i] = b
        alloctab.append([base, 2 ** A, 1, 1])
    addr_of = {g: e["base"] for g, e in layout.get("globals", {}).items()}
    addr_of.update({r: irs[r]["base"] for r in irs})
    ptr_mask = (1 << int(hdr["ptr_width"])) - 1
    state = {"steps": 0, "depth": 0, "result": 0, "sp": 0}

    def step():
        state["steps"] += 1
        if state["steps"] > B:
            raise Budget()

    def inrange(p, n):
        return any(l and b <= p and p + n <= b + sz for (b, sz, l, pin) in alloctab)

    def exec_fn(fn, env):
        regs = parse_regs(fn["regs"]) if fn["regs"] else {}
        widths = dict(regs)
        if fn["kind"] == "lproc":
            for (n, t, _) in parse_params(fn["plists"][0]) + parse_params(fn["plists"][1]):
                widths[n] = int(re.match(r"reg\[(\d+)\]", t).group(1))
        else:
            for (n, t, _) in parse_params(fn["plists"][0]):
                widths[n] = int(re.match(r"wire\[(\d+)\]", t).group(1))
        blocks = {b["name"]: b for b in fn["blocks"]}
        cur = fn["blocks"][0]["name"]
        pc = 0
        while True:
            ln = blocks[cur]["instrs"][pc]
            lhs, op, ops = parse_instr(ln)
            step()

            def rd(n):
                return env[n]

            def wr(n, v):
                env[n] = v & ((1 << widths[n]) - 1)
            if op.startswith("lift.const"):
                wr(lhs, int(ops[0]))
            elif op in ("lift.add", "lift.sub", "lift.mov"):
                a = rd(ops[0]); b = rd(ops[1]) if op != "lift.mov" else 0
                wr(lhs, a + b if op == "lift.add" else a - b if op == "lift.sub" else a)
            elif op.startswith("lift.icmp."):
                pred = op.split(".")[-1]; a, b = rd(ops[0]), rd(ops[1])
                wr(lhs, {"eq": a == b, "ne": a != b, "ult": a < b, "ule": a <= b}[pred])
            elif op.startswith("lift.zext."):
                wr(lhs, rd(ops[0]))
            elif op == "lift.addr":
                wr(lhs, addr_of[ops[0][1:]])
            elif op == "lift.boundscheck":
                if not inrange(rd(ops[0]), int(ops[1])):
                    raise Fault(FAULT["MEMFAULT"])
            elif op.startswith("lift.load."):
                n = int(op.split(".i")[1]) // 8; a = rd(ops[0])
                if not inrange(a, n):
                    raise Fault(FAULT["MEMFAULT"])
                wr(lhs, sum(mem.get(a + i, 0) << (8 * i) for i in range(n)))
            elif op == "lift.call":
                callee = fns[ops[0][1:]]
                args = [rd(x) for x in ops[1].strip("()").split(", ") if x]
                # §3.7 flag: depth or stack exhaustion; the stack is monotonic
                if state["depth"] + 1 > depth_limit or state["sp"] + frame_cells(callee) > stack_limit:
                    raise Fault(FAULT["DEPTH"])
                state["depth"] += 1
                state["sp"] += frame_cells(callee)
                cenv = {}
                for (pn, _, _), v in zip(parse_params(callee["plists"][0]), args):
                    cenv[pn] = v
                r = exec_fn(callee, cenv)
                wr(lhs, r)
            elif op == "lift.ret":
                if state["depth"] == 0:
                    raise Fault(FAULT["TRAP"])
                state["depth"] -= 1
                return rd(ops[0])
            elif op == "lift.retval":
                state["result"] ^= rd(ops[0])
                return None
            elif op == "qbranch":
                cur = ops[1][1:] if rd(ops[0]) else ops[2][1:]; pc = 0; continue
            elif op == "qjump":
                cur = ops[0][1:]; pc = 0; continue
            else:
                raise AssertionError(f"interpreter: unsupported row {op}")
            pc += 1

    env = {n: v for (n, _, _), v in zip(parse_params(oracle["plists"][0]), ins)}
    try:
        exec_fn(oracle, env)
        return (state["result"], 0, state["steps"])
    except Budget:
        return (0, FAULT["STEPS"], state["steps"])
    except Fault as f:
        return (0, f.code, state["steps"])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------- checks

def envelopes_of(hdr, sections):
    """name -> envelope bytes for every function/data symbol (single-member SCCs)."""
    out = {}
    symbols = {v["name"]: v for v in sections["symbols"].values()}
    fns = {f["name"]: f for f in parse_functions(sections.get("functions", []))}
    hashes, _ = compute_hashes(hdr, sections)
    data_lines = dict(l.split(" ") for l in sections.get("data", []))
    for v, sym in symbols.items():
        if v in fns:
            fn = fns[v]
            refs = []
            def repl(m):
                w = m.group(1)
                if w == v:
                    return "@$0"
                if w in symbols:
                    if hashes[w] not in refs:
                        refs.append(hashes[w])
                    return "@" + hashes[w]
                return m.group(0)
            body = [fn["lines"][0]] + [re.sub(r"@([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*)", repl, l) for l in fn["lines"][1:]]
            data, leaves = closure_set(sym, fn, sections)
            out[v] = envelope(hdr["isa"], hdr["ptr_width"], sym["signature"], body, data, leaves, refs)
        else:
            out[v] = envelope(hdr["isa"], hdr["ptr_width"], sym["signature"], [f"{v} {data_lines[v]}"], {}, {}, [])
    return out


def repatch(text):
    """Rewrite every printed hash (symbols lines, table, prose) to the computed one."""
    mapping = {}
    for obj in extract_examples(text):
        hdr, sections = parse_object(obj)
        hashes, symbols = compute_hashes(hdr, sections)
        for n, h in hashes.items():
            old = symbols[n]["interface_hash"]
            if old != h:
                mapping[old] = h
    for old, new in mapping.items():
        text = text.replace(old, new)
    return text, mapping


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == "--repatch":
        text, mapping = repatch(SPEC.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        SPEC.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        for old, new in mapping.items():
            print(f"repatched {old[:12]} -> {new[:12]}")
        print("re-run without --repatch to verify")
        return
    if len(sys.argv) > 2 and sys.argv[1] == "--print-envelope":
        text = SPEC.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for obj in extract_examples(text):
            hdr, sections = parse_object(obj)
            envs = envelopes_of(hdr, sections)
            if sys.argv[2] in envs:
                sys.stdout.write(envs[sys.argv[2]].decode())
                return
        sys.exit(f"no symbol {sys.argv[2]}")
    text = SPEC.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    examples = extract_examples(text)
    assert len(examples) >= 2, "expected at least two example objects"
    failures = []
    printed = dict(re.findall(r"^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*) = ([0-9a-f]{64})$", text, re.M))
    all_hashes = {}
    for obj in examples:
        hdr, sections = parse_object(obj)
        hashes, symbols = compute_hashes(hdr, sections)
        all_hashes.update(hashes)
        for n, h in hashes.items():
            ih = symbols[n]["interface_hash"]
            if ih != h:
                failures.append(f"{n}: symbols interface_hash {ih[:12]} != computed {h[:12]}")
            if printed.get(n) != h:
                failures.append(f"{n}: printed table hash {str(printed.get(n))[:12]} != computed {h[:12]}")
        names = set(symbols)
        if "inc8" in names:
            for x in range(256):
                r, c, st = run_oracle(hdr, sections, "inc8", [x], {}, 3)
                if (r, c) != ((x + 1) & 255, 0):
                    failures.append(f"inc8({x}) B=3 -> {(r, c)}")
                r, c, st = run_oracle(hdr, sections, "inc8", [x], {}, 2)
                if (r, c) != (0, FAULT["STEPS"]):
                    failures.append(f"inc8({x}) B=2 -> {(r, c)} expected STEPS")
        if "sum_db" in names:
            import random
            rnd = random.Random(7)
            db = [rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(16)]
            for n in range(0, 24):
                r, c, st = run_oracle(hdr, sections, "sum_db", [n], {"db": db}, 10 ** 6)
                exp = (sum(db[:n]) & 255, 0) if n <= 16 else (0, FAULT["MEMFAULT"])
                if (r, c) != exp:
                    failures.append(f"sum_db({n}) -> {(r, c)} expected {exp}")
            # stack capacity (§3.7, §16.3): R_sum = 16 cells; n needs 16(n+1) cells
            fns = {f["name"]: f for f in parse_functions(sections["functions"])}
            if frame_cells(fns["sum"]) != 16:
                failures.append(f"R_sum = {frame_cells(fns['sum'])}, text says 16")
            for n in (0, 5, 15, 16):
                need = 16 * (n + 1)
                r, c, _ = run_oracle(hdr, sections, "sum_db", [n], {"db": db}, 10 ** 6, stack_limit=need)
                if c != 0:
                    failures.append(f"sum_db({n}) stack_limit={need} -> code {c}, expected success")
                r, c, _ = run_oracle(hdr, sections, "sum_db", [n], {"db": db}, 10 ** 6, stack_limit=need - 1)
                if c != FAULT["DEPTH"]:
                    failures.append(f"sum_db({n}) stack_limit={need - 1} -> code {c}, expected DEPTH")
            if 2 ** sections["layout"]["S_cells"] < 16 * 17:
                failures.append("S_cells too small for the stated n <= 16 success domain")
            for n in (1, 3, 7):
                r, c, _ = run_oracle(hdr, sections, "sum_db", [n], {"db": db}, 10 ** 6, depth_limit=n)
                if c != FAULT["DEPTH"]:
                    failures.append(f"sum_db({n}) depth_limit={n} -> code {c}, expected DEPTH")
                r, c, _ = run_oracle(hdr, sections, "sum_db", [n], {"db": db}, 10 ** 6, depth_limit=n + 1)
                if c != 0:
                    failures.append(f"sum_db({n}) depth_limit={n + 1} -> code {c}, expected success")
            _, _, st = run_oracle(hdr, sections, "sum_db", [0], {"db": db}, 10 ** 6)
            r, c, _ = run_oracle(hdr, sections, "sum_db", [0], {"db": db}, st - 1)
            if c != FAULT["STEPS"]:
                failures.append(f"sum_db(0) with B=steps-1 -> code {c}, expected STEPS")
        # layout disjointness
        lay = sections.get("layout")
        if lay:
            rngs = [(0, lay["null_size"], "null")]
            rngs += [(g["base"], g["base"] + g["size"], n) for n, g in lay.get("globals", {}).items()]
            rngs += [(lay["heap_base"], lay["heap_base"] + lay["heap_limit_max"], "heap")]
            for o, rs in lay.get("interface_regions", {}).items():
                fn = next(f for f in parse_functions(sections["functions"]) if f["name"] == o)
                for (rn, rt, _) in parse_params(fn["plists"][3]):
                    A = int(re.match(r"region\[(\d+),", rt).group(1))
                    rngs.append((rs[rn]["base"], rs[rn]["base"] + 2 ** A, rn))
            rngs.sort()
            for (a0, a1, an), (b0, b1, bn) in zip(rngs, rngs[1:]):
                if a1 > b0:
                    failures.append(f"layout ranges overlap: {an} [{a0},{a1}) and {bn} [{b0},{b1})")
            if rngs[-1][1] > 2 ** lay["H"]:
                failures.append(f"layout exceeds 2^H: {rngs[-1]}")
    # every printed envelope block must hash to a computed symbol hash
    env_blocks = re.findall(r"```\n(isa=0\.[0-9]+\n.*?)```", text, re.S)
    if not env_blocks:
        failures.append("no printed envelope block found")
    for blk in env_blocks:
        h = sha(blk.encode())
        # a plain symbol hashes its envelope; a one-member SCC with a self-reference
        # hashes "<scc_hash>:0" where scc_hash is the SHA-256 of the envelope (§9.2)
        candidates = {h, sha(f"{h}:0".encode())}
        if not candidates & set(all_hashes.values()):
            failures.append(f"printed envelope starting {blk.splitlines()[3][:40]!r} hashes to {h[:12]}, no symbol has it")
    if failures:
        print("ISA CHECK FAILED:")
        for f in failures:
            print(" -", f)
        sys.exit(1)
    print(f"isa_check ok: {len(examples)} example objects parse, hash per §9.2, {len(env_blocks)} printed envelopes verified, and execute as stated")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
````

````rust
use crate::{
    err,
    object::list,
    quantum::Wire,
    validation::{gate, normalize_call},
    Argument, Error, Function, Instruction, Object, QuantumBindings, QuantumRegion, QuantumState,
    Result, Type,
};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

struct Environment {
    bindings: QuantumBindings,
    predicates: Vec<Wire>,
    borrowed: BTreeMap<String, Vec<usize>>,
    borrow_used: BTreeSet<usize>,
}
impl Environment {
    fn bundle(&self, n: &str) -> Result<Vec<Wire>> {
        if let Some((base, index)) = n.split_once('[') {
            let index = index
                .strip_suffix(']')
                .and_then(|s| s.parse::<usize>().ok())
                .ok_or_else(|| Error("§3.3: invalid wire index".into()))?;
            let ws = self
                .bindings
                .bundles
                .get(base)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§3.3: unknown live bundle {base}")))?;
            return ws
                .get(index)
                .map(|w| vec![*w])
                .ok_or_else(|| Error("§3.3: wire index out of range".into()));
        }
        self.bindings
            .bundles
            .get(n)
            .cloned()
            .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§3.3: unknown live bundle {n}")))
    }
    fn scalar(&self, n: &str) -> Result<Wire> {
        let w = self.bundle(n)?;
        if w.len() != 1 {
            return err("§3.3", "scalar wire required");
        }
        Ok(w[0])
    }
    fn controls(&self, inherited: &[(Wire, bool)]) -> Vec<(Wire, bool)> {
        let mut c = inherited.to_vec();
        for w in &self.predicates {
            if !c.contains(&(*w, true)) {
                c.push((*w, true));
            }
        }
        c
    }
    fn produce(&mut self, n: &str, wires: Vec<Wire>) -> Result<()> {
        if self.bindings.bundles.contains_key(n) {
            return err("§3.3", "live bundle produced twice");
        }
        self.bindings.bundles.insert(n.into(), wires);
        Ok(())
    }
}
impl Object {
    pub(crate) fn permutation_action_vectors(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        mutables: &[crate::BitVector],
        inputs: &[crate::BitVector],
        regions: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>,
        args: &[Argument],
        adjoint: bool,
    ) -> Result<Vec<crate::BitVector>> {
        let f = &self.functions[name];
        if f.kind != "perm_action"
            || mutables.len() != f.params[0].len()
            || inputs.len() != f.params[1].len()
            || args.len() != f.params[3].len()
        {
            return err("§4.2", "lift.perm_call interface mismatch");
        }
        let mut q = QuantumState::new();
        let mut b = QuantumBindings::default();
        for (values, ps) in [(mutables, &f.params[0]), (inputs, &f.params[1])] {
            for (v, p) in values.iter().zip(ps) {
                let wires = q.allocate(p.ty.width(self.ptr_width)? as usize)?;
                for (i, w) in wires.iter().enumerate() {
                    if v.bit(i)? {
                        q.gate("x", &[*w], None, &[])?;
                    }
                }
                b.bundles.insert(p.name.clone(), wires);
            }
        }
        for p in &f.params[2] {
            let Type::Region(a, w) = p.ty else {
                return err("§5.1", "mem slot requires region type");
            };
            let bytes = regions
                .get(&p.name)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error("§4.2: missing lifted action region".into()))?;
            let mut cells = Vec::new();
            for byte in bytes {
                let cell = q.allocate(w as usize)?;
                for (i, wire) in cell.iter().enumerate() {
                    if i < 8 && byte & (1u8 << i) != 0 {
                        q.gate("x", &[*wire], None, &[])?;
                    }
                }
                cells.push(cell);
            }
            b.regions.insert(
                p.name.clone(),
                QuantumRegion {
                    address_width: a,
                    cell_width: w,
                    cells,
                },
            );
        }
        for (p, v) in f.params[3].iter().zip(args) {
            b.args.insert(p.name.clone(), v.clone());
        }
        let capacity = self.borrow_capacity(name)?;
        let idle = q.allocate(capacity)?;
        if !idle.is_empty() {
            b.borrowed.push(idle.clone());
        }
        self.execute_action(name, &mut q, &b, adjoint, &[])?;
        q.release(&idle)?;
        f.params[0]
            .iter()
            .map(|p| {
                let wires = &b.bundles[&p.name];
                let mut value = crate::BitVector::zero(wires.len())?;
                for (i, wire) in wires.iter().enumerate() {
                    value.set(i, q.read_basis(&[*wire])? != 0)?;
                }
                Ok(value)
            })
            .collect()
    }
    /// The number of borrowed wires an action body's `qborrow` rows can
    /// draw from its caller's idle pool (§5.6), summed over the call closure.
    pub fn borrow_capacity(&self, root: &str) -> Result<usize> {
        fn scan(seq: &[Instruction], count: &mut usize, children: &mut Vec<String>) -> Result<()> {
            for i in seq {
                if i.op == "qborrow" {
                    *count =
                        count
                            .checked_add(i.operands[1].parse::<usize>().map_err(|_| {
                                Error("§5.6: borrow count exceeds host storage".into())
                            })?)
                            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§5.6: borrow capacity overflow".into()))?;
                }
                if let Ok(call) = normalize_call(i) {
                    if call.instruction.op == "action_call" {
                        children.push(call.instruction.operands[0].trim_start_matches('@').into());
                    }
                }
                for body in &i.bodies {
                    scan(body, count, children)?;
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        let mut count = 0;
        let mut pending = vec![root.to_string()];
        let mut visited = BTreeSet::new();
        while let Some(name) = pending.pop() {
            if !visited.insert(name.clone()) {
                continue;
            }
            let function = self
                .functions
                .get(&name)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§9.3: unresolved action @{name}")))?;
            for block in &function.blocks {
                scan(&block.instructions, &mut count, &mut pending)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(count)
    }
    pub fn execute_action(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        q: &mut QuantumState,
        bindings: &QuantumBindings,
        adjoint: bool,
        controls: &[Wire],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        self.ensure_linked()?;
        self.action_internal(
            name,
            q,
            bindings,
            adjoint,
            &controls.iter().map(|w| (*w, true)).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        )
    }
    fn action_internal(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        q: &mut QuantumState,
        bindings: &QuantumBindings,
        adjoint: bool,
        controls: &[(Wire, bool)],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let entry_next_wire = q.next_wire_id();
        let f = self
            .functions
            .get(name)
            .filter(|f| matches!(f.kind.as_str(), "action" | "perm_action"))
            .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§5.3: unknown action @{name}")))?;
        let mut used = BTreeSet::new();
        for p in f.params[0].iter().chain(&f.params[1]) {
            let w = bindings
                .bundles
                .get(&p.name)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§5.1: missing bundle {}", p.name)))?;
            if w.len() != p.ty.width(self.ptr_width)? as usize {
                return err("§3.3", "action bundle width mismatch");
            }
            for wire in w {
                q.position(*wire)?;
                if !used.insert(wire) {
                    return err("§3.3", "action interface bundles overlap");
                }
            }
        }
        for p in &f.params[2] {
            let Type::Region(a, w) = p.ty else {
                return err("§5.1", "mem slot requires region type");
            };
            let r = bindings
                .regions
                .get(&p.name)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error("§5.1: missing interface region".into()))?;
            if r.address_width != a
                || r.cell_width != w
                || crate::oracle::power_of_two(a as u128) != Some(r.cells.len() as u128)
                || r.cells.iter().any(|c| c.len() != w as usize)
            {
                return err("§3.3", "action interface region dimensions mismatch");
            }
            for wire in r.cells.iter().flatten() {
                q.position(*wire)?;
                if !used.insert(wire) {
                    return err("§3.3", "action regions overlap interface");
                }
            }
        }
        for p in &f.params[3] {
            let arg = bindings
                .args
                .get(&p.name)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error("§5.1: missing action classical argument".into()))?;
            // §3.3 classical types, ptr included (ptr_width bits).
            crate::oracle::check_argument(self, &p.ty, arg)?;
        }
        let mut env = Environment {
            bindings: bindings.clone(),
            predicates: Vec::new(),
            borrowed: BTreeMap::new(),
            borrow_used: BTreeSet::new(),
        };
        let mut regions = Vec::new();
        for b in &f.blocks {
            gather_regions(&b.instructions, &mut regions);
        }
        let mut local = Vec::new();
        for i in regions {
            let a = crate::object::host_count(&i.operands[1], "qregion address width")?;
            let w = crate::object::host_count(&i.operands[2], "qregion cell width")?;
            let count = crate::oracle::power_of_two(a as u128)
                .and_then(|n| usize::try_from(n).ok())
                .ok_or_else(|| {
                    Error("host limit: local region exceeds host address space".into())
                })?;
            let n = count
                .checked_mul(w as usize)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error("§4.6: region bit size overflow".into()))?;
            let wires = q.allocate(n)?;
            let image = if i.operands.len() == 4 {
                self.data[i.operands[3].trim_start_matches('@')].clone()
            } else {
                vec![0; n.div_ceil(8)]
            };
            for (bit, wire) in wires.iter().enumerate() {
                if image[bit / 8] & (1 << (bit % 8)) != 0 {
                    q.gate("x", &[*wire], None, &[])?;
                }
            }
            let cells = wires.chunks_exact(w as usize).map(|c| c.to_vec()).collect();
            env.bindings.regions.insert(
                i.operands[0].clone(),
                QuantumRegion {
                    address_width: a,
                    cell_width: w,
                    cells,
                },
            );
            local.push((wires, image));
        }
        let mut live_widths = bindings
            .bundles
            .iter()
            .map(|(n, w)| (n.clone(), w.len()))
            .collect();
        let instructions: Vec<_> = f
            .blocks
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|b| b.instructions.iter().cloned())
            .collect();
        let widths = infer_widths(&instructions, &env, &mut live_widths)?;
        self.action_sequence(&instructions, &widths, q, &mut env, adjoint, controls)?;
        if !env.predicates.is_empty() || !env.borrowed.is_empty() {
            return err("§5.1", "action exited with unclosed predicate/borrow frame");
        }
        let interface: BTreeSet<_> = bindings.bundles.keys().collect();
        if env.bindings.bundles.keys().any(|n| !interface.contains(n)) {
            return err("§5.1", "action exited with live workspace");
        }
        for (wires, image) in local.into_iter().rev() {
            for (bit, wire) in wires.iter().enumerate() {
                if image[bit / 8] & (1 << (bit % 8)) != 0 {
                    q.gate("x", &[*wire], None, &[])?;
                }
            }
            q.release(&wires)?;
        }
        // Region-local identities cannot escape through caller-owned interfaces.
        // Reclaim them once all local factors have been explicitly cleaned.
        q.restore_next_wire_id(entry_next_wire)?;
        Ok(())
    }
    fn action_sequence(
        &self,
        sequence: &[Instruction],
        widths: &[LifetimeWidths],
        q: &mut QuantumState,
        e: &mut Environment,
        adjoint: bool,
        inherited: &[(Wire, bool)],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let indices: Vec<_> = if adjoint {
            (0..sequence.len()).rev().collect()
        } else {
            (0..sequence.len()).collect()
        };
        for index in indices {
            let i = &sequence[index];
            let width = &widths[index];
            let a = &i.operands;
            let context = e.controls(inherited);
            let op = i.op.as_str();
            if gate(op) {
                if !matches!(op, "x" | "cx" | "ccx" | "mcx" | "swap") {
                    q.audit_frame()?;
                }
                let mut wires = Vec::new();
                let mut angle = None;
                if op == "mcx" {
                    for n in list(&a[0])? {
                        wires.push(e.scalar(&n)?);
                    }
                    wires.push(e.scalar(&a[1])?);
                } else if matches!(op, "rx" | "ry" | "rz") {
                    let theta = match a[0].parse::<f64>() {
                        Ok(n) => n,
                        Err(_) => match e.bindings.args.get(&a[0]) {
                            Some(Argument::Float(n)) => *n,
                            _ => return err("§4.4", "angle is not a finite classical f64"),
                        },
                    };
                    angle = Some(if adjoint { -theta } else { theta });
                    wires.push(e.scalar(&a[1])?);
                } else {
                    for n in a {
                        wires.push(e.scalar(n)?);
                    }
                }
                let inverse = if adjoint {
                    match op {
                        "s" => "sdg",
                        "sdg" => "s",
                        "t" => "tdg",
                        "tdg" => "t",
                        _ => op,
                    }
                } else {
                    op
                };
                q.controlled_gate(inverse, &wires, angle, &context)?;
                continue;
            }
            match op {
                "qregion" => {}
                "qpred" | "qunpred" => {
                    let push = (op == "qpred") ^ adjoint;
                    let wire = e.scalar(&a[0])?;
                    if push {
                        e.predicates.push(wire);
                    } else if e.predicates.pop() != Some(wire) {
                        return err("§3.5", "action predicate pop mismatch");
                    }
                }
                "qif" => {
                    let w = e.scalar(&a[0])?;
                    let mut yes = context.clone();
                    yes.push((w, true));
                    let mut no = context.clone();
                    no.push((w, false));
                    // Reverse the complete §4.6 expansion, including its
                    // unconditional lifetime operations (SPEC-QUESTIONS 28).
                    if adjoint {
                        self.action_sequence(&i.bodies[1], &width.bodies[1], q, e, true, &no)?;
                        self.action_sequence(&i.bodies[0], &width.bodies[0], q, e, true, &yes)?;
                    } else {
                        self.action_sequence(&i.bodies[0], &width.bodies[0], q, e, false, &yes)?;
                        self.action_sequence(&i.bodies[1], &width.bodies[1], q, e, false, &no)?;
                    }
                }
                "qloop" => {
                    let n = a[0]
                        .parse::<usize>()
                        .map_err(|_| Error("§4.6: loop bound exceeds host index space".into()))?;
                    if a.len() == 1 {
                        // body n times (§4.6). The iterated state is exact, so once
                        // it returns to its loop-entry value the remaining iterations
                        // are whole periods and are skipped (X^(2^40) needs 2).
                        let entry = (q.content(), e.bindings.bundles.clone());
                        let mut done = 0usize;
                        while done < n {
                            let iteration = if adjoint { n - 1 - done } else { done };
                            self.action_sequence(
                                &i.bodies[0],
                                width.iteration(iteration),
                                q,
                                e,
                                adjoint,
                                &context,
                            )?;
                            done += 1;
                            // Reverse traversal must execute the transient prefix
                            // separately, even if a steady iteration is identity.
                            let periodic_end = if adjoint { n - width.cycle_start } else { n };
                            if done < periodic_end
                                && !q.auditing_borrows()
                                && (q.content(), e.bindings.bundles.clone()) == entry
                            {
                                done += (periodic_end - done) / done * done;
                            }
                        }
                    } else {
                        let condition = e.bundle(&a[2])?;
                        let flags = q.allocate(n)?;
                        if adjoint {
                            for j in 0..n {
                                let controls = if j == 0 {
                                    vec![condition[j], flags[j]]
                                } else {
                                    vec![flags[j - 1], condition[j], flags[j]]
                                };
                                q.controlled_gate(
                                    if j == 0 { "cx" } else { "ccx" },
                                    &controls,
                                    None,
                                    &context,
                                )?;
                            }
                            for j in (0..n).rev() {
                                let mut c = context.clone();
                                c.push((flags[j], true));
                                self.action_sequence(
                                    &i.bodies[0],
                                    width.iteration(j),
                                    q,
                                    e,
                                    true,
                                    &c,
                                )?;
                            }
                        } else {
                            for j in 0..n {
                                let controls = if j == 0 {
                                    vec![condition[j], flags[j]]
                                } else {
                                    vec![flags[j - 1], condition[j], flags[j]]
                                };
                                q.controlled_gate(
                                    if j == 0 { "cx" } else { "ccx" },
                                    &controls,
                                    None,
                                    &context,
                                )?;
                                let mut c = context.clone();
                                c.push((flags[j], true));
                                self.action_sequence(
                                    &i.bodies[0],
                                    width.iteration(j),
                                    q,
                                    e,
                                    false,
                                    &c,
                                )?;
                            }
                        }
                        for j in (0..n).rev() {
                            let controls = if j == 0 {
                                vec![condition[j], flags[j]]
                            } else {
                                vec![flags[j - 1], condition[j], flags[j]]
                            };
                            q.controlled_gate(
                                if j == 0 { "cx" } else { "ccx" },
                                &controls,
                                None,
                                &context,
                            )?;
                        }
                        q.release(&flags)?;
                    }
                }
                "qalloc" | "qfree" => {
                    let allocate = (op == "qalloc") ^ adjoint;
                    let name = if op == "qalloc" { &i.lhs[0] } else { &a[0] };
                    if allocate {
                        let n = width
                            .produced
                            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§4.3: missing matched lifetime width".into()))?;
                        let w = q.allocate(n)?;
                        e.produce(name, w)?;
                    } else {
                        let w = e.bundle(name)?;
                        q.release(&w)?;
                        e.bindings.bundles.remove(name);
                    }
                }
                "qborrow" | "qreturn" => {
                    let borrow = (op == "qborrow") ^ adjoint;
                    let name = if op == "qborrow" { &i.lhs[0] } else { &a[0] };
                    if borrow {
                        let n = width
                            .produced
                            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§4.3: missing matched lifetime width".into()))?;
                        let pool = e
                            .bindings
                            .borrowed
                            .iter()
                            .flatten()
                            .copied()
                            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
                        let indices = (0..pool.len())
                            .filter(|i| !e.borrow_used.contains(i))
                            .take(n)
                            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
                        if indices.len() != n {
                            return err(
                                "§5.6",
                                "designated idle set lacks requested borrowed wires",
                            );
                        }
                        let wires: Vec<_> = indices.iter().map(|i| pool[*i]).collect();
                        e.borrow_used.extend(&indices);
                        e.borrowed.insert(name.into(), indices);
                        q.audit_borrow(&wires);
                        e.produce(name, wires)?;
                    } else {
                        q.audit_return(&e.bundle(name)?)?;
                        let indices = e
                            .borrowed
                            .remove(name)
                            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§5.6: unmatched return".into()))?;
                        for index in indices {
                            e.borrow_used.remove(&index);
                        }
                        e.bindings.bundles.remove(name);
                    }
                }
                "qcopy" | "quncopy" => {
                    let copy = (op == "qcopy") ^ adjoint;
                    let source = e.bundle(&a[0])?;
                    let name = if op == "qcopy" { &i.lhs[0] } else { &a[1] };
                    let destination = if copy {
                        let w = q.allocate(source.len())?;
                        e.produce(name, w.clone())?;
                        w
                    } else {
                        e.bundle(name)?
                    };
                    bundle_xor(q, &source, &destination, &context)?;
                    if !copy {
                        q.release(&destination)?;
                        e.bindings.bundles.remove(name);
                    }
                }
                "qxor" => bundle_xor(q, &e.bundle(&a[0])?, &e.bundle(&a[1])?, &context)?,
                "qexch" => bundle_exchange(q, &e.bundle(&a[0])?, &e.bundle(&a[1])?, &context)?,
                "qload" | "qunload" | "qstore" | "qexchm" => {
                    let region = e
                        .bindings
                        .regions
                        .get(&a[0])
                        .cloned()
                        .ok_or_else(|| Error("§4.6: quantum region not found".into()))?;
                    let address = e.bundle(&a[1])?;
                    let load = matches!(op, "qload" | "qunload");
                    let compute = (op == "qload") ^ adjoint;
                    let name = if op == "qload" { &i.lhs[0] } else { &a[2] };
                    let value = if load && compute {
                        let w = q.allocate(region.cell_width as usize)?;
                        e.produce(name, w.clone())?;
                        w
                    } else {
                        e.bundle(name)?
                    };
                    for (index, cell) in region.cells.iter().enumerate() {
                        let mut c = context.clone();
                        for (bit, w) in address.iter().enumerate() {
                            c.push((*w, index & (1usize << bit) != 0));
                        }
                        if op == "qexchm" {
                            bundle_exchange(q, cell, &value, &c)?;
                        } else if load {
                            bundle_xor(q, cell, &value, &c)?;
                        } else {
                            bundle_xor(q, &value, cell, &c)?;
                        }
                    }
                    if load && !compute {
                        q.release(&value)?;
                        e.bindings.bundles.remove(name);
                    }
                }
                "oracle_call" | "action_call" | "adj" | "ctl" => {
                    let call = normalize_call(i)?;
                    let mut c = context.clone();
                    if let Some(w) = call.control {
                        c.push((e.scalar(&w)?, true));
                    }
                    let ca = &call.instruction.operands;
                    let callee = &self.functions[ca[0].trim_start_matches('@')];
                    if call.instruction.op == "oracle_call" {
                        let token = e
                            .bindings
                            .args
                            .get(&ca[1])
                            .and_then(|v| {
                                if let Argument::Token(b) = v {
                                    Some(*b)
                                } else {
                                    None
                                }
                            })
                            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§4.7: missing oracle token".into()))?;
                        let ins = list(&ca[2])?
                            .iter()
                            .map(|n| e.bundle(n))
                            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
                        let target = e.bundle(&ca[3])?;
                        let fault = e.bundle(&ca[4])?;
                        let mut regions = BTreeMap::new();
                        for (p, n) in callee.params[3].iter().zip(list(&ca[5])?) {
                            regions.insert(
                                p.name.clone(),
                                e.bindings
                                    .regions
                                    .get(&n)
                                    .ok_or_else(|| Error("§4.7: missing memory region".into()))?
                                    .clone(),
                            );
                        }
                        let args =
                            list(&ca[6])?
                                .iter()
                                .map(|n| {
                                    e.bindings.args.get(n).cloned().ok_or_else(|| {
                                        Error("§4.7: missing classical argument".into())
                                    })
                                })
                                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
                        self.oracle_quantum(
                            callee, q, &ins, &target, &fault, &regions, &args, token, &c,
                        )?;
                    } else {
                        let mut binding = QuantumBindings {
                            borrowed: vec![e
                                .bindings
                                .borrowed
                                .iter()
                                .flatten()
                                .enumerate()
                                .filter_map(|(i, w)| (!e.borrow_used.contains(&i)).then_some(*w))
                                .collect()],
                            ..QuantumBindings::default()
                        };
                        for group in 0..2 {
                            for (p, n) in callee.params[group].iter().zip(list(&ca[group + 1])?) {
                                binding.bundles.insert(p.name.clone(), e.bundle(&n)?);
                            }
                        }
                        for (p, n) in callee.params[2].iter().zip(list(&ca[3])?) {
                            binding
                                .regions
                                .insert(p.name.clone(), e.bindings.regions[&n].clone());
                        }
                        for (p, n) in callee.params[3].iter().zip(list(&ca[4])?) {
                            binding
                                .args
                                .insert(p.name.clone(), e.bindings.args[&n].clone());
                        }
                        self.action_internal(
                            &callee.name,
                            q,
                            &binding,
                            adjoint ^ call.adjoint,
                            &c,
                        )?;
                    }
                }
                "qinplace" => {
                    let g = &a[if adjoint { 1 } else { 0 }];
                    let gi = &a[if adjoint { 0 } else { 1 }];
                    let x = e.bundle(&a[3])?;
                    let token = e
                        .bindings
                        .args
                        .get(&a[2])
                        .and_then(|v| {
                            if let Argument::Token(b) = v {
                                Some(*b)
                            } else {
                                None
                            }
                        })
                        .ok_or_else(|| Error("§4.5: qinplace token".into()))?;
                    let gf = &self.functions[g.trim_start_matches('@')];
                    let gif = &self.functions[gi.trim_start_matches('@')];
                    // §4.5 requires, under tk, FAULT_NONE on every input and
                    // g∘ginv = ginv∘g = id. Decided here exactly, on the full
                    // n-bit domain at this token's budget, before any state change.
                    self.verify_inverse_pair(gf, gif, token)?;
                    let fw = gf.params[2][0].ty.width(self.ptr_width)? as usize;
                    let t = q.allocate(x.len())?;
                    let fault = q.allocate(fw)?;
                    self.oracle_quantum(
                        gf,
                        q,
                        std::slice::from_ref(&x),
````
