                        token,
                        &context,
                    )?;
                    bundle_exchange(q, &x, &t, &context)?;
                    self.oracle_quantum(
                        gif,
                        q,
                        &[x],
                        &t,
                        &fault,
                        &BTreeMap::new(),
                        &[],
                        token,
                        &context,
                    )?;
                    q.release(&t)?;
                    q.release(&fault)?;
                }
                _ => return err("§4.8", format!("unimplemented Q instruction {op}")),
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    /// §4.5: both oracles are fault-free on every n-bit input under `budget`
    /// and inverse to each other; otherwise the qinplace is not executed.
    pub(crate) fn verify_inverse_pair(
        &self,
        g: &Function,
        ginv: &Function,
        budget: crate::Budget,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let n = g.params[0][0].ty.bits(self.ptr_width)?;
        let run = |f: &Function, x: &crate::BitVector| -> Result<crate::BitVector> {
            let input = crate::OracleVectorInput {
                ins: vec![x.clone()],
                ..Default::default()
            };
            let r = self.run_oracle_vectors(&f.name, &input, budget)?;
            if !r.code.is_zero() {
                return err(
                    "§4.5",
                    format!(
                        "qinplace oracle @{} faults with code {} on input {} under this token",
                        f.name,
                        r.code.to_decimal(),
                        x.to_decimal()
                    ),
                );
            }
            Ok(r.payload)
        };
        let mut x = crate::BitVector::zero(n)?;
        let one = crate::BitVector::from_u128(n, 1)?;
        loop {
            for (first, second) in [(g, ginv), (ginv, g)] {
                if run(second, &run(first, &x)?)? != x {
                    return err(
                        "§4.5",
                        format!(
                            "@{} is not the inverse of @{} at input {}",
                            second.name,
                            first.name,
                            x.to_decimal()
                        ),
                    );
                }
            }
            x = x.binary("add", &one)?;
            if x.is_zero() {
                return Ok(());
            }
        }
    }
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub(crate) fn oracle_quantum(
        &self,
        callee: &Function,
        q: &mut QuantumState,
        ins: &[Vec<Wire>],
        target: &[Wire],
        fault: &[Wire],
        regions: &BTreeMap<String, QuantumRegion>,
        args: &[Argument],
        budget: crate::Budget,
        controls: &[(Wire, bool)],
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let input_positions = ins
            .iter()
            .map(|w| w.iter().map(|w| q.position(*w)).collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>())
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
        let target = target
            .iter()
            .map(|w| q.position(*w))
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
        let fault = fault
            .iter()
            .map(|w| q.position(*w))
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
        let controls = controls
            .iter()
            .map(|(w, v)| Ok((q.position(*w)?, *v)))
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
        let regions: BTreeMap<_, _> = regions
            .iter()
            .map(|(n, r)| {
                Ok((
                    n.clone(),
                    r.cells
                        .iter()
                        .map(|c| c.iter().map(|w| q.position(*w)).collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>())
                        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?,
                ))
            })
            .collect::<Result<_>>()?;
        q.permute(|bits| {
            let mut result = bits.to_vec();
            if controls.iter().any(|(p, v)| bits[*p] != *v) {
                return Ok(result);
            }
            let vectors = input_positions
                .iter()
                .map(|positions| {
                    let mut value = crate::BitVector::zero(positions.len())?;
                    for (i, p) in positions.iter().enumerate() {
                        value.set(i, bits[*p])?;
                    }
                    Ok(value)
                })
                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
            let mut input = crate::OracleVectorInput {
                ins: vectors,
                args: args.to_vec(),
                ..Default::default()
            };
            for (n, cells) in &regions {
                // Oracle interface regions have W = 8 (§7.2): one byte per cell.
                let bytes = cells
                    .iter()
                    .map(|cell| {
                        if cell.len() != 8 {
                            return err("§7.2", "oracle interface region cells must be wire[8]");
                        }
                        Ok(cell
                            .iter()
                            .enumerate()
                            .fold(0u8, |b, (i, p)| b | (u8::from(bits[*p]) << i)))
                    })
                    .collect::<Result<_>>()?;
                input.regions.insert(n.clone(), bytes);
            }
            let mut machine = crate::OracleVectorMachine::new(self, &callee.name, &input, budget)?;
            let entry = machine.snapshot();
            for _ in 0..budget.steps {
                machine.forward_step()?;
            }
            let outcome = machine.outcome()?;
            for _ in 0..budget.steps {
                machine.inverse_step()?;
            }
            if machine.snapshot() != entry || !machine.frames_clean() {
                return err("§5.2", "oracle workspace failed prefix reversal");
            }
            for (i, p) in target.iter().enumerate() {
                result[*p] ^= outcome.payload.bit(i)?;
            }
            for (i, p) in fault.iter().enumerate() {
                result[*p] ^= outcome.code.bit(i)?;
            }
            Ok(result)
        })
    }
}
fn gather_regions<'a>(seq: &'a [Instruction], out: &mut Vec<&'a Instruction>) {
    for i in seq {
        if i.op == "qregion" {
            out.push(i);
        }
        for b in &i.bodies {
            gather_regions(b, out);
        }
    }
}
/// A structured execution plan, indexed by sequence position and dynamic
/// loop entry, never by static source line. Width environments are finite
/// deterministic maps: repeated entries share a cycle, with no trip-count cap.
#[derive(Default)]
struct LifetimeWidths {
    produced: Option<usize>,
    bodies: Vec<Vec<LifetimeWidths>>,
    cycle_start: usize,
}
impl LifetimeWidths {
    fn iteration(&self, index: usize) -> &[LifetimeWidths] {
        let index = if index < self.bodies.len() {
            index
        } else {
            self.cycle_start + (index - self.cycle_start) % (self.bodies.len() - self.cycle_start)
        };
        &self.bodies[index]
    }
}
fn infer_widths(
    seq: &[Instruction],
    e: &Environment,
    live: &mut BTreeMap<String, usize>,
) -> Result<Vec<LifetimeWidths>> {
    let mut plan = Vec::new();
    for i in seq {
        let mut step = LifetimeWidths::default();
        let width = match i.op.as_str() {
            "qalloc" | "qborrow" => Some(
                i.operands[1]
                    .parse()
                    .map_err(|_| Error("§4.3: allocation width".into()))?,
            ),
            "qcopy" => Some(if i.operands[0].contains('[') {
                1
            } else {
                *live
                    .get(&i.operands[0])
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error("§3.3: copy source width".into()))?
            }),
            "qload" => Some(
                e.bindings
                    .regions
                    .get(&i.operands[0])
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error("§4.6: load region width".into()))?
                    .cell_width as usize,
            ),
            _ => None,
        };
        if let Some(width) = width {
            if live.insert(i.lhs[0].clone(), width).is_some() {
                return err("§3.3", "live bundle produced twice");
            }
            step.produced = Some(width);
        }
        let consumed = match i.op.as_str() {
            "qfree" | "qreturn" => Some(&i.operands[0]),
            "quncopy" => Some(&i.operands[1]),
            "qunload" => Some(&i.operands[2]),
            _ => None,
        };
        if let Some(name) = consumed {
            step.produced = Some(
                live.remove(name)
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error("§3.3: missing consumed lifetime width".into()))?,
            );
        }
        if i.op == "qloop" {
            let n = i.operands[0]
                .parse::<usize>()
                .map_err(|_| Error("§4.6: loop bound exceeds host index space".into()))?;
            let mut seen = BTreeMap::new();
            let mut entries: Vec<BTreeMap<String, usize>> = Vec::new();
            while step.bodies.len() < n {
                if let Some(&start) = seen.get(live) {
                    step.cycle_start = start;
                    let period = step.bodies.len() - start;
                    *live = entries[start + (n - start) % period].clone();
                    break;
                }
                seen.insert(live.clone(), step.bodies.len());
                entries.push(live.clone());
                step.bodies.push(infer_widths(&i.bodies[0], e, live)?);
                step.cycle_start = step.bodies.len();
            }
            // n=0 has no lifetime effects. Lexical qregions were hoisted above.
        } else {
            for body in &i.bodies {
                step.bodies.push(infer_widths(body, e, live)?);
            }
        }
        plan.push(step);
    }
    Ok(plan)
}
fn bundle_xor(
    q: &mut QuantumState,
    source: &[Wire],
    target: &[Wire],
    context: &[(Wire, bool)],
) -> Result<()> {
    if source.len() != target.len() {
        return err("§3.3", "XOR bundle widths differ");
    }
    for (s, t) in source.iter().zip(target) {
        q.controlled_gate("cx", &[*s, *t], None, context)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}
fn bundle_exchange(
    q: &mut QuantumState,
    a: &[Wire],
    b: &[Wire],
    context: &[(Wire, bool)],
) -> Result<()> {
    if a.len() != b.len() {
        return err("§3.3", "exchange bundle widths differ");
    }
    for (s, t) in a.iter().zip(b) {
        q.controlled_gate("swap", &[*s, *t], None, context)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

//! Concrete little-endian bit vectors, with no host integer width restriction.
use crate::{err, Error, Result};
use std::cmp::Ordering;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct BitVector {
    width: usize,
    words: Vec<u64>,
}
impl BitVector {
    pub fn zero(width: usize) -> Result<Self> {
        if width == 0 {
            return err("§3.3", "bit-vector width must be positive");
        }
        let count = width
            .checked_add(63)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§3.3: bit-vector width overflow".into()))?
            / 64;
        let mut words = Vec::new();
        words
            .try_reserve_exact(count)
            .map_err(|e| Error(format!("§3.3: bit-vector storage: {e}")))?;
        words.resize(count, 0);
        Ok(Self { width, words })
    }
    /// `value` as a bit-vector of `width` bits; an unrepresentable value is an
    /// error, never a truncation.
    pub fn from_u128_exact(width: usize, value: u128) -> Result<Self> {
        if width < 128 && value >> width != 0 {
            return err("§3.3", format!("value {value} does not fit {width} bits"));
        }
        Self::from_u128(width, value)
    }
    /// XOR `src` into the low `src.width()` bits of `self`.
    pub fn xor_low(&mut self, src: &Self) -> Result<()> {
        if src.width > self.width {
            return err("§3.6", "XOR source is wider than its destination");
        }
        for (d, s) in self.words.iter_mut().zip(&src.words) {
            *d ^= s;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    /// True iff every bit at index >= n is zero.
    pub fn high_clear(&self, n: usize) -> bool {
        (n..self.width).all(|i| !self.get(i))
    }
    /// Exchange the low `n` bits of two vectors (§3.7: a location of width N
    /// exchanged with a wider cell exchanges the cell's low N bits).
    pub fn swap_low(&mut self, other: &mut Self, n: usize) -> Result<()> {
        if n > self.width || n > other.width {
            return err("§3.6", "exchange wider than an operand");
        }
        for i in 0..n {
            let (a, b) = (self.get(i), other.get(i));
            self.put(i, b);
            other.put(i, a);
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    pub fn width(&self) -> usize {
        self.width
    }
    pub fn is_zero(&self) -> bool {
        self.words.iter().all(|w| *w == 0)
    }
    pub fn from_u128(width: usize, value: u128) -> Result<Self> {
        let mut out = Self::zero(width)?;
        out.words[0] = value as u64;
        if out.words.len() > 1 {
            out.words[1] = (value >> 64) as u64;
        }
        out.trim();
        Ok(out)
    }
    pub fn from_le_bytes(width: usize, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self> {
        let mut out = Self::zero(width)?;
        if bytes.len() != width.div_ceil(8) {
            return err("§3.3", "byte count differs from bit-vector width");
        }
        if !width.is_multiple_of(8) && bytes.last().is_some_and(|b| *b >> (width % 8) != 0) {
            return err("§3.3", "nonzero high padding bits");
        }
        for (i, b) in bytes.iter().enumerate() {
            out.words[i / 8] |= (*b as u64) << ((i % 8) * 8);
        }
        Ok(out)
    }
    pub fn to_le_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        (0..self.width.div_ceil(8))
            .map(|i| (self.words[i / 8] >> ((i % 8) * 8)) as u8)
            .collect()
    }
    pub fn parse_decimal(width: usize, s: &str) -> Result<Self> {
        if !crate::object::integer(s) {
            return err("§16.1", "invalid canonical integer literal");
        }
        let mut out = Self::zero(width)?;
        for digit in s.trim_start_matches('-').bytes() {
            let mut carry = (digit - b'0') as u128;
            for word in &mut out.words {
                let n = (*word as u128) * 10 + carry;
                *word = n as u64;
                carry = n >> 64;

        }

            out = out.negate();
        }
        Ok(out)
    }
    pub fn parse_unsigned_exact(width: usize, s: &str) -> Result<Self> {
        if !crate::object::integer(s) || s.starts_with('-') {

                format!("unsigned canonical INT required, found {s}"),

            .len()
            .checked_mul(4)

    pub fn to_decimal(&self) -> String {
        if self.is_zero() {
            return "0".into();
        }
        let mut words = self.words.clone();
        let mut digits = Vec::new();
        while words.iter().any(|w| *w != 0) {
            let mut remainder = 0u128;
            for word in words.iter_mut().rev() {
                let n = (remainder << 64) | (*word as u128);

    pub fn to_u128(&self) -> Result<u128> {

    fn get(&self, index: usize) -> bool {

    fn put(&mut self, index: usize, value: bool) {
        let bit = 1u64 << (index % 64);

            self.words[index / 64] |= bit;

    fn trim(&mut self) {

    }
    fn same(&self, other: &Self) -> Result<()> {
        if self.width != other.width {
            err("§3.3", "bit-vector operand width mismatch")
        } else {
            Ok(())
        }
    }
    pub fn resize(&self, width: usize, sign_extend: bool) -> Result<Self> {
        let mut out = Self::zero(width)?;
        for i in 0..width.min(self.width) {
            out.put(i, self.get(i));
        }
        if sign_extend && width > self.width && self.get(self.width - 1) {
            for i in self.width..width {
                out.put(i, true);
            }
        }
        Ok(out)
    }
    pub fn unsigned_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Result<Ordering> {
        self.same(other)?;
        Ok(self.words.iter().rev().cmp(other.words.iter().rev()))
    }
    pub fn signed_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Result<Ordering> {
        self.same(other)?;
        let a = self.get(self.width - 1);
        let b = other.get(self.width - 1);
        if a != b {
            Ok(if a { Ordering::Less } else { Ordering::Greater })
        } else {
            self.unsigned_cmp(other)
        }
    }
    fn negate(&self) -> Self {
        let mut out = self.clone();
        let mut carry = true;
        for word in &mut out.words {
            let (n, c) = (!*word).overflowing_add(u64::from(carry));
            *word = n;
            carry = c;
        }
        out.trim();
        out
    }
    pub fn binary(&self, op: &str, other: &Self) -> Result<Self> {
        self.same(other)?;
        let mut out = Self::zero(self.width)?;
        match op {
            "and" | "or" | "xor" => {
                for ((out, a), b) in out.words.iter_mut().zip(&self.words).zip(&other.words) {
                    *out = match op {
                        "and" => a & b,
                        "or" => a | b,
                        _ => a ^ b,
                    };
                }
            }
            "add" => {
                let mut carry = 0u128;
                for ((out, a), b) in out.words.iter_mut().zip(&self.words).zip(&other.words) {

    /// The §4.2 lift.div flag: Some(5) for a zero divisor, Some(6) for signed

    pub fn division_fault(&self, other: &Self, signed: bool) -> Result<Option<u128>> {

                *w == if i + 1 == other.words.len() && !self.width.is_multiple_of(64) {
                    (1u64 << (self.width % 64)) - 1
                } else {
                    u64::MAX
                }
            })
        {
            return err("§5.4", "FAULT_UB_SDIV_OVERFLOW (6)");
        }
        let a = if negative_a {
            self.negate()
        } else {
            self.clone()
        };
        let b = if negative_b {
            other.negate()
        } else {
            other.clone()
        };
        let mut q = Self::zero(self.width)?;
        let mut r = Self::zero(self.width)?;
        for i in (0..self.width).rev() {
            // r<b before the shift. Preserve the one extra comparison bit.
            let overflow = r.get(self.width - 1);
            let mut carry = u64::from(a.get(i));
            for word in &mut r.words {
                let next = *word >> 63;
                *word = (*word << 1) | carry;
                carry = next;
            }
            r.trim();
            if overflow || r.unsigned_cmp(&b)? != Ordering::Less {
                r = r.binary("sub", &b)?;
                q.put(i, true);
            }
        }
        if negative_a != negative_b {
            q = q.negate();
        }
        if negative_a {
            r = r.negate();
        }
        Ok((q, r))
    }
}

//! §5.6 borrowed systems: the translation lemma, and an exact symbolic decision
//! of the frame factorisation P_F = P' ⊗ I_B.
//!
//! A frame is a permutation, so its action on basis states is a vector of
//! Boolean functions. Each is held in algebraic normal form (ANF: an XOR of
//! AND-monomials over the frame's input wires), which is canonical: two ANFs
//! denote the same function iff they are equal. P_F = P' ⊗ I_B iff every
//! borrowed output equals its input variable and no other output mentions a
//! borrowed variable. For Boolean-gate circuits this is a total, exact decision
//! over the frame's full domain (T3), with no wire-count limit; permutation loops use repeated
//! squaring; mixed loops carry facts through every iteration or a proved invariant. Opaque applications retain their full
//! input expressions: composition substitutes recursively into those inputs and
//! interns the resulting application, rather than freezing an ANF variable.
//! This proves identities valid for arbitrary black-box functions; unresolved
//! function-specific identities need a checked claim. Calls whose outputs would
//! depend on borrowed wires cannot be decided this way: they require the
//! §12 borrow_frames claim the specification names, checked when present
//! (src/claims.rs). SPEC-QUESTIONS 20 records this reading.
use crate::{
    err,
    object::list,
    validation::{gate, gate_operands, normalize_call},
    Error, Function, Instruction, Object, Result, Type,
};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

pub fn validate_translation_lemma(
    v: &[Instruction],
    w: &[Instruction],
    x: &BTreeSet<String>,
    borrowed: &BTreeSet<String>,
) -> Result<()> {
    if !x.is_disjoint(borrowed) {
        return err("§5.6", "translation lemma requires X disjoint from B");
    }
    let flips = |sequence: &[Instruction]| -> Result<Vec<(Vec<String>, String)>> {
        sequence
            .iter()
            .map(|i| {
                if !["x", "cx", "ccx", "mcx"].contains(&i.op.as_str()) {
                    return err("§5.6", "translation lemma contains a non-X-family gate");
                }
                let (c, t, _, _) = gate_operands(i)?;
                Ok((c, t[0].clone()))
            })
            .collect()
    };
    let v = flips(v)?;
    let w = flips(w)?;
    let controls: BTreeSet<_> = w.iter().flat_map(|(c, _)| c.iter().cloned()).collect();
    for (c, t) in v {
        if !borrowed.contains(&t) || c.iter().any(|c| !x.contains(c)) {
            return err("§5.6", "V must target only B with controls only in X");
        }
    }
    for (c, t) in w {
        if x.contains(&t) || borrowed.contains(&t) || controls.contains(&t) {
            return err("§5.6", "W target overlaps X, B, or W's controls");
        }
        if c.iter().filter(|c| borrowed.contains(*c)).count() > 1 {
            return err("§5.6", "W gate has more than one borrowed control");
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// An ANF monomial: sorted, distinct variable ids (the empty monomial is 1).
type Mono = Vec<u32>;
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Default)]
struct Poly(BTreeSet<Mono>);
impl Poly {
    fn zero() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }
    fn one() -> Self {
        Self(BTreeSet::from([Vec::new()]))
    }
    fn var(v: u32) -> Self {
        Self(BTreeSet::from([vec![v]]))
    }
    fn xor(&self, o: &Self) -> Self {
        Self(self.0.symmetric_difference(&o.0).cloned().collect())
    }
    fn and(&self, o: &Self) -> Self {
        let mut out = BTreeSet::new();
        for a in &self.0 {
            for b in &o.0 {
                let mut m: Mono = a.iter().chain(b).copied().collect();
                m.sort_unstable();
                m.dedup();
                if !out.insert(m.clone()) {
                    out.remove(&m);
                }
            }
        }
        Self(out)
    }
    fn mentions(&self, vars: &BTreeSet<u32>) -> bool {
        self.0.iter().flatten().any(|v| vars.contains(v))
    }
}

/// A compiled operation on named wires.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Node {
    /// Target ^= AND of controls (with polarity).
    Flip(Vec<(String, bool)>, String),
    /// Controlled exchange of two wires.
    Swap(Vec<(String, bool)>, String, String),
    /// The actual `n` repetitions of a structured body. Permutation bodies
    /// compose carried maps AND return obligations by squaring; mixed bodies
    /// transfer gate facts per visit or under a proved invariant. This includes
    /// borrowing inside inlined child calls.
    Repeat(u64, Vec<Node>),
    /// A black-box function of `inputs` XORed (or, for qinplace, assigned)
    /// into `outputs`, keyed by the callee: oracle calls and qinplace.
    Opaque {
        key: String,
        controls: Vec<(String, bool)>,
        inputs: Vec<String>,
        outputs: Vec<String>,
        assign: bool,
    },
    /// A non-permutation operation (non-diagonal or diagonal gate, measurement-free
    /// non-permutation call): it ends a frame and may not touch a borrowed wire.
    Other(Vec<String>),
    /// Known gate action, separate from its FULL touched set used by §5.6.
    Quantum {
        key: String,
        inverse: String,
        controls: Vec<(String, bool)>,
        targets: Vec<String>,
        diagonal: bool,
    },
    /// Allocate clean wires; image preparation is represented by explicit flips.
    Alloc(Vec<String>),
    Free(Vec<String>),
    /// Unconditional lifetime boundaries, retained inside Repeat and adjoints.
    Borrow(Vec<String>),
    Return(Vec<String>),
}
impl Node {
    fn wires(&self, out: &mut BTreeSet<String>) {
        match self {
            Self::Flip(c, t) => {
                out.extend(c.iter().map(|(w, _)| w.clone()));
                out.insert(t.clone());
            }
            Self::Swap(c, a, b) => {
                out.extend(c.iter().map(|(w, _)| w.clone()));
                out.insert(a.clone());
                out.insert(b.clone());
            }
            Self::Repeat(_, body) => body.iter().for_each(|n| n.wires(out)),
            Self::Opaque {
                controls,
                inputs,
                outputs,
                ..
            } => {
                out.extend(controls.iter().map(|(w, _)| w.clone()));
                out.extend(inputs.iter().cloned());
                out.extend(outputs.iter().cloned());
            }
            Self::Quantum {
                controls, targets, ..
            } => {
                out.extend(controls.iter().map(|(w, _)| w.clone()));
                out.extend(targets.iter().cloned());
            }
            Self::Other(w) | Self::Alloc(w) | Self::Free(w) | Self::Borrow(w) | Self::Return(w) => {
                out.extend(w.iter().cloned());
            }
        }
    }
    fn permutation(&self) -> bool {
        match self {
            Self::Other(_) | Self::Quantum { .. } => false,
            Self::Repeat(n, body) => *n == 0 || body.iter().all(Self::permutation),
            _ => true,
        }
    }
    fn adjoint(&self) -> Self {
        match self {
            Self::Repeat(n, body) => {
                Self::Repeat(*n, body.iter().rev().map(Self::adjoint).collect())
            }
            Self::Opaque {
                assign: true,
                key,
                controls,
                inputs,
                outputs,
            } => Self::Opaque {
                key: format!("inverse({key})"),
                controls: controls.clone(),
                inputs: inputs.clone(),
                outputs: outputs.clone(),
                assign: true,
            },
            Self::Quantum {
                key,
                inverse,
                controls,
                targets,
                diagonal,
            } => Self::Quantum {
                key: inverse.clone(),
                inverse: key.clone(),
                controls: controls.clone(),
                targets: targets.clone(),
                diagonal: *diagonal,
            },
            Self::Alloc(w) => Self::Free(w.clone()),
            Self::Free(w) => Self::Alloc(w.clone()),
            Self::Borrow(w) => Self::Return(w.clone()),
            Self::Return(w) => Self::Borrow(w.clone()),
            other => other.clone(),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone)]
struct Trace {
    bundles: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>,
    borrowed: BTreeSet<String>,
    nodes: Vec<Node>,
}
struct Compiler<'a> {
    trace: Option<BTreeMap<usize, Vec<Trace>>>,
    live_borrowed: BTreeSet<String>,
    object: &'a Object,
    bundles: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>,
    regions: BTreeMap<String, (u64, Vec<Vec<String>>)>,
    borrowed: BTreeSet<String>,
    classical: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    generation: usize,
}
impl Compiler<'_> {
    fn classical(&self, name: &str) -> Result<String> {
        self.classical
            .get(name)
            .cloned()
            .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§3.3: unknown classical binding {name}")))
    }
    fn bundle(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
        if let Some((base, index)) = name.split_once('[') {
            let index = crate::object::host_count(index.trim_end_matches(']'), "wire index")?;
            return self
                .bundles
                .get(base)
                .and_then(|w| w.get(index as usize))
                .map(|w| vec![w.clone()])
                .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§3.3: unknown indexed operand {name}")));
        }
        self.bundles
            .get(name)
            .cloned()
            .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§3.3: unknown operand {name}")))
    }
    fn scalar(&self, name: &str) -> Result<String> {
        let w = self.bundle(name)?;
        if w.len() != 1 {
            return err("§3.3", format!("{name} must be one wire"));
        }
        Ok(w[0].clone())
    }
    fn fresh(&mut self, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
        let generation = self.generation;
        self.generation += 1;
        (0..width)
            .map(|bit| format!("v{generation}_{bit}"))
            .collect()
    }
    fn produce(&mut self, name: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
        let wires = self.fresh(width);
        self.bundles.insert(name.into(), wires.clone());
        wires
    }
    /// The address condition `a == i` as literals on the address wires.
    fn address(&self, a: &str, i: usize) -> Result<Vec<(String, bool)>> {
        Ok(self
            .bundle(a)?
            .into_iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(bit, w)| (w, i >> bit & 1 == 1))
            .collect())
    }
    fn declare_regions(&mut self, f: &Function, out: &mut Vec<Node>) -> Result<()> {
        for i in crate::validation::region_declarations(f) {
            let a = &i.operands;
            let aw = crate::object::host_count(&a[1], "qregion address width")?;
            let w = crate::object::host_count(&a[2], "qregion cell width")? as usize;
            let cells = crate::oracle::power_of_two(aw as u128)
                .and_then(|n| usize::try_from(n).ok())
                .ok_or_else(|| Error("host limit: region exceeds host address space".into()))?;
            let image = match a.get(3) {
                Some(img) => self
                    .object
                    .data
                    .get(img.trim_start_matches('@'))
                    .cloned()
                    .ok_or_else(|| Error("§4.6: unresolved qregion image".into()))?,
                None => vec![0; (cells * w).div_ceil(8)],
            };
            let mut all = Vec::new();
            for _ in 0..cells {
                all.push(self.fresh(w));
            }
            let flat: Vec<String> = all.iter().flatten().cloned().collect();
            out.push(Node::Alloc(flat.clone()));
            for (bit, wire) in flat.into_iter().enumerate() {
                if image[bit / 8] >> (bit % 8) & 1 == 1 {
                    // §4.6: image gates, like allocation/release, are unconditional.
                    out.push(Node::Flip(Vec::new(), wire));
                }
            }
            self.regions.insert(a[0].clone(), (aw, all));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    /// Compile the complete §4.6 local-region lifetime, not just its entry.
    /// Reversing these nodes (§5.3) recreates each image before the inverse
    /// body and restores/releases it afterward, even under a call predicate.
    fn compile_function(
        &mut self,
        f: &Function,
        context: &[(String, bool)],
        out: &mut Vec<Node>,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let mut entry = Vec::new();
        self.declare_regions(f, &mut entry)?;
        let exit: Vec<_> = entry.iter().rev().map(Node::adjoint).collect();
        out.extend(entry);
        for block in &f.blocks {
            self.compile(&block.instructions, context, out)?;
        }
        out.extend(exit);
        Ok(())
    }
    fn compile(
        &mut self,
        seq: &[Instruction],
        context: &[(String, bool)],
        out: &mut Vec<Node>,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let mut predicate = context.to_vec();
        for i in seq {
            let start = out.len();
            let snapshot = self.trace.as_ref().map(|_| Trace {
                bundles: self.bundles.clone(),
                borrowed: self.live_borrowed.clone(),
                nodes: Vec::new(),
            });
            let a = &i.operands;
            let op = i.op.as_str();
            let with = |extra: &[(String, bool)], base: &[(String, bool)]| {
                let mut c = base.to_vec();
                for e in extra {
                    if !c.contains(e) {
                        c.push(e.clone());
                    }
                }
                c
            };
            match op {
                "qalloc" | "qborrow" => {
                    let n = crate::object::host_count(&a[1], "allocation width")? as usize;
                    let wires = self.produce(&i.lhs[0], n);
                    if op == "qborrow" {
                        self.borrowed.extend(wires.iter().cloned());
                        self.live_borrowed.extend(wires.iter().cloned());
                        out.push(Node::Borrow(wires));
                    } else {
                        out.push(Node::Alloc(wires.clone()));
                    }
                }
                "qfree" => out.push(Node::Free(self.bundle(&a[0])?)),
                "qreturn" => {
                    let wires = self.bundle(&a[0])?;
                    for w in &wires {
                        self.live_borrowed.remove(w);
                    }
                    out.push(Node::Return(wires));
                }
                "qpred" => predicate.push((self.scalar(&a[0])?, true)),
                "qunpred" => {
                    predicate
                        .pop()
                        .ok_or_else(|| Error("§3.5: predicate underflow".into()))?;
                }
                "qcopy" | "quncopy" | "qxor" => {
                    let source = self.bundle(&a[0])?;
                    let target = match op {
                        "qcopy" => {
                            let w = self.produce(&i.lhs[0], source.len());
                            out.push(Node::Alloc(w.clone()));
                            w
                        }
                        _ => self.bundle(&a[1])?,
                    };
                    for (s, t) in source.iter().zip(&target) {
                        out.push(Node::Flip(
                            with(&[(s.clone(), true)], &predicate),
                            t.clone(),
                        ));
                    }
                    if op == "quncopy" {
                        out.push(Node::Free(target));
                    }
                }
                "qexch" => {
                    for (s, t) in self.bundle(&a[0])?.into_iter().zip(self.bundle(&a[1])?) {
                        out.push(Node::Swap(predicate.clone(), s, t));
                    }
                }
                "qif" => {
                    let selector = self.scalar(&a[0])?;
                    self.compile(
                        &i.bodies[0],
                        &with(&[(selector.clone(), true)], &predicate),
                        out,
                    )?;
                    self.compile(&i.bodies[1], &with(&[(selector, false)], &predicate), out)?;
                }
                "qloop" => {
                    let n = crate::object::host_count(&a[0], "qloop trip count")?;
                    if a.len() == 3 {
                        // Coherent while: iteration i runs under cond[0..=i] (§4.6),
                        // n = the width of cond, which is materialised anyway.
                        let selectors = self.bundle(&a[2])?;
                        for iteration in 0..n as usize {
                            let c: Vec<_> = selectors[..=iteration]
                                .iter()
                                .map(|w| (w.clone(), true))
                                .collect();
                            self.compile(&i.bodies[0], &with(&c, &predicate), out)?;
                        }
                    } else {
                        let mut body = Vec::new();
                        self.compile(&i.bodies[0], &predicate, &mut body)?;
                        out.push(Node::Repeat(n, body));
