````rust
//! Exact amplitude arithmetic for the §14.2 state-vector simulator.
//!
//! Every amplitude the gates of §4.4 can produce from |0...0> lies in the ring
//! K[z, 1/z] of Laurent polynomials over K = Q(sqrt 2, i) with dyadic rational
//! coordinates, where z = e^{i 2^-1075}: h contributes sqrt(2)/2, s and t
//! contribute i and (1+i) sqrt(2)/2, and a rotation by a finite binary64
//! angle theta contributes e^{+-i theta/2} = z^{+-m} with the exact integer
//! m = theta * 2^1074 (theta/2 is an integer multiple of 2^-1075 because every
//! finite binary64 value is an integer multiple of 2^-1074).
//!
//! z is transcendental over the algebraic numbers (Lindemann-Weierstrass:
//! e^alpha is transcendental for every nonzero algebraic alpha, here
//! alpha = i 2^-1075), so a Laurent polynomial in z is zero iff all of its
//! coefficients are zero. Cleanliness (§3.3 "clean on every basis
//! configuration", §4.3 qfree) is therefore decided exactly: no tolerance.
use std::cmp::Ordering;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

/// Signed arbitrary-precision integer, magnitude in little-endian u32 limbs.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct BigInt {
    negative: bool,
    limbs: Vec<u32>,
}
impl BigInt {
    pub fn zero() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }
    pub fn from_i128(v: i128) -> Self {
        let negative = v < 0;
        let mut m = v.unsigned_abs();
        let mut limbs = Vec::new();
        while m != 0 {
            limbs.push(m as u32);
            m >>= 32;
        }
        Self { negative, limbs }
    }
    pub fn is_zero(&self) -> bool {
        self.limbs.is_empty()
    }
    fn normalize(mut self) -> Self {
        while self.limbs.last() == Some(&0) {
            self.limbs.pop();
        }
        if self.limbs.is_empty() {
            self.negative = false;
        }
        self
    }
    fn cmp_magnitude(a: &[u32], b: &[u32]) -> Ordering {
        a.len()
            .cmp(&b.len())
            .then_with(|| a.iter().rev().cmp(b.iter().rev()))
    }
    fn add_magnitude(a: &[u32], b: &[u32]) -> Vec<u32> {
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(a.len().max(b.len()) + 1);
        let mut carry = 0u64;
        for i in 0..a.len().max(b.len()) {
            let s = *a.get(i).unwrap_or(&0) as u64 + *b.get(i).unwrap_or(&0) as u64 + carry;
            out.push(s as u32);
            carry = s >> 32;
        }
        if carry != 0 {
            out.push(carry as u32);
        }
        out
    }
    /// a - b for |a| >= |b|.
    fn sub_magnitude(a: &[u32], b: &[u32]) -> Vec<u32> {
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(a.len());
        let mut borrow = 0i64;
        for (i, x) in a.iter().enumerate() {
            let mut d = *x as i64 - *b.get(i).unwrap_or(&0) as i64 - borrow;
            borrow = 0;
            if d < 0 {
                d += 1 << 32;
                borrow = 1;
            }
            out.push(d as u32);
        }
        out
    }
    pub fn add(&self, other: &Self) -> Self {
        if self.negative == other.negative {
            return Self {
                negative: self.negative,
                limbs: Self::add_magnitude(&self.limbs, &other.limbs),
            }
            .normalize();
        }
        match Self::cmp_magnitude(&self.limbs, &other.limbs) {
            Ordering::Equal => Self::zero(),
            Ordering::Greater => Self {
                negative: self.negative,
                limbs: Self::sub_magnitude(&self.limbs, &other.limbs),
            }
            .normalize(),
            Ordering::Less => Self {
                negative: other.negative,
                limbs: Self::sub_magnitude(&other.limbs, &self.limbs),
            }
            .normalize(),
        }
    }
    pub fn neg(&self) -> Self {
        Self {
            negative: !self.negative && !self.is_zero(),
            limbs: self.limbs.clone(),
        }
    }
    pub fn mul(&self, other: &Self) -> Self {
        if self.is_zero() || other.is_zero() {
            return Self::zero();
        }
        let mut out = vec![0u32; self.limbs.len() + other.limbs.len()];
        for (i, a) in self.limbs.iter().enumerate() {
            let mut carry = 0u64;
            for (j, b) in other.limbs.iter().enumerate() {
                let t = out[i + j] as u64 + (*a as u64) * (*b as u64) + carry;
                out[i + j] = t as u32;
                carry = t >> 32;
            }
            let mut k = i + other.limbs.len();
            while carry != 0 {
                let t = out[k] as u64 + carry;
                out[k] = t as u32;
                carry = t >> 32;
                k += 1;
            }
        }
        Self {
            negative: self.negative != other.negative,
            limbs: out,
        }
        .normalize()
    }
    pub fn shl(&self, bits: u64) -> Self {
        if self.is_zero() {
            return Self::zero();
        }
        let words = (bits / 32) as usize;
        let shift = (bits % 32) as u32;
        let mut limbs = vec![0u32; words];
        let mut carry = 0u32;
        for l in &self.limbs {
            limbs.push((l << shift) | carry);
            carry = if shift == 0 { 0 } else { l >> (32 - shift) };
        }
        if carry != 0 {
            limbs.push(carry);
        }
        Self {
            negative: self.negative,
            limbs,
        }
        .normalize()
    }
    pub fn trailing_zeros(&self) -> u64 {
        let mut n = 0u64;
        for l in &self.limbs {
            if *l == 0 {
                n += 32;
            } else {
                return n + l.trailing_zeros() as u64;
            }
        }
        n
    }
    /// Right shift of the magnitude, truncating toward zero.
    fn shr(&self, bits: u64) -> Self {
        let words = (bits / 32) as usize;
        let shift = (bits % 32) as u32;
        let src = &self.limbs[words.min(self.limbs.len())..];
        let mut limbs = Vec::with_capacity(src.len());
        for (i, l) in src.iter().enumerate() {
            let high = if shift == 0 {
                0
            } else {
                src.get(i + 1).map_or(0, |h| h << (32 - shift))
            };
            limbs.push((l >> shift) | high);
        }
        Self {
            negative: self.negative,
            limbs,
        }
        .normalize()
    }
}
impl PartialOrd for BigInt {
    fn partial_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<Ordering> {
        Some(self.cmp(other))
    }
}
impl Ord for BigInt {
    fn cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Ordering {
        match (self.negative, other.negative) {
            (false, true) => Ordering::Greater,
            (true, false) => Ordering::Less,
            (false, false) => Self::cmp_magnitude(&self.limbs, &other.limbs),
            (true, true) => Self::cmp_magnitude(&other.limbs, &self.limbs),
        }
    }
}

/// A dyadic rational n * 2^-k, normalized (n odd or k = 0).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct Dyadic {
    n: BigInt,
    k: u64,
}
impl Dyadic {
    pub fn int(v: i128) -> Self {
        Self {
            n: BigInt::from_i128(v),
            k: 0,
        }
    }
    /// v * 2^-k.
    pub fn scaled(v: i128, k: u64) -> Self {
        Self {
            n: BigInt::from_i128(v),
            k,
        }
        .normalize()
    }
    fn normalize(mut self) -> Self {
        if self.n.is_zero() {
            self.k = 0;
            return self;
        }
        let t = self.n.trailing_zeros().min(self.k);
        if t > 0 {
            self.n = self.n.shr(t);
            self.k -= t;
        }
        self
    }
    pub fn is_zero(&self) -> bool {
        self.n.is_zero()
    }
    pub fn add(&self, o: &Self) -> Self {
        let k = self.k.max(o.k);
        Self {
            n: self.n.shl(k - self.k).add(&o.n.shl(k - o.k)),
            k,
        }
        .normalize()
    }
    pub fn neg(&self) -> Self {
        Self {
            n: self.n.neg(),
            k: self.k,
        }
    }
    pub fn mul(&self, o: &Self) -> Self {
        Self {
            n: self.n.mul(&o.n),
            k: self.k + o.k,
        }
        .normalize()
    }
    pub fn to_f64(&self) -> f64 {
        if self.n.is_zero() {
            return 0.0;
        }
        let bits = 32 * (self.n.limbs.len() as i128 - 1)
            + i128::from(32 - self.n.limbs.last().unwrap().leading_zeros());
        let exponent = bits - 1 - i128::from(self.k);
        let sign = if self.n.negative { -1.0 } else { 1.0 };
        if exponent > 1023 {
            return sign * f64::INFINITY;
        }
        if exponent < -1075 {
            return sign * 0.0;
        }
        // Round once, to 53 significant bits for normals or the 2^-1074
        // subnormal grid. Neither numerator nor cancelling denominator is ever
        // converted separately. Guard + sticky implement nearest, ties to even.
        let shift = (bits - 53).max(i128::from(self.k) - 1074).max(0) as u64;
        let top = self.n.shr(shift);
        let mut mantissa = top
            .limbs
            .iter()
            .rev()
            .fold(0u64, |v, l| (v << 32) | u64::from(*l));
        if shift != 0 {
            let guard_index = shift - 1;
            let guard = self
                .n
                .limbs
                .get((guard_index / 32) as usize)
                .is_some_and(|l| (l >> (guard_index % 32)) & 1 != 0);
            let sticky = self.n.trailing_zeros() < guard_index;
            if guard && (sticky || mantissa & 1 != 0) {
                mantissa += 1;
            }
        }
        let scale = i128::from(shift) - i128::from(self.k);
        // Here scale is in [-1074, 971]. Multiplying by the representable
        // power of two introduces no second rounding except final overflow.
        let power = if scale < -1022 {
            f64::from_bits(1u64 << (scale + 1074))
        } else {
            f64::from_bits(((scale + 1023) as u64) << 52)
        };
        sign * (mantissa as f64 * power)
    }
}
/// a + b sqrt(2), a and b dyadic.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct Root2 {
    a: Dyadic,
    b: Dyadic,
}
impl Root2 {
    fn is_zero(&self) -> bool {
        self.a.is_zero() && self.b.is_zero()
    }
    fn add(&self, o: &Self) -> Self {
        Self {
            a: self.a.add(&o.a),
            b: self.b.add(&o.b),
        }
    }
    fn neg(&self) -> Self {
        Self {
            a: self.a.neg(),
            b: self.b.neg(),
        }
    }
    fn mul(&self, o: &Self) -> Self {
        // (a + b r)(c + d r) = (ac + 2bd) + (ad + bc) r.
        Self {
            a: self.a.mul(&o.a).add(&self.b.mul(&o.b).mul(&Dyadic::int(2))),
            b: self.a.mul(&o.b).add(&self.b.mul(&o.a)),
        }
    }
    fn to_f64(&self) -> f64 {
        let a = self.a.to_f64();
        let b = self.b.to_f64() * std::f64::consts::SQRT_2;
        let value = a + b;
        if !value.is_finite()
            || (a.signum() != b.signum() && value.abs() < a.abs().max(b.abs()) * 1e-12)
        {
            measurement::root2_approximate(self)
        } else {
            value
        }
    }
}
/// x + y i over Q(sqrt 2).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct Coefficient {
    re: Root2,
    im: Root2,
}
impl Coefficient {
    pub fn is_zero(&self) -> bool {
        self.re.is_zero() && self.im.is_zero()
    }
    fn add(&self, o: &Self) -> Self {
        Self {
            re: self.re.add(&o.re),
            im: self.im.add(&o.im),
        }
    }
    fn mul(&self, o: &Self) -> Self {
        Self {
            re: self.re.mul(&o.re).add(&self.im.mul(&o.im).neg()),
            im: self.re.mul(&o.im).add(&self.im.mul(&o.re)),
        }
    }
    fn new(re_a: Dyadic, re_b: Dyadic, im_a: Dyadic, im_b: Dyadic) -> Self {
        Self {
            re: Root2 { a: re_a, b: re_b },
            im: Root2 { a: im_a, b: im_b },
        }
    }
}
/// An exact amplitude: a Laurent polynomial in z with K coefficients.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct Amplitude {
    terms: BTreeMap<BigInt, Coefficient>,
}
impl Amplitude {
    pub fn zero() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }
    pub fn one() -> Self {
        Self::constant(Coefficient::new(
            Dyadic::int(1),
            Dyadic::default(),
            Dyadic::default(),
            Dyadic::default(),
        ))
    }
    fn constant(c: Coefficient) -> Self {
        Self::monomial(BigInt::zero(), c)
    }
    fn monomial(e: BigInt, c: Coefficient) -> Self {
        let mut terms = BTreeMap::new();
        if !c.is_zero() {
            terms.insert(e, c);
        }
        Self { terms }
    }
    pub fn is_zero(&self) -> bool {
        self.terms.is_empty()
    }
    pub fn add(&self, o: &Self) -> Self {
        let mut terms = self.terms.clone();
        for (e, c) in &o.terms {
            let sum = terms.get(e).map_or_else(|| c.clone(), |p| p.add(c));
            if sum.is_zero() {
                terms.remove(e);
            } else {
                terms.insert(e.clone(), sum);
            }
        }
        Self { terms }
    }
    pub fn mul(&self, o: &Self) -> Self {
        let mut out = Self::zero();
        for (e, c) in &self.terms {
            for (f, d) in &o.terms {
                out = out.add(&Self::monomial(e.add(f), c.mul(d)));
            }
        }
        out
    }
    /// A floating-point value of the amplitude, for diagnostics only.
    pub fn approximate(&self) -> (f64, f64) {
        let mut re = 0f64;
        let mut im = 0f64;
        for (e, c) in &self.terms {
            // Evaluate exp(i * e * 2^-1075) as a product of finite
            // limb phases. The exponent is unbounded even though each input
            // angle is binary64. Converting their sum first can overflow.
            let (mut co, mut si) = (1.0, 0.0);
            for (j, limb) in e.limbs.iter().enumerate() {
                if *limb == 0 {
                    continue;
                }
                let scale = 32 * j as i64 - 1075;
                // Keep as much argument as binary64 can represent exactly;
                // extra squarings amplify phase rounding error unnecessarily.
                let highest_bit = 31 - limb.leading_zeros();
                let bounded = scale.min(1023 - i64::from(highest_bit));
                let angle = if bounded < -1022 {
                    // Scale the limb before rounding a subnormal phase.
                    (*limb as f64 * 2f64.powi((bounded + 1022) as i32)) * 2f64.powi(-1022)
                } else {
                    *limb as f64 * 2f64.powi(bounded as i32)
                };
                let (mut s, mut c) = angle.sin_cos();
                for _ in bounded..scale {
                    (c, s) = (c * c - s * s, 2.0 * c * s);
                    // Squaring a rounded unit complex otherwise amplifies
                    // radial error; this affects display only, never equality.
                    let norm = c.hypot(s);
                    (c, s) = (c / norm, s / norm);
                }
                (co, si) = (co * c - si * s, co * s + si * c);
            }
            let s = if e.negative { -si } else { si };
            let (x, y) = (c.re.to_f64(), c.im.to_f64());
            re += x * co - y * s;
            im += x * s + y * co;
        }
        (re, im)
    }
}

/// A finite binary64 as the dyadic rational it denotes exactly.
fn dyadic_from_f64(v: f64) -> Option<Dyadic> {
    if !v.is_finite() {
        return None;
    }
    if v == 0.0 {
        return Some(Dyadic::default());
    }
    let bits = v.to_bits();
    let negative = bits >> 63 == 1;
    let exponent = ((bits >> 52) & 0x7ff) as i64;
    let fraction = (bits & ((1u64 << 52) - 1)) as i128;
    // v = mantissa * 2^e with e >= -1074 (subnormals have no implicit bit).
    let (mantissa, e) = if exponent == 0 {
        (fraction, -1074i64)
    } else {
        (fraction | (1i128 << 52), exponent - 1075)
    };
    let n = BigInt::from_i128(if negative { -mantissa } else { mantissa });
    Some(if e >= 0 {
        Dyadic {
            n: n.shl(e as u64),
            k: 0,
        }
        .normalize()
    } else {
        Dyadic { n, k: (-e) as u64 }.normalize()
    })
}
/// The exact amplitude of a pair of finite binary64 values (each denotes a
/// dyadic rational, held exactly; the pair is zero iff both are zero).
pub fn amplitude_from_f64(re: f64, im: f64) -> Option<Amplitude> {
    Some(Amplitude::constant(Coefficient::new(
        dyadic_from_f64(re)?,
        Dyadic::default(),
        dyadic_from_f64(im)?,
        Dyadic::default(),
    )))
}

/// Exact entries of the §4.4 gates. `m` is theta * 2^1074 (theta/2 in units
/// of 2^-1075) for the rotations.
pub fn rotation_exponent(theta: f64) -> Option<BigInt> {
    if !theta.is_finite() {
        return None;
    }
    if theta == 0.0 {
        return Some(BigInt::zero());
    }
    let bits = theta.to_bits();
    let negative = bits >> 63 == 1;
    let exponent = ((bits >> 52) & 0x7ff) as i64;
    let fraction = (bits & ((1u64 << 52) - 1)) as i128;
    // theta = mantissa * 2^(e) with e >= -1074.
    let (mantissa, e) = if exponent == 0 {
        (fraction, -1074i64)
    } else {
        (fraction | (1i128 << 52), exponent - 1075)
    };
    let m = BigInt::from_i128(if negative { -mantissa } else { mantissa });
    // m * 2^(e + 1074) is an integer because e >= -1074.
    Some(m.shl((e + 1074) as u64))
}
pub fn gate_matrix(op: &str, angle: Option<f64>) -> Option<[Amplitude; 4]> {
    let zero = Dyadic::default;
    let half_root = || Dyadic::scaled(1, 1);
    let c = |re: (i128, u64, i128, u64), im: (i128, u64, i128, u64)| {
        Amplitude::constant(Coefficient::new(
            Dyadic::scaled(re.0, re.1),
            Dyadic::scaled(re.2, re.3),
            Dyadic::scaled(im.0, im.1),
            Dyadic::scaled(im.2, im.3),
        ))
    };
    let one = Amplitude::one;
    let z = Amplitude::zero;
    let i = || c((0, 0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0, 0));
    let minus_i = || c((0, 0, 0, 0), (-1, 0, 0, 0));
    let h = || Amplitude::constant(Coefficient::new(zero(), half_root(), zero(), zero()));
    let minus_h = || {
        Amplitude::constant(Coefficient::new(
            zero(),
            Dyadic::scaled(-1, 1),
            zero(),
            zero(),
        ))
    };
    let phase = |e: BigInt| {
        Amplitude::monomial(e, Coefficient::new(Dyadic::int(1), zero(), zero(), zero()))
    };
    let half = |v: i128, imag: bool, e: BigInt| {
        let d = Dyadic::scaled(v, 1);
        Amplitude::monomial(
            e,
            if imag {
                Coefficient::new(zero(), zero(), d, zero())
            } else {
                Coefficient::new(d, zero(), zero(), zero())
            },
        )
    };
    Some(match op {
        "x" | "cx" | "ccx" | "mcx" => [z(), one(), one(), z()],
        "h" => [h(), h(), h(), minus_h()],
        "s" => [one(), z(), z(), i()],
        "sdg" => [one(), z(), z(), minus_i()],
        "t" => [one(), z(), z(), c((0, 0, 1, 1), (0, 0, 1, 1))],
        "tdg" => [one(), z(), z(), c((0, 0, 1, 1), (0, 0, -1, 1))],
        "rz" => {
            let m = rotation_exponent(angle?)?;
            [phase(m.neg()), z(), z(), phase(m)]
        }
        "rx" | "ry" => {
            let m = rotation_exponent(angle?)?;
            // cos = (z^m + z^-m)/2; sin = (z^m - z^-m)/(2i) = -i(z^m - z^-m)/2.
            let cos = half(1, false, m.clone()).add(&half(1, false, m.neg()));
            let minus_i_sin = half(-1, false, m.clone()).add(&half(1, false, m.neg()));
            let sin = half(-1, true, m.clone()).add(&half(1, true, m.neg()));
            if op == "rx" {
                [cos.clone(), minus_i_sin.clone(), minus_i_sin, cos]
            } else {
                let minus_sin = half(1, true, m.clone()).add(&half(-1, true, m.neg()));
                [cos.clone(), minus_sin, sin, cos]
            }
        }
        _ => return None,
    })
}
/// The exact amplitude -1 (cz, and controlled phases).
pub fn minus_one() -> Amplitude {
    Amplitude::constant(Coefficient::new(
        Dyadic::int(-1),
        Dyadic::default(),
        Dyadic::default(),
        Dyadic::default(),
    ))
}

impl BigInt {
    fn mul_small(&self, m: u32) -> Self {
        self.mul(&Self::from_i128(m as i128))
    }
    /// (quotient, remainder) of a nonnegative value by a small divisor.
    fn divmod_small(&self, d: u32) -> (Self, u32) {
        let mut out = vec![0u32; self.limbs.len()];
        let mut rem = 0u64;
        for (i, l) in self.limbs.iter().enumerate().rev() {
            let cur = (rem << 32) | *l as u64;
            out[i] = (cur / d as u64) as u32;
            rem = cur % d as u64;
        }
        (
            Self {
                negative: self.negative,
                limbs: out,
            }
            .normalize(),
            rem as u32,
        )
    }
    pub fn to_decimal(&self) -> String {
        if self.is_zero() {
            return "0".into();
        }
        let mut digits = Vec::new();
        let mut v = Self {
            negative: false,
            limbs: self.limbs.clone(),
        };
        while !v.is_zero() {
            let (q, r) = v.divmod_small(10);
            digits.push(b'0' + r as u8);
            v = q;
        }
        if self.negative {
            digits.push(b'-');
        }
        digits.reverse();
        String::from_utf8(digits).unwrap_or_default()
    }
}
/// An exact decimal m * 10^e, for §12.3 error composition (no rounding).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Decimal {
    m: BigInt,
    e: i64,
}
impl Decimal {
    pub fn zero() -> Self {
        Self {
            m: BigInt::zero(),
            e: 0,
        }
    }
    /// Parses a nonnegative JSON decimal (digits, optional fraction, optional exponent).
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        let (mantissa, exponent) = match s.split_once(['e', 'E']) {
            Some((m, e)) => (m, e.trim_start_matches('+').parse::<i64>().ok()?),
            None => (s, 0),
        };
        let (int, frac) = mantissa.split_once('.').unwrap_or((mantissa, ""));
        if int.is_empty()
            || !int.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit())
            || !frac.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit())
        {
            return None;
        }
        let mut m = BigInt::zero();
        for d in int.bytes().chain(frac.bytes()) {
            m = m.mul_small(10).add(&BigInt::from_i128((d - b'0') as i128));
        }
        Some(Self {
            m,
            e: exponent - frac.len() as i64,
        })
    }
    fn align(&self, e: i64) -> BigInt {
        let mut m = self.m.clone();
        for _ in e..self.e {
            m = m.mul_small(10);
        }
        m
    }
    pub fn add(&self, o: &Self) -> Self {
        let e = self.e.min(o.e);
        Self {
            m: self.align(e).add(&o.align(e)),
            e,
        }
    }
    pub fn mul_int(&self, n: u128) -> Self {
        Self {
            m: self.m.mul(&BigInt::from_i128(n as i128)),
            e: self.e,
        }
    }
    /// Plain decimal text without an exponent, trailing zeros removed.
    pub fn to_text(&self) -> String {
        let mut m = self.m.clone();
        let mut e = self.e;
        while e < 0 && !m.is_zero() {
            let (q, r) = m.divmod_small(10);
            if r != 0 {
                break;
            }
            m = q;
            e += 1;
        }
        let digits = m.to_decimal();
        if m.is_zero() {
            return "0".into();
        }
        if e >= 0 {
            return format!("{digits}{}", "0".repeat(e as usize));
        }
        let point = digits.len() as i64 + e;
        if point > 0 {
            format!(
                "{}.{}",
                &digits[..point as usize],
                &digits[point as usize..]
            )
        } else {
            format!("0.{}{digits}", "0".repeat((-point) as usize))
        }
    }
}

mod measurement;
pub(crate) use measurement::{normalized, probability};

#[cfg(test)]
mod r7_tests {
    use super::*;
    #[test]
    fn r7_root2_cancellation_does_not_overflow_intermediate_terms() {
        // (1 - sqrt(2))^810 has enormous opposite-sign coordinates, but
        // a positive representable subnormal value. Independent scalar formula.
        let factor = Root2 {
            a: Dyadic::int(1),
            b: Dyadic::int(-1),
        };
        let mut value = Root2 {
            a: Dyadic::int(1),
            b: Dyadic::int(0),
        };
        for _ in 0..810 {
            value = value.mul(&factor);
        }
        let actual = value.to_f64();
        let expected = (std::f64::consts::SQRT_2 - 1.0).powi(810);
        assert!(actual.is_finite() && actual > 0.0);
        assert!((actual / expected - 1.0).abs() < 1e-10);
    }
    #[test]
    fn r7_dyadic_scaled_conversion_boundary_rounding_and_subnormals() {
        for k in [1023, 1024, 1056, 2000, 5000] {
            let n = BigInt::from_i128(1).shl(k).add(&BigInt::from_i128(1));
            assert_eq!(Dyadic { n: n.clone(), k }.to_f64(), 1.0, "k={k}");
            assert_eq!(Dyadic { n: n.neg(), k }.to_f64(), -1.0);
        }
        assert_eq!(Dyadic::scaled(1, 1074).to_f64().to_bits(), 1);
        assert_eq!(Dyadic::scaled(1, 1075).to_f64().to_bits(), 0);
        assert_eq!(Dyadic::scaled(3, 1075).to_f64().to_bits(), 2);
        assert_eq!(Dyadic::scaled(5, 1075).to_f64().to_bits(), 2);
        assert_eq!(Dyadic::scaled((1i128 << 53) + 1, 53).to_f64(), 1.0);
        assert_eq!(
            Dyadic::scaled((1i128 << 53) + 3, 53).to_f64().to_bits(),
            1.0f64.to_bits() + 2
        );
        assert_eq!(dyadic_from_f64(f64::MAX).unwrap().to_f64(), f64::MAX);
    }
}
````

````rust
use crate::{err, object::list, validation::normalize_call, Error, Function, Object, Result, Type};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
#[derive(Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
struct Views {
    live: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    dead: BTreeSet<String>,
}
impl Object {
    pub(crate) fn validate_handle_views(
        &self,
        f: &Function,
        types: &BTreeMap<String, Type>,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let mut work = vec![(0usize, Views::default())];
        let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
        while let Some((block, mut views)) = work.pop() {
            if !seen.insert((block, views.clone())) {
                continue;
            }
            for instruction in &f.blocks[block].instructions {
                let op = instruction.op.as_str();
                let a = &instruction.operands;
                let region = matches!(op, "oracle_call" | "action_call" | "ctl" | "adj");
                let operands: Vec<String> = match op {
                    "qreg.new" => Vec::new(),
                    "qreg.slice" | "qreg.free" | "measure" => vec![a[0].clone()],
                    "qreg.concat" => a.clone(),
                    _ => {
                        let mut values = Vec::new();
                        for operand in a {
                            if operand.starts_with('(') {
                                values.extend(list(operand)?);
                            } else if operand.starts_with('^') {
                                if let Some((_, suffix)) = operand.split_once('(') {
                                    values.extend(list(&format!("({suffix}"))?);
                                }
                            } else {
                                values.push(operand.clone());
                            }
                        }
                        values
                    }
                };
                let handles: Vec<_> = operands
                    .into_iter()
                    .filter(|n| matches!(types.get(n), Some(Type::Qreg(_))))
                    .collect();
                for handle in &handles {
                    if views.live.values().any(|parent| parent == handle) {
                        return err("§3.3", format!("use of viewed parent {handle}"));
                    }
                    if views.dead.contains(handle) {
                        return err("§3.3", format!("view {handle} used after its region call"));
                    }
                    if views.live.contains_key(handle) && !region {
                        return err(
                            "§3.3",
                            format!("view {handle} may only be an operand of one region call"),
                        );
                    }
                }
                if op == "qreg.slice" {
                    let view = instruction.lhs[0].clone();
                    views.dead.remove(&view);
                    views.live.insert(view, a[0].clone());
                }
                if region {
                    normalize_call(instruction)?;
                    for handle in handles {
                        if views.live.remove(&handle).is_some() {
                            views.dead.insert(handle);
                        }
                    }
                }
                if op == "br" {
                    for branch in if a.len() == 1 { &a[..] } else { &a[1..] } {
                        let (label, _) = branch
                            .trim_start_matches('^')
                            .split_once('(')
                            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§3.4: malformed branch".into()))?;
                        let target = f
                            .blocks
                            .iter()
                            .position(|b| b.name == label)
                            .expect("validated block");
                        work.push((target, views.clone()));
                    }
                }
                if matches!(op, "ret" | "trap") && !views.live.is_empty() {
                    return err(
                        "§3.3",
                        "view is not consumed by exactly one region call on every exit path",
                    );
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
````

````rust
use crate::{err, json::Json, sha256_hex, Error, Object, Result};
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Identity {
    pub interface_hashes: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// None denotes a symbol whose dependency closure still has an unresolved import.
    pub closure_hashes: BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>,
    pub envelopes: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    pub object_hash: String,
    pub scc_members: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>,
    pub scc_hashes: BTreeMap<String, String>,
}

/// Symbol reference tokens only: @ inside a quoted string is ordinary text.
fn references(line: &str) -> Vec<(usize, usize, &str)> {
    let bytes = line.as_bytes();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    let mut quoted = false;
    while i < bytes.len() {
        if quoted {
            if bytes[i] == b'\\' {
                i += 2;
                continue;
            }
            if bytes[i] == b'"' {
                quoted = false;
            }
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }
        if bytes[i] == b'"' {
            quoted = true;
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }
        if bytes[i] == b'@'
            && i + 1 < bytes.len()
            && (bytes[i + 1].is_ascii_alphabetic() || bytes[i + 1] == b'_')
        {
            let start = i;
            i += 2;
            while i < bytes.len()
                && (bytes[i].is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(bytes[i], b'_' | b'.'))
            {
                i += 1;
            }
            out.push((start, i, &line[start + 1..i]));
        } else {
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    out
}

        Ok(Identity {
            interface_hashes: hashes,
            closure_hashes: closure,
            envelopes,
            object_hash: sha256_hex(canonical.as_bytes()),
            scc_members,
            scc_hashes,

    }
    pub fn check_hashes(&self) -> Result<()> {
        let identity = self.identity()?;
        for s in self.symbols()?.values() {
            let n = s.get("name")?.string()?;
            if s.get("interface_hash")?.string()? != identity.interface_hashes[n] {

    fn envelope(
        &self,
        n: &str,

        let kind = symbol.get("kind")?.string()?;

                lines.push(format!("device {key} {}", v.canonical()));
            }
        }

#[derive(Default)]
struct HashPass {
    hashes: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    closed: BTreeMap<String, bool>,
    envelopes: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    scc_members: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>,
    scc_hashes: BTreeMap<String, String>,
}
pub(crate) fn hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    bytes.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()
}
pub(crate) fn layout_leaves(layout: &Json) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, Json>> {
    let mut leaves = BTreeMap::new();
    for (k, v) in layout.object()? {
        match k.as_str() {
            "globals" => {
                for (n, e) in v.object()? {
                    leaves.insert(format!("globals.{n}"), e.clone());
                }
            }
            "interface_regions" => {
                for (n, rs) in v.object()? {
                    for (r, e) in rs.object()? {
                        leaves.insert(format!("interface_regions.{n}.{r}"), e.clone());
                    }
                }
            }
            _ => {
                leaves.insert(k.clone(), v.clone());
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(leaves)
}
fn components(graph: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>) -> Vec<Vec<String>> {
    struct Tarjan<'a> {
        graph: &'a BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>,
        index: BTreeMap<String, usize>,
        low: BTreeMap<String, usize>,
        stack: Vec<String>,
        on: BTreeSet<String>,
        result: Vec<Vec<String>>,
    }
    fn visit(t: &mut Tarjan<'_>, v: &str) {
        let index = t.index.len();
        t.index.insert(v.into(), index);
        t.low.insert(v.into(), index);
        t.stack.push(v.into());
        t.on.insert(v.into());
        for w in &t.graph[v] {
            if !t.graph.contains_key(w) {
                continue;
            }
            if !t.index.contains_key(w) {
                visit(t, w);
                t.low.insert(v.into(), t.low[v].min(t.low[w]));
            } else if t.on.contains(w) {
                t.low.insert(v.into(), t.low[v].min(t.index[w]));
            }
        }
        if t.low[v] == t.index[v] {
            let mut comp = Vec::new();
            loop {
                let w = t.stack.pop().expect("Tarjan stack");
                t.on.remove(&w);
                comp.push(w.clone());
                if w == v {
                    break;
                }
            }
            comp.sort();
            t.result.push(comp);
        }
    }
    let mut t = Tarjan {
        graph,
        index: BTreeMap::new(),
        low: BTreeMap::new(),
        stack: Vec::new(),
        on: BTreeSet::new(),
        result: Vec::new(),
    };
    for v in graph.keys() {
        if !t.index.contains_key(v) {
            visit(&mut t, v);
        }
    }
    t.result
}
````

````rust
//! Strict JSON and RFC 8785 canonical serialization, without dependencies.
use crate::{err, Result};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Json {
    Null,
    Bool(bool),
    Number(String),
    String(String),
    Array(Vec<Json>),
    Object(BTreeMap<String, Json>),
}

impl Json {
    pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<Self> {
        let mut p = Parser {
            text,
            pos: 0,
            depth: 0,
        };
        let value = p.value()?;
        p.ws();
        if p.pos != text.len() {
            return err("§16.1", "trailing JSON input");
        }
        Ok(value)
    }
    pub fn canonical(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Self::Null => "null".into(),
            Self::Bool(b) => b.to_string(),
            Self::Number(n) => n.clone(),
            Self::String(s) => quote(s),
            Self::Array(a) => format!(
                "[{}]",
                a.iter().map(Self::canonical).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(",")
            ),
            Self::Object(o) => {
                let mut entries: Vec<_> = o.iter().collect();
                entries.sort_by(|(a, _), (b, _)| a.encode_utf16().cmp(b.encode_utf16()));
                format!(
                    "{{{}}}",
                    entries
                        .into_iter()
                        .map(|(k, v)| format!("{}:{}", quote(k), v.canonical()))
                        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                        .join(",")
                )
            }
        }
    }
    pub fn object(&self) -> Result<&BTreeMap<String, Json>> {
        if let Self::Object(o) = self {
            Ok(o)
        } else {
            err("§9.1", "expected JSON object")
        }
    }
    pub fn array(&self) -> Result<&[Json]> {
        if let Self::Array(a) = self {
            Ok(a)
        } else {
            err("§9.1", "expected JSON array")
        }
    }
    pub fn string(&self) -> Result<&str> {
        if let Self::String(s) = self {
            Ok(s)
        } else {
            err("§9.1", "expected JSON string")
        }
    }
    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Result<&Json> {
        self.object()?
            .get(key)
            .ok_or_else(|| crate::Error(format!("§9.1: missing field {key}")))
    }
    /// The canonical decimal text of a metadata integer of any size (§9.1):
    /// a JSON number iff it is at most 2^53 - 1, otherwise a decimal string.
    pub fn uint_text(&self) -> Result<&str> {
        let s = match self {
            Self::Number(s) | Self::String(s) => s,
            _ => return err("§9.1", "expected unsigned integer"),
        };
        if !crate::object::integer(s) || s.starts_with('-') {
            return err("§9.1", format!("invalid canonical unsigned integer {s}"));
        }
        let exact = s.len() < 16 || (s.len() == 16 && s.as_str() <= "9007199254740991");
        if matches!(self, Self::Number(_)) != exact {
            return err(
                "§9.1",
                format!("integer {s} must be a JSON number iff it is at most 2^53 - 1"),
            );
        }
        Ok(s)
    }
    /// Metadata integers may be JSON numbers or decimal strings (§9.1).
    pub fn uint(&self) -> Result<u128> {
        let s = self.uint_text()?;
        let value = s.parse::<u128>().map_err(|_| {
            crate::Error(format!("§9.1: integer {s} exceeds this field's u128 range"))
        })?;
        // §9.1 "Integers that may exceed 2^53 are decimal strings": a value above
        // 2^53 - 1 is a string and a smaller one a number (SPEC-QUESTIONS 17).
        let exact = value <= 9_007_199_254_740_991;
        if matches!(self, Self::Number(_)) != exact {
            return err(
                "§9.1",
                format!("integer {s} must be a JSON number iff it is at most 2^53 - 1"),
            );
        }
        Ok(value)
    }
    pub fn fields(&self, required: &[&str], optional: &[&str]) -> Result<()> {
        let obj = self.object()?;
        for key in required {
            self.get(key)?;
        }
        for key in obj.keys() {
            if !required.contains(&key.as_str()) && !optional.contains(&key.as_str()) {
                return err("§9.1", format!("unknown field {key}"));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

pub fn quote(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::from("\"");
    for c in s.chars() {
        match c {
            '"' => out.push_str("\\\""),
            '\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            '\u{8}' => out.push_str("\\b"),
            '\t' => out.push_str("\\t"),
            '\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
            '\u{c}' => out.push_str("\\f"),
            '\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            c if c < ' ' => out.push_str(&format!("\\u{:04x}", c as u32)),
            c => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out.push('"');
    out
}

fn canonical_number(raw: &str) -> Result<String> {
    let n: f64 = raw
        .parse()
        .map_err(|_| crate::Error("§16.1: invalid JSON number".into()))?;
    if !n.is_finite() {
        return err("§16.1", "non-finite JSON number");
    }
    if n == 0.0 {
        return Ok("0".into());
    }
    let negative = n < 0.0;
    let display = n.abs().to_string();
    let (mantissa, exponent) = match display.split_once('e') {
        Some((m, e)) => (m, e.parse::<i32>().expect("Rust float exponent")),
        None => (display.as_str(), 0),
    };
    let dot = mantissa.find('.').unwrap_or(mantissa.len()) as i32;
    let digits: String = mantissa.chars().filter(|c| *c != '.').collect();
    let leading = digits.bytes().take_while(|b| *b == b'0').count();
    let position = dot + exponent - leading as i32;
    let digits = digits[leading..].trim_end_matches('0');
    let mut out = if negative {
        "-".to_string()
    } else {
        String::new()
    };
    if position > 0 && position <= 21 {
        if position as usize >= digits.len() {
            out.push_str(digits);
            out.push_str(&"0".repeat(position as usize - digits.len()));
        } else {
            let (a, b) = digits.split_at(position as usize);
            out.push_str(a);
            out.push('.');
            out.push_str(b);
        }
    } else if position > -6 && position <= 0 {
        out.push_str("0.");
        out.push_str(&"0".repeat((-position) as usize));
        out.push_str(digits);
    } else {
        out.push_str(&digits[..1]);
        if digits.len() > 1 {
            out.push('.');
            out.push_str(&digits[1..]);
        }
        out.push('e');
        let e = position - 1;
        if e >= 0 {
            out.push('+');
        }
        out.push_str(&e.to_string());
    }
    Ok(out)
}

struct Parser<'a> {
    text: &'a str,
    pos: usize,
    depth: usize,
}
impl Parser<'_> {
    fn peek(&self) -> Option<u8> {
        self.text.as_bytes().get(self.pos).copied()
    }
    fn ws(&mut self) {
        while matches!(self.peek(), Some(b' ' | b'\n' | b'\r' | b'\t')) {
            self.pos += 1;
        }
    }
    fn take(&mut self, b: u8) -> bool {
        if self.peek() == Some(b) {
            self.pos += 1;
            true
        } else {
            false
        }
    }
    fn expect(&mut self, b: u8) -> Result<()> {
        if self.take(b) {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            err(
                "§16.1",
                format!("expected JSON '{}' at byte {}", b as char, self.pos),
            )
        }
    }
    fn value(&mut self) -> Result<Json> {
        self.ws();
        self.depth += 1;
        if self.depth > 256 {
            return err("§16.1", "JSON nesting exceeds 256");
        }
        let value = match self.peek() {
            Some(b'"') => Json::String(self.string()?),
            Some(b'{') => {
                self.pos += 1;
                self.ws();
                let mut o = BTreeMap::new();
                if !self.take(b'}') {
                    loop {
                        self.ws();
                        let key = self.string()?;
                        self.ws();
                        self.expect(b':')?;
                        let v = self.value()?;
                        if o.insert(key.clone(), v).is_some() {
                            return err("§16.1", format!("duplicate JSON key {key}"));
                        }
                        self.ws();
                        if self.take(b'}') {
                            break;
                        }
                        self.expect(b',')?;
                    }
                }
                Json::Object(o)
            }
            Some(b'[') => {
                self.pos += 1;
                self.ws();
                let mut a = Vec::new();
                if !self.take(b']') {
                    loop {
                        a.push(self.value()?);
                        self.ws();
                        if self.take(b']') {
                            break;
                        }
                        self.expect(b',')?;
                    }
                }
                Json::Array(a)
            }
            Some(b'-' | b'0'..=b'9') => {
                let start = self.pos;
                self.take(b'-');
                if !self.take(b'0') {
                    if !matches!(self.peek(), Some(b'1'..=b'9')) {
                        return err("§16.1", "invalid JSON integer");
                    }
                    while matches!(self.peek(), Some(b'0'..=b'9')) {
                        self.pos += 1;
                    }
                }
                if self.take(b'.') {
                    let p = self.pos;
                    while matches!(self.peek(), Some(b'0'..=b'9')) {
                        self.pos += 1;
                    }
                    if p == self.pos {
                        return err("§16.1", "empty fraction");
                    }
                }
                if self.take(b'e') || self.take(b'E') {
                    if !self.take(b'+') {
                        self.take(b'-');
                    }
                    let p = self.pos;
                    while matches!(self.peek(), Some(b'0'..=b'9')) {
                        self.pos += 1;
                    }
                    if p == self.pos {
                        return err("§16.1", "empty exponent");
                    }
                }
                Json::Number(canonical_number(&self.text[start..self.pos])?)
            }
            _ => {
                let mut found = None;
                for (s, v) in [
                    ("null", Json::Null),
                    ("true", Json::Bool(true)),
                    ("false", Json::Bool(false)),
                ] {
                    if self.text[self.pos..].starts_with(s) {
                        self.pos += s.len();
                        found = Some(v);
                        break;
                    }
                }
                found.ok_or_else(|| {
                    crate::Error(format!("§16.1: invalid JSON at byte {}", self.pos))
                })?
            }
        };
        self.depth -= 1;
        Ok(value)
    }
    fn hex4(&mut self) -> Result<u16> {
        let end = self.pos + 4;
        let s = self
            .text
            .as_bytes()
            .get(self.pos..end)
            .ok_or_else(|| crate::Error("§16.1: short Unicode escape".into()))?;
        let mut n = 0;
        for b in s {
            n = n * 16
                + match b {
                    b'0'..=b'9' => (b - b'0') as u16,
                    b'a'..=b'f' => (b - b'a' + 10) as u16,
                    b'A'..=b'F' => (b - b'A' + 10) as u16,
                    _ => return err("§16.1", "invalid Unicode escape"),
                };
        }
        self.pos = end;
        Ok(n)
    }
    fn string(&mut self) -> Result<String> {
        self.expect(b'"')?;
        let mut out = String::new();
        loop {
            match self.peek() {
                None => return err("§16.1", "unterminated JSON string"),
                Some(b'"') => {
                    self.pos += 1;
                    return Ok(out);
                }
                Some(b'\\') => {
                    self.pos += 1;
                    let b = self
                        .peek()
                        .ok_or_else(|| crate::Error("§16.1: short escape".into()))?;
                    self.pos += 1;
                    out.push(match b {
                        b'"' => '"',
                        b'\\' => '\\',
                        b'/' => '/',
                        b'b' => '\u{8}',
                        b'f' => '\u{c}',
                        b'n' => '\n',
                        b'r' => '\r',
                        b't' => '\t',
                        b'u' => {
                            let hi = self.hex4()?;
                            let n = if (0xd800..=0xdbff).contains(&hi) {
                                self.expect(b'\\')?;
                                self.expect(b'u')?;
                                let lo = self.hex4()?;
                                if !(0xdc00..=0xdfff).contains(&lo) {
                                    return err("§16.1", "invalid low surrogate");
                                }
                                0x10000 + (((hi as u32 - 0xd800) << 10) | (lo as u32 - 0xdc00))
                            } else {
                                hi as u32
                            };
                            char::from_u32(n)
                                .ok_or_else(|| crate::Error("§16.1: lone surrogate".into()))?
                        }
                        _ => return err("§16.1", "invalid JSON escape"),
                    });
                }
                Some(0..=31) => return err("§16.1", "unescaped JSON control character"),
                _ => {
                    let c = self.text[self.pos..].chars().next().expect("UTF-8 char");
                    self.pos += c.len_utf8();
                    out.push(c);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
````

````rust
/// A diagnostic always names the normative rule that was violated.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Error(pub String);
impl std::fmt::Display for Error {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(&self.0)
    }
}
impl std::error::Error for Error {}
pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, Error>;
pub(crate) fn err<T>(rule: &str, message: impl std::fmt::Display) -> Result<T> {
    Err(Error(format!("{rule}: {message}")))
}
pub fn version() -> &'static str {
    "0.8"
}
````

````rust
//! Symbol resolution and canonical linked objects (§9.3).
use crate::{err, identity::hex, json::Json, Error, Object, Result, SECTIONS};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

impl Object {
    pub fn link(objects: &[Object]) -> Result<Self> {
        let first = objects
            .first()
            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§9.3: no objects to link".into()))?;
        let mut result = Self {
            text: String::new(),
            ptr_width: first.ptr_width,
            metadata: BTreeMap::new(),
            functions: BTreeMap::new(),
            function_order: Vec::new(),
            data: BTreeMap::new(),
        };
        let mut definitions: BTreeMap<String, Json> = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut imports: Vec<(String, Json)> = Vec::new();
        let mut known_closures: BTreeMap<String, String> = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut old_identities = Vec::new();
        let mut certificates: Vec<Json> = Vec::new();
        for object in objects {
            object.check_hashes()?;
            if object.ptr_width != result.ptr_width {
                return err("§9.3", "pointer widths differ");
            }
            let identity = object.identity()?;
            for (name, hash) in &identity.closure_hashes {
                if let Some(hash) = hash {
                    if known_closures.get(name).is_some_and(|prior| prior != hash) {
                        return err("§9.3", format!("unequal closure definitions for @{name}"));
                    }
                    known_closures.insert(name.clone(), hash.clone());
                }
            }
            old_identities.push(identity);
            for symbol in object.symbols()?.values() {
                let name = symbol.get("name")?.string()?;
                if let Some(prior) = definitions.get(name) {
                    if prior.get("signature")? != symbol.get("signature")?
                        || prior.get("kind")? != symbol.get("kind")?
                    {
                        return err("§9.3", format!("incompatible duplicate @{name}"));
                    }
                } else {
                    definitions.insert(name.into(), symbol.clone());
                }
            }
            for (name, function) in &object.functions {
                if result
                    .functions
                    .get(name)
                    .is_some_and(|prior| prior.lines != function.lines)
                {
                    return err("§9.3", format!("conflicting function bodies for @{name}"));
                }
                result.functions.insert(name.clone(), function.clone());
            }
            for (name, bytes) in &object.data {
                if result.data.get(name).is_some_and(|prior| prior != bytes) {
                    return err("§9.3", format!("conflicting data @{name}"));
                }
                result.data.insert(name.clone(), bytes.clone());
            }
            if let Some(entries) = object.section("imports") {
                for (name, value) in entries.object()? {
                    imports.push((name.clone(), value.clone()));
                }
            }
            if let Some(c) = object.section("certificate") {
                certificates.push(c.clone());
            }
            for (section, value) in &object.metadata {
                if matches!(section.as_str(), "symbols" | "imports" | "certificate") {
                    continue;
                }
                match result.metadata.get_mut(section) {
                    None => {
                        result.metadata.insert(section.clone(), value.clone());
                    }
                    Some(prior) => merge_metadata(prior, value, section)?,
                }
            }
        }
        for (name, import) in &imports {
            let definition = definitions
                .get(name)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error(format!("§9.3: unresolved import @{name}")))?;
            if import.get("signature")? != definition.get("signature")? {
                return err("§9.3", format!("import signature mismatch for @{name}"));
            }
        }
        result.function_order = result.functions.keys().cloned().collect();
        result.metadata.insert(
            "symbols".into(),
            Json::Object(
                definitions
                    .values()
                    .cloned()
                    .enumerate()
                    .map(|(i, s)| (i.to_string(), s))
                    .collect(),
            ),
        );
        // Resolution changes envelopes which used unresolved-name fingerprints.
        // Recompute the graph before rebinding any external metadata.
        let identity = result.identity()?;
        for (name, import) in &imports {
            if let Some(pin) = import.object()?.get("pinned_closure_hash") {
                if identity.closure_hashes[name].as_deref() != Some(pin.string()?) {
                    return err("§9.3", format!("pinned closure mismatch for @{name}"));
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(Json::Object(symbols)) = result.metadata.get_mut("symbols") {
            for symbol in symbols.values_mut() {
                let n = symbol.get("name")?.string()?.to_string();
                let Json::Object(fields) = symbol else {
                    return err("§9.1", "symbol entries are objects");
                };
                fields.insert(
                    "interface_hash".into(),
                    Json::String(identity.interface_hashes[&n].clone()),
                );
            }
        }
        let mut replacements = BTreeMap::new();
        for old in old_identities {
            for (name, hash) in old.interface_hashes {
                replacements.insert(hash, identity.interface_hashes[&name].clone());
            }
            for (name, hash) in old.closure_hashes {
                if let Some(hash) = hash {
                    let next = identity.closure_hashes[&name].clone().ok_or_else(|| {
                        Error(format!("§9.3: @{name} is still unresolved after linking"))
                    })?;
                    replacements.insert(hash, next);
                }
            }
        }
        let old_schedule = result
            .metadata
            .get("schedule")
            .map(|s| crate::sha256_hex(s.canonical().as_bytes()));
        for section in ["schedule", "coverage"] {
            if let Some(value) = result.metadata.get_mut(section) {
                replace_hashes(value, &replacements)?;
            }
        }
        // A rebound schedule has a new schedule_hash (§9.2): rebind references.
        if let (Some(old), Some(new)) = (
            old_schedule,
            result
                .metadata
                .get("schedule")
                .map(|s| crate::sha256_hex(s.canonical().as_bytes())),
        ) {
            replacements.insert(old, new);
        }
        for c in &mut certificates {
            replace_hashes(c, &replacements)?;
        }
        if !certificates.is_empty() {
            result
                .metadata
                .insert("certificate".into(), compose_certificates(&certificates)?);
        }
        result.text = result.render()?;
        let object_hash = result.identity()?.object_hash;
        if let Some(Json::Object(cert)) = result.metadata.get_mut("certificate") {
            if let Some(Json::Object(bindings)) = cert.get_mut("bindings") {
                bindings.insert("object_hash".into(), Json::String(object_hash));
            }
        }
        result.text = result.render()?;
        let linked = Self::parse(&result.text)?;
        linked.check_hashes()?;
        Ok(linked)
    }
    pub(crate) fn render(&self) -> Result<String> {
        let mut text=format!("bennett-object isa=0.8 object=0.8 launch=0.8 sched=0.8 cert=0.8 coverage=0.8 target=0.8 ptr_width={}\n",self.ptr_width);
        for section in SECTIONS {
            let body = match section {
                "functions" => {
                    if self.functions.is_empty() {
                        continue;
                    }
                    self.function_order
                        .iter()
                        .map(|n| self.functions[n].lines.join("\n"))
                        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                        .join("\n")
                }
                "data" => {
                    if self.data.is_empty() {
                        continue;
                    }
                    self.data
                        .iter()
                        .map(|(n, b)| format!("{n} {}", hex(b)))
                        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                        .join("\n")
                }
                _ => match self.section(section) {
                    Some(value) => value.canonical(),
                    None => continue,
                },
            };
            text.push_str(&format!("\nsection {section}\n{body}\n"));
        }
        Ok(text)
    }
}
fn merge_metadata(destination: &mut Json, source: &Json, path: &str) -> Result<()> {
    if destination == source {
        return Ok(());
    }
    if path == "coverage.entries" {
        let (Json::Array(a), Json::Array(b)) = (destination, source) else {
            return err("§9.3", "coverage entries must be arrays");
        };
        for e in b {
            if !a.contains(e) {
                a.push(e.clone());
            }
        }
        return Ok(());
    }
    let recursive = matches!(
        path,
        "layout"
            | "layout.globals"
            | "layout.interface_regions"
            | "devices"
            | "devices.models"
            | "devices.services"
            | "coverage"
    ) || path.starts_with("layout.interface_regions.")
        && path.split('.').count() == 3;
    if !recursive {
        return err("§9.3", format!("conflicting metadata at {path}"));
    }
    let Json::Object(target) = destination else {
        return err("§9.3", format!("metadata object required at {path}"));
    };
    for (key, value) in source.object()? {
        if let Some(prior) = target.get_mut(key) {
            merge_metadata(prior, value, &format!("{path}.{key}"))?;
        } else {
            target.insert(key.clone(), value.clone());
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
fn replace_hashes(value: &mut Json, replacements: &BTreeMap<String, String>) -> Result<()> {
    match value {
        Json::String(s) => {
            if let Some(next) = replacements.get(s) {
                *s = next.clone();
            }
        }
        Json::Array(values) => {
            for v in values {
                replace_hashes(v, replacements)?;
            }
        }
        Json::Object(fields) => {
            let previous = std::mem::take(fields);
            for (key, mut value) in previous {
                replace_hashes(&mut value, replacements)?;
                // Composite keys "<hash>:<variant>:<controls>" rebind their hash.
                let key = match replacements.get(&key) {
                    Some(next) => next.clone(),
                    None => match key.split_once(':') {
                        Some((h, rest)) if replacements.contains_key(h) => {
                            format!("{}:{rest}", replacements[h])
                        }
                        _ => key,
                    },
                };
                if let Some(prior) = fields.insert(key.clone(), value.clone()) {
                    if prior != value {
                        return err(
                            "§9.3",
                            format!("two metadata keys rebind to {key} with different values"),
                        );
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        _ => {}
    }
    Ok(())
}
/// §9.3 linking performs certificate composition (§12.3): the region records
/// of every certificate are united (one record per closure hash, equal where
/// they meet), multiplicities are united (equal where they meet), and
/// epsilon_total is recomputed by the sum over multiplicities from the local
/// error bounds, operator norms converting to diamond by x2 (SPEC-QUESTIONS 22).
/// The composed certificate binds to the first certificate's root region.
fn compose_certificates(certificates: &[Json]) -> Result<Json> {
    let first = &certificates[0];
    for c in &certificates[1..] {
        if c.get("versions")? != first.get("versions")? {
            return err("§9.3", "certificates disagree on versions");
        }
        for key in ["dialect_mapping_version", "target_hash"] {
            if c.get("bindings")?.get(key)? != first.get("bindings")?.get(key)? {
                return err("§9.3", format!("certificates bind different {key} values"));
            }
        }
        if c.get("composition")?.get("method")? != first.get("composition")?.get("method")? {
            return err("§12.3", "certificates use different composition methods");
        }
    }
    let mut regions = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut multiplicities = BTreeMap::new();
    for c in certificates {
        for (k, r) in c.get("regions")?.object()? {
            if regions.get(k).is_some_and(|prior: &Json| prior != r) {
                return err(
                    "§9.3",
                    format!("conflicting certificate records for region {k}"),
                );
            }
            regions.insert(k.clone(), r.clone());
        }
        for (k, n) in c.get("composition")?.get("multiplicities")?.object()? {
            if multiplicities.get(k).is_some_and(|prior: &Json| prior != n) {
                return err("§12.3", format!("conflicting multiplicities for {k}"));
            }
            multiplicities.insert(k.clone(), n.clone());
        }
    }
    let local = |region: &str, key: &str| -> Result<crate::exact::Decimal> {
        let Some(r) = regions.get(region) else {
            return err(
                "§12.3",
                format!("multiplicity names region {region} with no record"),
            );
        };
        let Some(e) = r.get("error")?.object()?.get(key) else {
            return Ok(crate::exact::Decimal::zero());
        };
        let l = e.get("local")?.object()?;
        let text = |v: &Json| -> Result<String> {
            Ok(match v {
                Json::Number(s) | Json::String(s) => s.clone(),
                _ => return err("§12.3", "error bound must be a decimal"),
            })
        };
        if let Some(d) = l.get("diamond") {
            return crate::exact::Decimal::parse(&text(d)?)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error("§12.3: invalid diamond bound".into()));
        }
        if let Some(o) = l.get("operator_norm") {
            return Ok(crate::exact::Decimal::parse(&text(o)?)
                .ok_or_else(|| Error("§12.3: invalid operator_norm bound".into()))?
                .mul_int(2));
        }
        Ok(crate::exact::Decimal::zero())
    };
    let mut total = crate::exact::Decimal::zero();
    for (k, n) in &multiplicities {
        let (region, key) = k
            .split_once(':')
            .ok_or_else(|| Error("§12.3: malformed multiplicity key".into()))?;
        total = total.add(&local(region, key)?.mul_int(n.uint()?));
    }
    let root = first.get("bindings")?.get("closure_hash")?.string()?;
    if let Some(r) = regions.get(root) {
        for key in r.get("error")?.object()?.keys() {
            total = total.add(&local(root, key)?);
        }
    }
    let mut out = first.clone();
    let Json::Object(fields) = &mut out else {
        return err("§12", "certificate must be an object");
    };
    fields.insert("regions".into(), Json::Object(regions));
    let total_text = total.to_text();
    let total_json = if total_text.contains('.') || total_text.len() > 15 {
        Json::String(total_text)
    } else {
        Json::Number(total_text)
    };
    fields.insert(
        "composition".into(),
        Json::Object(BTreeMap::from([
            (
                "epsilon_total".into(),
                Json::Object(BTreeMap::from([("diamond".into(), total_json)])),
            ),
            (
                "method".into(),
                first.get("composition")?.get("method")?.clone(),
            ),
            ("multiplicities".into(), Json::Object(multiplicities)),
        ])),
    );
    Ok(out)
}
````
