````rust
mod support;
use bennett_isa_ref::{
    validate_translation_lemma, Instruction, Object, QuantumBindings, QuantumState,
};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;
use support::object;
fn gate(op: &str, operands: &[&str]) -> Instruction {
    Instruction {
        lhs: Vec::new(),
        op: op.into(),
        operands: operands.iter().map(|s| (*s).into()).collect(),
        bodies: Vec::new(),
        line: 1,
    }
}
#[test]
fn translation_lemma_checks_all_four_required_negative_patterns() {
    let b = BTreeSet::from(["b".into(), "b2".into()]);
    let x = BTreeSet::from(["x".into()]);
    let v = [gate("cx", &["x", "b"])];
    let w = [gate("cx", &["b", "t"])];
    validate_translation_lemma(&v, &w, &x, &b).unwrap();
    // A V;W;V^-1 prefix lacks the required final W and is checked as a full frame below.
    assert!(validate_translation_lemma(
        &[gate("cx", &["b2", "b"])],
        &w,
        &BTreeSet::from(["b2".into()]),
        &b
    )
    .is_err());
    assert!(validate_translation_lemma(
        &[gate("cx", &["b", "x"])],
        &w,
        &BTreeSet::from(["b".into()]),
        &b
    )
    .is_err());
    assert!(validate_translation_lemma(
        &v,
        &[gate("swap", &["y", "z"]), gate("cx", &["b", "y"])],
        &x,
        &b
    )
    .is_err());
    assert!(validate_translation_lemma(
        &v,
        &[gate("cx", &["b", "y"]), gate("cx", &["y", "z"])],
        &x,
        &b
    )
    .is_err());
}
fn borrowed(body: &str) -> String {
    let signature = r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[1],"kind":"perm_action","mem":[],"mut":[1,1,1],"tier":"q"}"#;
    object(&[("a",signature,&format!("perm_action @a (t:wire mut, y:wire mut, z:wire mut) (x:wire in) () () ()\n^entry():\nb = qborrow any 1\n{body}\nqreturn b"))],"{}","")
}
#[test]
fn borrow_frame_exhaustion_rejects_hidden_dependence_on_borrowed_bits() {
    let raw = borrowed("cx b y\ncx y z\ncx b y");
    let error = Object::parse(&raw).expect_err("borrowed-dependent output accepted");
    assert!(error.to_string().contains("§5.6"));
}
#[test]
fn translation_pattern_returns_an_entangled_borrowed_system() {
    let o = Object::parse(&borrowed("cx x b\ncx b t\ncx x b\ncx b t")).unwrap();
    let mut q = QuantumState::new();
    let t = q.allocate(1).unwrap();
    let y = q.allocate(1).unwrap();
    let z = q.allocate(1).unwrap();
    let x = q.allocate(1).unwrap();
    let b = q.allocate(1).unwrap();
    let reference = q.allocate(1).unwrap();
    q.gate("h", &[b[0]], None, &[]).unwrap();
    q.gate("cx", &[b[0], reference[0]], None, &[]).unwrap();
    q.gate("x", &x, None, &[]).unwrap();
    let mut bindings = QuantumBindings::default();
    for (n, w) in [("t", t.clone()), ("y", y), ("z", z), ("x", x)] {
        bindings.bundles.insert(n.into(), w);
    }
    bindings.borrowed.push(b.clone());
    o.execute_action("a", &mut q, &bindings, false, &[])
        .unwrap();
    // The output is t=1 tensor the original Bell pair on borrowed b/reference.
    q.gate("x", &t, None, &[]).unwrap();
    q.gate("cx", &[b[0], reference[0]], None, &[]).unwrap();
    q.gate("h", &b, None, &[]).unwrap();
    q.release(&b).unwrap();
    q.release(&reference).unwrap();
}

#[test]
fn classical_region_calls_supply_only_designated_idle_registers() {
    use bennett_isa_ref::{ClassicalMachine, ClassicalValue, QuantumRegisters};
    let action = support::rehash(&borrowed("cx x b\ncx b t\ncx x b\ncx b t"));
    let sig = r#"{"abi":"0.8","kind":"cc","params":["qreg[1]","qreg[1]","qreg[1]","qreg[1]"],"results":[],"tier":"cc"}"#;
    let imports = format!(
        "{{\"a\":{{\"signature\":{}}}}}",
        action.symbols().unwrap()["0"]
            .get("signature")
            .unwrap()
            .canonical()
    );
    let caller=support::rehash(&object(&[("invoke",sig,"fn cc @invoke (t:qreg[1], y:qreg[1], z:qreg[1], x:qreg[1]) () () () ()\n^entry():\naction_call @a (t, y, z) (x) () ()\nret")],&imports,""));
    let program = Object::link(&[caller, action]).unwrap();
    let mut registers = QuantumRegisters::new();
    let mut ids = Vec::new();
    for _ in 0..5 {
        ids.push(registers.allocate(1).unwrap());
    }
    registers.prepare(ids[3], &[true]).unwrap();
    registers.prepare(ids[4], &[true]).unwrap();
    let args = ids[..4]
        .iter()
        .map(|id| ClassicalValue::Qreg(*id))
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    let mut m = ClassicalMachine::with_quantum_registers(&program, "invoke", &args, &[], registers)
        .unwrap();
    m.designate_idle_registers(&[ids[4]]).unwrap();
    let before = m.snapshot();
    assert_eq!(m.run(100).unwrap().fault, None);
    let r = m.quantum_registers();
    for id in [ids[0], ids[4]] {
        assert_eq!(
            r.quantum_state().read_basis(r.bundle(id).unwrap()).unwrap(),
            1
        );
    }
    m.reverse().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), before);
}

#[test]
fn lifted_permutation_actions_can_borrow_workspace_and_reverse() {
    use bennett_isa_ref::{Budget, OracleInput, OracleMachine};
    let action = support::rehash(&borrowed("cx x b\ncx b t\ncx x b\ncx b t"));
    let signature =
        r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[1],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":1,"tier":"q"}"#;
    let imports = format!(
        "{{\"a\":{{\"signature\":{}}}}}",
        action.symbols().unwrap()["0"]
            .get("signature")
            .unwrap()
            .canonical()
    );
    let caller=support::rehash(&object(&[("lifted",signature,"oracle @lifted (input:wire in) (target:wire) (fault:wire[4]) () ()\nregs { t:reg[1], y:reg[1], z:reg[1], x:reg[1] }\n^entry():\nx = lift.mov input\nt = lift.const.i1 0\ny = lift.const.i1 0\nz = lift.const.i1 0\nlift.perm_call @a (t, y, z) (x) () ()\nlift.retval t")],&imports,""));
    let o = Object::link(&[caller, action]).unwrap();
    for x in 0..2 {
        for steps in 0..8 {
            let input = OracleInput::bits(&[x]);
            let budget = Budget::steps(steps);
            let result = o.run_oracle("lifted", &input, budget).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(
                (result.payload, result.code),
                if steps >= 6 { (x, 0) } else { (0, 1) }
            );
            let mut m = OracleMachine::new(&o, "lifted", &input, budget).unwrap();
            let before = m.snapshot();
            for _ in 0..steps {
                m.forward_step().unwrap();
            }
            assert_eq!(m.outcome().unwrap(), result);
            for _ in 0..steps {
                m.inverse_step().unwrap();
            }
            assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), before);
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn exhaustive_borrow_identity_need_not_be_adjacent_gate_cancellation() {
    // The linear map (b,t) -> (t,b XOR t) has order three over GF(2).
    let text = borrowed("cx b t\ncx t b\ncx b t\ncx t b\ncx b t\ncx t b");
    let o = Object::parse(&text).unwrap();
    for b in 0..2 {
        for t in 0..2 {
            let mut q = QuantumState::new();
            let wires = q.allocate(5).unwrap();
            for (wire, value) in [(wires[0], t), (wires[4], b)] {
                if value == 1 {
                    q.gate("x", &[wire], None, &[]).unwrap();
                }
            }
            let mut bindings = QuantumBindings::default();
            for (name, wire) in ["t", "y", "z", "x"].iter().zip(&wires) {
                bindings.bundles.insert((*name).into(), vec![*wire]);
            }
            bindings.borrowed.push(vec![wires[4]]);
            let before = q.clone();
            o.execute_action("a", &mut q, &bindings, false, &[])
                .unwrap();
            assert_eq!(q, before);
        }
    }
}
````

````rust
use bennett_isa_ref::{ClassicalMachine, ClassicalValue, Object};

#[test]
fn dynamic_instances_loop_and_whole_run_reversal() {
    let o = Object::parse(include_str!("fixtures/classical.bisa")).unwrap();
    for n in 0..=8 {
        let mut m =
            ClassicalMachine::new(&o, "sum", &[ClassicalValue::int(8, n).unwrap()], &[]).unwrap();
        let before = m.snapshot();
        let r = m.run(1000).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(r.fault, None);
        assert_eq!(
            r.values,
            vec![ClassicalValue::int(8, n * (n + 1) / 2).unwrap()]
        );
        m.reverse().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), before);
    }
}
#[test]
fn nested_uncall_and_effects_are_reversed_exactly_once() {
    let o = Object::parse(include_str!("fixtures/classical.bisa")).unwrap();
    for name in ["nested", "effects"] {
        let mut m = ClassicalMachine::new(&o, name, &[], &[11, 22, 33]).unwrap();
        let before = m.snapshot();
        let result = m.run(1000).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(result.fault, None);
        assert_eq!(result.values, vec![ClassicalValue::int(64, 0).unwrap()]);
        if name == "nested" {
            assert_eq!(m.clock(), 0);
            assert_eq!(m.effect_tape_len(), 0);
        } else {
            assert_eq!(m.clock(), 1);
            assert_eq!(m.console(), &[11, 22, 33]);
            assert_eq!(m.effect_tape_len(), 5);
        }
        m.reverse().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), before);
    }
}
#[test]
fn faults_are_atomic_terminal_and_reversible() {
    let o = Object::parse(include_str!("fixtures/classical.bisa")).unwrap();
    for (name, code) in [
        ("impure", 4),
        ("entropy_short", 10),
        ("unknown_effect", 8),
        ("memfault", 7),
        ("divzero", 5),
    ] {
        let mut m = ClassicalMachine::new(&o, name, &[], &[]).unwrap();
        let before = m.snapshot();
        let result = m.run(1000).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(result.fault, Some(code), "{name}");
        assert!(result.values.is_empty());
        if name == "entropy_short" {
            assert_eq!(m.effect_tape_len(), 0);
        }
        m.reverse().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), before, "{name}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn host_request_reply_records_full_length_and_reverses_bytes() {
    let o = Object::parse(include_str!("fixtures/classical.bisa")).unwrap();
    let mut m = ClassicalMachine::new(&o, "host", &[], &[]).unwrap();
    let before = m.snapshot();
    let waiting = m.run(100).unwrap();
    let request = waiting.request.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(request.service, "org.bennett.test");
    assert_eq!(request.payload, [165, 0, 0]);
    m.reply(&[17, 34, 51, 68, 85]).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(m.memory_bytes(request.address, 3).unwrap(), [17, 34, 51]);
    let result = m.run(100).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(result.values, vec![ClassicalValue::int(16, 5).unwrap()]);
    m.reverse().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(m.snapshot(), before);
    assert!(m.reply(&[]).is_err());
    let mut invalid = ClassicalMachine::new(&o, "host_invalid", &[], &[]).unwrap();
    let result = invalid.run(100).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(result.fault, Some(7));
    assert!(result.request.is_none());
}
````

## `tests/cli_xam.rs` (1522 lines)

````rust
//! CLI commands of bead b-isa-spec-xam (`run-cc`, `reverse`, `run-action`,
//! `run-program`) for the dialect 0.2 pre-flight checker. Every expected
//! value below is hand-derived from the fixture text and the ISA rules cited
//! in the comments; the fixtures' own `.comments` files carry the same
//! derivations for the library-level outcomes.
mod support;
use bennett_isa_ref::{json::Json, Object};
use std::process::Command;

fn fixture(name: &str) -> String {
    format!("{}/tests/fixtures/{name}.bisa", env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
}
fn cli(args: &[&str]) -> std::process::Output {
    Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_bennett-isa-ref"))
        .args(args)
        .output()
        .unwrap()
}
fn ok(args: &[&str]) -> Json {
    let output = cli(args);
    assert!(
        output.status.success(),
        "{}",
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
    );
    Json::parse(std::str::from_utf8(&output.stdout).unwrap()).unwrap()
}
fn fails(args: &[&str], needle: &str) {
    let output = cli(args);
    assert_eq!(
        output.status.code(),
        Some(1),
        "stdout: {}",
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout)
    );
    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
    assert!(stderr.contains(needle), "{stderr} must contain {needle}");
    assert!(
        stderr.contains('§'),
        "diagnostic must cite the ISA: {stderr}"
    );
    assert!(output.stdout.is_empty(), "no partial JSON on a diagnostic");
}
fn field<'a>(v: &'a Json, key: &str) -> &'a Json {
    v.get(key)
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!("missing field {key} in {}", v.canonical()))
}
fn text<'a>(v: &'a Json, key: &str) -> &'a str {
    field(v, key).string().unwrap()
}
fn uint(v: &Json, key: &str) -> u128 {
    field(v, key).uint().unwrap()
}
fn array<'a>(v: &'a Json, key: &str) -> &'a [Json] {
    field(v, key).array().unwrap()
}
/// A `{"type":..,"value":..}` result object renders an iN as the unsigned
/// decimal string of its bit-vector value (the dialect checker's
/// INT(w):v form; bd note on b-isa-spec-xam records the reading).
fn result(v: &Json) -> (String, String) {
    (
        field(v, "type").string().unwrap().to_string(),
        field(v, "value").string().unwrap().to_string(),
    )
}
fn tmp_file(name: &str, contents: &str) -> String {
    let dir = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join(".tmp");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
    let path = dir.join(name);
    std::fs::write(&path, contents).unwrap();
    path.to_str().unwrap().to_string()
}

#[test]
fn run_cc_sum_reports_every_step_with_register_deltas() {
    // classical.bisa @sum(n) = n+(n-1)+...+1 (fixture comment). For n = 3 the
    // value is 6 and the executed rows are, by hand:
    //   entry 3 (const, const, br) + 3 loop passes x (icmp, br, sub, add, br)
    //   + final pass (icmp, br) + ret = 3 + 15 + 2 + 1 = 21 steps.
    let v = ok(&["run-cc", &fixture("classical"), "sum", "--args", "3"]);
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "status"), "COMPLETED");
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "budgets").len(), 0);
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "steps"), 21);
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "fault"), &Json::Null);
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "faults").len(), 0);
    assert_eq!(
        array(&v, "results").iter().map(result).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        [("i8".to_string(), "6".to_string())]
    );
    let trace = array(&v, "trace");
    assert_eq!(trace.len(), 21);
    // Step 0 is `zero = const.i8 0` in ^entry(): defines `zero` from nothing.
    let t0 = &trace[0];
    assert_eq!(text(t0, "function"), "sum");
    assert_eq!(text(t0, "block"), "entry");
    assert_eq!(uint(t0, "index"), 0);
    assert_eq!(text(t0, "op"), "const.i8");
    let registers = array(t0, "registers");
    assert_eq!(registers.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(text(&registers[0], "name"), "zero");
    assert_eq!(field(&registers[0], "pre"), &Json::Null);
    assert_eq!(
        result(field(&registers[0], "post")),
        ("i8".into(), "0".into())
    );
    assert_eq!(array(t0, "memory").len(), 0);
    assert_eq!(text(&trace[20], "op"), "ret");
    // --input is the same positional argument list under the run-oracle name.
    let alias = ok(&["run-cc", &fixture("classical"), "sum", "--input", "3"]);
    assert_eq!(alias, v);
}

#[test]
fn run_cc_effects_entropy_tape_console_and_memory_deltas() {
    // classical.bisa @effects with entropy [11, 22, 33]: entropy.read copies
    // the three bytes to the fresh 1024-byte allocation at heap_base 16,
    // console.write emits them, clock.read writes c = 0 (then c = 1),
    // block.write/read move 512 zero bytes, and the i64 load is 0 (fixture
    // comment; §7.3 device rows).
    let v = ok(&[
        "run-cc",
        &fixture("classical"),
        "effects",
        "--args",
        "",
        "--entropy",
        "0b1621",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "status"), "COMPLETED");
    assert_eq!(
        array(&v, "results").iter().map(result).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        [("i64".to_string(), "0".to_string())]
    );
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "console_hex"), "0b1621");
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "clock"), 1);
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "effect_tape_length"), 5);
    // Tape entries are (dev, op, args) of §7.3 plus the transferred bytes:
    // entropy bytes land verbatim; the clock writes eight little-endian
    // bytes of 0.
    let tape = array(&v, "tape");
    assert_eq!(tape.len(), 5);
    assert_eq!(text(&tape[0], "dev"), "entropy");
    assert_eq!(text(&tape[0], "op"), "read");
    assert_eq!(text(&tape[0], "bytes"), "0b1621");
    assert_eq!(
        array(&tape[0], "args")
            .iter()
            .map(|a| a.uint().unwrap())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        [16, 3]
    );
    assert_eq!(text(&tape[1], "dev"), "console");
    assert_eq!(text(&tape[1], "bytes"), "0b1621");
    assert_eq!(text(&tape[2], "dev"), "clock");
    assert_eq!(text(&tape[2], "bytes"), "0000000000000000");
    assert_eq!(text(&tape[3], "dev"), "block");
    assert_eq!(text(&tape[3], "bytes").len(), 1024);
    // The entropy.read is step 3 (const, alloc, const, effect): three memory
    // bytes change 0 -> 11, 22, 33 at the allocation base 16.
    let t3 = &array(&v, "trace")[3];
    assert_eq!(text(t3, "op"), "effect");
    let memory = array(t3, "memory");
    assert_eq!(memory.len(), 3);
    for (i, want) in [11u128, 22, 33].iter().enumerate() {
        assert_eq!(uint(&memory[i], "address"), 16 + i as u128);
        assert_eq!(uint(&memory[i], "pre"), 0);
        assert_eq!(uint(&memory[i], "post"), *want);
    }
}

#[test]
fn run_cc_hostcall_consumes_a_checked_replies_file() {
    // classical.bisa @host stores a5 in a 3-byte allocation at 16 and issues
    // hostcall org.bennett.test p n; the request payload is a5 00 00. The
    // reply 11 22 33 44 55 writes its first three bytes and rlen is the full
    // reply length 5 (§10 hostcall; fixture comment).
    let replies = tmp_file(
        "xam-host-replies.json",
        r#"[{"payload":"a50000","reply":"1122334455","service":"org.bennett.test"}]"#,
    );
    let v = ok(&[
        "run-cc",
        &fixture("classical"),
        "host",
        "--args",
        "",
        "--replies",
        &replies,
    ]);
    assert_eq!(
        array(&v, "results").iter().map(result).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        [("i16".to_string(), "5".to_string())]
    );
    let requests = array(&v, "host_requests");
    assert_eq!(requests.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(text(&requests[0], "service"), "org.bennett.test");
    assert_eq!(text(&requests[0], "payload"), "a50000");
    assert_eq!(text(&requests[0], "reply"), "1122334455");
    assert_eq!(uint(&requests[0], "address"), 16);
    assert_eq!(uint(&requests[0], "capacity"), 3);
    // A reply that names the wrong payload is a §10 mismatch, not a result;
    // an unanswered HOST_REQUEST is likewise a diagnostic.
    let wrong = tmp_file(
        "xam-host-wrong.json",
        r#"[{"payload":"00","reply":"","service":"org.bennett.test"}]"#,
    );
    fails(
        &[
            "run-cc",
            &fixture("classical"),
            "host",
            "--args",
            "",
            "--replies",
            &wrong,
        ],
        "§10",
    );
    fails(
        &["run-cc", &fixture("classical"), "host", "--args", ""],
        "HOST_REQUEST",
    );
}

#[test]
fn run_cc_fault_is_a_failed_result_not_a_diagnostic() {
    // classical.bisa @divzero computes 3/0: FAULT_UB_DIV0 = 5 (§5.4), no
    // values (§10: a FAILED run exposes no values).
    let v = ok(&["run-cc", &fixture("classical"), "divzero", "--args", ""]);
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "status"), "FAILED");
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "fault"), 5);
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "results").len(), 0);
    let faults = array(&v, "faults");
    assert_eq!(faults.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(uint(&faults[0], "code"), 5);
    assert_eq!(text(&faults[0], "name"), "FAULT_UB_DIV0");
    // Steps: const 3, const 0, udiv (the faulting row executes and halts).
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "steps"), 3);
}

#[test]
fn run_cc_rejects_bad_entries_and_arguments_loudly() {
    // 256 does not fit the i8 parameter (§10 positional INT binding: E_ARG).
    fails(
        &["run-cc", &fixture("classical"), "sum", "--args", "256"],
        "E_ARG",
    );
    // @sum takes one argument, not zero.
    fails(
        &["run-cc", &fixture("classical"), "sum", "--args", ""],
        "E_ARG",
    );
    // An action is not a CC/R entry (§3.4).
    fails(
        &["run-cc", &fixture("actions"), "bell", "--args", ""],
        "§3.4",
    );
    fails(
        &["run-cc", &fixture("classical"), "missing", "--args", ""],
        "§3.4",
    );
    // Both spellings of the argument list at once is ambiguous.
    fails(
        &[
            "run-cc",
            &fixture("classical"),
            "sum",
            "--args",
            "3",
            "--input",
            "3",
        ],
        "--args",
    );
}

#[test]
fn reverse_cc_restores_the_entry_state_after_effects() {
    // Whole-run reversal (§7.4 LIFO history traversal, §10 bennett_reverse,
    // T4): the effects run of 11 instructions (const, alloc, const, the
    // sector const and 5 effects, load, ret) is undone frame by frame, so
    // the console is empty again, the clock returns to 0, the formerly
    // absent block sector is absent again, and the whole snapshot equals
    // the entry snapshot.
    let v = ok(&[
        "reverse",
        &fixture("classical"),
        "effects",
        "--args",
        "",
        "--entropy",
        "0b1621",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "status"), "REVERSED");
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "steps"), 11);
    assert_eq!(
        array(&v, "results").iter().map(result).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        [("i64".to_string(), "0".to_string())]
    );
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "equals_entry"), &Json::Bool(true));
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "memory_equals_entry"), &Json::Bool(true));
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "first_difference"), &Json::Null);
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "console"), "");
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "console_hex"), "");
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "clock"), 0);
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "effect_tape_length"), 0);
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "memory_digest"), text(&v, "entry_memory_digest"));
    // The forward run's memory digest differs from the entry digest, so the
    // equality above is a restoration, not an untouched run.
    let forward = ok(&[
        "run-cc",
        &fixture("classical"),
        "effects",
        "--args",
        "",
        "--entropy",
        "0b1621",
    ]);
    assert_ne!(text(&forward, "memory_digest"), text(&v, "memory_digest"));
}

#[test]
fn reverse_cc_prefix_stops_and_reverses_mid_run() {
    // --steps 5 runs the first five instructions of @sum(3) (const, const,
    // br, icmp, br -- still inside the loop), then reverses that prefix.
    let v = ok(&[
        "reverse",
        &fixture("classical"),
        "sum",
        "--args",
        "3",
        "--steps",
        "5",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "status"), "REVERSED");
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "steps"), 5);
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "results").len(), 0);
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "fault"), &Json::Null);
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "equals_entry"), &Json::Bool(true));
}

#[test]
fn reverse_cc_measurement_is_not_reversible() {
    // registers.bisa @measurement measures a Bell pair; §10 reverse
    // eligibility excludes any run containing measure (E_NOT_REVERSIBLE).
    fails(
        &[
            "reverse",
            &fixture("registers"),
            "measurement",
            "--args",
            "",
            "--draws",
            "0.1",
        ],
        "E_NOT_REVERSIBLE",

#[test]
fn reverse_oracle_prefix_reversal_restores_the_basis_tuple() {
    // §14.1/§3.6 prefix reversal of inc8 at B = 3: three forward steps give
    // F_3(8) = 9, code 0; three inverse steps restore the complete entry
    // tuple (pc 0, all §3.7 counters 0, x = 8, regs one = r = 0) with every
    // frame clean (T2).
    let v = ok(&[
        "reverse",
        &fixture("inc8"),
        "inc8",
        "--input",
        "8",
        "--budget",
        "3",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "status"), "REVERSED");
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "payload"), 9);
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "code"), 0);
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "steps"), 3);
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "reverse_steps"), 3);
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "equals_entry"), &Json::Bool(true));
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "frames_clean"), &Json::Bool(true));
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "first_difference"), &Json::Null);
    let state = field(&v, "state_after_reversal");
    assert_eq!(uint(state, "pc"), 0);
    assert_eq!(field(state, "faulted"), &Json::Bool(false));
    assert_eq!(
        array(state, "counters")
            .iter()
            .map(|c| c.uint().unwrap())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        [0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
    );
    let locations = field(state, "locations");
    assert_eq!(locations.get("inc8.x").unwrap().uint().unwrap(), 8);
    assert_eq!(locations.get("inc8.one").unwrap().uint().unwrap(), 0);
    assert_eq!(locations.get("inc8.r").unwrap().uint().unwrap(), 0);
    // At prefix 2 of the same budget the commit is not at HALT, so the code
    // is FAULT_BUDGET_STEPS (1) with payload 0, as run-oracle reports for
    // F_2; the two inverse steps still restore the entry tuple.
    let prefix = ok(&[
        "reverse",
        &fixture("inc8"),
        "inc8",
        "--input",
        "8",
        "--budget",
        "3",
        "--steps",
        "2",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(uint(&prefix, "payload"), 0);
    assert_eq!(uint(&prefix, "code"), 1);
    assert_eq!(uint(&prefix, "steps"), 2);
    assert_eq!(uint(&prefix, "reverse_steps"), 2);
    assert_eq!(field(&prefix, "equals_entry"), &Json::Bool(true));
}

#[test]
fn reverse_action_adjoint_returns_to_the_entry_state() {
    // actions.bisa @bell applies h t[0]; cx t[0] t[1] to the mut bundle t
    // (in bundle p untouched). From |0000> over the interface order
    // (t0, t1, p0, p1) the forward state is (|0000> + |1100>)/sqrt(2); the
    // adjoint then restores |0000> exactly (§10: top-level Q calls reverse
    // by adjoint).
    let v = ok(&[
        "reverse",
        &fixture("actions"),
        "bell",
        "--mut",
        "0",
        "--in",
        "0",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "status"), "REVERSED");
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "equals_entry"), &Json::Bool(true));
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "first_difference"), &Json::Null);
    let forward = field(&v, "forward_state").object().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(forward.len(), 2);
    for key in ["0000", "1100"] {
        let amp = forward[key].array().unwrap();
        let re: f64 = amp[0].canonical().parse().unwrap();
        assert!(
            (re - std::f64::consts::FRAC_1_SQRT_2).abs() < 1e-12,
            "{key}: {re}"
        );
    }
    let state = field(&v, "state").object().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(state.len(), 1);
    let amp = state["0000"].array().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(amp[0].canonical(), "1");
    assert_eq!(amp[1].canonical(), "0");
}

#[test]
fn reverse_rejects_unknown_symbols_and_bad_prefixes() {
    fails(
        &["reverse", &fixture("classical"), "missing", "--args", ""],
        "§",
    );
    // A prefix longer than the oracle budget cannot run (B frames, §3.6).
    fails(
        &[
            "reverse",
            &fixture("inc8"),
            "inc8",
            "--input",
            "8",
            "--budget",
            "2",
            "--steps",
            "3",
        ],
        "§5.4",
    );
    // run-cc does not take --steps.
    fails(
        &[
            "run-cc",
            &fixture("classical"),
            "sum",
            "--args",
            "3",
            "--steps",
            "2",
        ],
        "--steps is a reverse option",
    );
}

#[test]
fn run_action_bell_from_basis_values() {
    // registers.bisa @bell (mut wire[2] only): h t[0]; cx t[0] t[1] maps
    // |00> to (|00> + |11>)/sqrt(2) in interface order (t0, t1). This is the
    // exact shape the dialect checker's state= examples consume: one JSON
    // `state` object keyed by bit string with [re, im] amplitudes.
    let v = ok(&["run-action", &fixture("registers"), "bell", "--mut", "0"]);
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "action"), "bell");
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "wires"), 2);
    let state = field(&v, "state").object().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(state.len(), 2);
    for key in ["00", "11"] {
        let amp = state[key].array().unwrap();
        let re: f64 = amp[0].canonical().parse().unwrap();
        let im: f64 = amp[1].canonical().parse().unwrap();
        assert!(
            (re - std::f64::consts::FRAC_1_SQRT_2).abs() < 1e-12,
            "{key}: {re}"
        );
        assert_eq!(im, 0.0);
    }
    // The mut bundle has no definite basis value, reported as null (never a
    // guessed outcome).
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "mut"), [Json::Null]);
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "in").len(), 0);
    // registers.bisa @toggle flips its single wire: |0> -> |1> exactly.
    let v = ok(&["run-action", &fixture("registers"), "toggle", "--mut", "0"]);
    let state = field(&v, "state").object().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(state.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(state["1"].canonical(), "[1,0]");
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "mut")[0].uint().unwrap(), 1);
}

#[test]
fn run_action_permutation_basis_and_adjoint() {
    // actions.bisa @flip computes t ^= p (fixture comment). With t = 1 and
    // p = 2 the result is t = 3, p = 2; in interface order (t0,t1,p0,p1)
    // that is |1101>. The same run spelled --basis starts from
    // (t0,t1,p0,p1) = 1001. flip is its own adjoint, so the adjoint run
    // from t = 3, p = 2 returns t = 1.
    let v = ok(&[
        "run-action",
        &fixture("actions"),
        "flip",
        "--mut",
        "1",
        "--in",
        "2",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "state").canonical(), "{\"1101\":[1,0]}");
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "mut")[0].uint().unwrap(), 3);
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "in")[0].uint().unwrap(), 2);
    let basis = ok(&["run-action", &fixture("actions"), "flip", "--basis", "1001"]);
    assert_eq!(field(&basis, "state"), field(&v, "state"));
    assert_eq!(array(&basis, "mut")[0].uint().unwrap(), 3);
    let adjoint = ok(&[
        "run-action",
        &fixture("actions"),
        "flip",
        "--mut",
        "3",
        "--in",
        "2",
        "--adjoint",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(field(&adjoint, "adjoint"), &Json::Bool(true));
    assert_eq!(array(&adjoint, "mut")[0].uint().unwrap(), 1);
    assert_eq!(field(&adjoint, "state").canonical(), "{\"1001\":[1,0]}");
}

#[test]
fn run_action_state_vector_input() {
    // The adjoint of Bell preparation maps (|00> + |11>)/sqrt(2) back to
    // |00>: cx gives (|00> + |10>)/sqrt(2), then h on t0 interferes to
    // |00>. The specified amplitude is a binary64 whose exact dyadic value
    // cancels exactly on the other component, so the support is a single
    // component of amplitude sqrt(2) * 0.7071067811865475 ~ 1.
    let v = ok(&[
        "run-action",
        &fixture("registers"),
        "bell",
        "--state",
        "00=0.7071067811865475,0;11=0.7071067811865475,0",
        "--adjoint",
    ]);
    let state = field(&v, "state").object().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(state.len(), 1);
    let amp = state["00"].array().unwrap();
    let re: f64 = amp[0].canonical().parse().unwrap();
    assert!((re - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12, "{re}");
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "mut")[0].uint().unwrap(), 0);
}

#[test]
fn run_action_mem_region_and_borrow_pool() {
    // control_flow.bisa @exchange swaps t with m[a] (fixture comment):
    // t = 2, a = 1, m = [1, 3] (one byte per 2-bit cell) gives t = 3 and
    // m = [1, 2]. All seven interface wires (t0,t1,a,m0.0,m0.1,m1.0,m1.1)
    // are then 1111001.
    let v = ok(&[
        "run-action",
        &fixture("control_flow"),
        "exchange",
        "--mut",
        "2",
        "--in",
        "1",
        "--mem",
        "m=0103",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "mut")[0].uint().unwrap(), 3);
    assert_eq!(
        field(field(&v, "mem"), "m")
            .array()
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .map(|c| c.uint().unwrap())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        [1, 2]
    );
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "state").canonical(), "{\"1111001\":[1,0]}");
    // Without --mem the region cells start zero: t swaps with m[1] = 0.
    let v = ok(&[
        "run-action",
        &fixture("control_flow"),
        "exchange",
        "--mut",
        "2",
        "--in",
        "1",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "mut")[0].uint().unwrap(), 0);
    assert_eq!(
        field(field(&v, "mem"), "m")
            .array()
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .map(|c| c.uint().unwrap())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        [0, 2]
    );
    // control_flow.bisa @borrowed borrows one pool wire and computes
    // t ^= x independently of it: --mut 0 --in 1 gives t = 1.
    let v = ok(&[
        "run-action",
        &fixture("control_flow"),
        "borrowed",
        "--mut",
        "0",
        "--in",
        "1",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "mut")[0].uint().unwrap(), 1);
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "state").canonical(), "{\"11\":[1,0]}");
}

#[test]
fn run_action_rejects_ambiguous_and_malformed_inputs() {
    let bell = fixture("registers");
    // Exactly one state mode.
    fails(
        &["run-action", &bell, "bell", "--mut", "0", "--basis", "00"],
        "exactly one of --mut, --basis, --state",
    );
    fails(
        &["run-action", &bell, "bell"],
        "exactly one of --mut, --basis, --state",
    );
    // --in only accompanies --mut.
    fails(
        &["run-action", &bell, "bell", "--basis", "00", "--in", "0"],
        "--in accompanies --mut only",
    );
    // Wrong bit-string length (2 interface wires).
    fails(&["run-action", &bell, "bell", "--basis", "000"], "§14.2");
    // A zero-amplitude state component is not a component.
    fails(&["run-action", &bell, "bell", "--state", "00=0,0"], "§14.2");
    // An oracle is not an action, and unknown names fail loudly.
    fails(
        &["run-action", &fixture("inc8"), "inc8", "--mut", "0"],
        "§5.3",
    );
    fails(&["run-action", &bell, "missing", "--mut", "0"], "§5.3");
}

#[test]
fn run_program_region_calls_complete_and_close() {
    // registers.bisa @views: qreg.new, slice, action_call @toggle, slice,
    // action_call @toggle, qreg.free, ret = 7 instructions with no result
    // values (fixture comment). The one-shot §10 launch walks
    // CREATED -> RUNNING -> COMPLETED and closes the run record.
    let v = ok(&["run-program", &fixture("registers"), "views", "--args", ""]);
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "status"), "COMPLETED");
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "run_state"), "CLOSED");
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "reversed"), &Json::Bool(false));
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "steps"), 7);
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "results").len(), 0);
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "faults").len(), 0);
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "fault"), &Json::Null);
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "measurements").len(), 0);
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "budgets").len(), 0);
    // With --reverse the completed run is reversed (§10) before closing.
    let v = ok(&[
        "run-program",
        &fixture("registers"),
        "views",
        "--args",
        "",
        "--reverse",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "status"), "REVERSED");
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "reversed"), &Json::Bool(true));
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "memory_equals_entry"), &Json::Bool(true));
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "equals_entry"), &Json::Bool(true));
}

#[test]
fn run_program_measurements_use_fixed_draws() {
    // registers.bisa @measurement: qreg.new, action_call @bell, measure,
    // ret = 4 instructions. Draw 0.9 selects the |11> branch above 1/2, so
    // the measured value and the i2 result are 3 (fixture comment). The
    // first allocated register has id 1.
    let v = ok(&[
        "run-program",
        &fixture("registers"),
        "measurement",
        "--args",
        "",
        "--draws",
        "0.9",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "status"), "COMPLETED");
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "steps"), 4);
    assert_eq!(
        array(&v, "results").iter().map(result).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        [("i2".to_string(), "3".to_string())]
    );
    let measurements = array(&v, "measurements");
    assert_eq!(measurements.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(uint(&measurements[0], "reg"), 1);
    assert_eq!(text(&measurements[0], "bits"), "11");
    assert_eq!(uint(&measurements[0], "value"), 3);
    // A run that measured is not reverse-eligible (§10).
    fails(
        &[
            "run-program",
            &fixture("registers"),
            "measurement",
            "--args",
            "",
            "--draws",
            "0.1",
            "--reverse",
        ],
        "E_NOT_REVERSIBLE",
    );
}

#[test]
fn run_program_failed_launch_exposes_no_values() {
    // registers.bisa @unclean: qreg.new, action_call @toggle, qreg.free
    // traps with FAULT_UB_TRAP (4) because the flipped register is not
    // clean (fixture comment). §10: a FAILED run exposes no values.
    let v = ok(&[
        "run-program",
        &fixture("registers"),
        "unclean",
        "--args",
        "",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "status"), "FAILED");
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "steps"), 3);
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "fault"), 4);
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "results").len(), 0);
    // bennett_reverse applies only to COMPLETED runs (§10).
    fails(
        &[
            "run-program",
            &fixture("registers"),
            "unclean",
            "--args",
            "",
            "--reverse",
        ],
        "E_INVALID_STATE",
    );
}

#[test]
fn run_program_oracle_call_with_qreg_and_token_arguments() {
    // A CC entry that calls the inc8 oracle as a region (§10 invocation
    // tree), linked from the inc8 fixture object the way tests/registers.rs
    // builds it. At token B = 3 the oracle delivers
    // t ^= (x + 1 mod 256): with x = 7 and entry t = 31 that is 31 ^ 8 =
    // 23; measuring t (a basis state, any draw) returns 23. Registers are
    // allocated in argument order, so t is register 2 and its bits in
    // wire-0-first order are 11101000.
    let inc = Object::parse(include_str!("fixtures/inc8.bisa")).unwrap();
    let oracle_sig = inc.symbols().unwrap()["0"]
        .get("signature")
        .unwrap()
        .canonical();
    let sig = r#"{"abi":"0.8","kind":"cc","params":["qreg[8]","qreg[8]","qreg[4]","token"],"results":["i8"],"tier":"cc"}"#;
    let body = "fn cc @invoke (x:qreg[8], t:qreg[8], f:qreg[4], tk:token) (r:i8) () () ()\n^entry():\noracle_call @inc8 tk (x) t f () ()\nr = measure t\nret r";
    let caller = support::rehash(&support::object(
        &[("invoke", sig, body)],
        &format!(r#"{{"inc8":{{"signature":{oracle_sig}}}}}"#),
        "",
    ));
    let linked = Object::link(&[caller, inc]).unwrap();
    let path = tmp_file("xam-invoke.bisa", &linked.text);
    let v = ok(&[
        "run-program",
        &path,
        "invoke",
        "--arg",
        "qreg:11100000",
        "--arg",
        "qreg:11111000",
        "--arg",
        "qreg:1100",
        "--arg",
        "token:3",
        "--draws",
        "0.5",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(text(&v, "status"), "COMPLETED");
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "steps"), 3);
    assert_eq!(
        array(&v, "results").iter().map(result).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        [("i8".to_string(), "23".to_string())]
    );
    let measurements = array(&v, "measurements");
    assert_eq!(measurements.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(uint(&measurements[0], "reg"), 2);
    assert_eq!(text(&measurements[0], "bits"), "11101000");
    assert_eq!(uint(&measurements[0], "value"), 23);
    let budgets = array(&v, "budgets");
    assert_eq!(budgets.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(uint(&budgets[0], "steps"), 3);
    assert_eq!(uint(&budgets[0], "heap"), 0);
}

#[test]
fn run_program_rejects_non_cc_entries_and_staged_inputs() {
    // §10: a run executes a device CC entry; an R or oracle symbol is E_ARG.
    fails(
        &["run-program", &fixture("classical"), "sum", "--args", "3"],
        "§10",
    );
    fails(
        &["run-program", &fixture("inc8"), "inc8", "--args", ""],
        "§10",
    );
    // bennett_load's target_jcs needs §8 target descriptions: staged
    // deliverable 9, an explicit diagnostic, never a silent run.
    let target = tmp_file("xam-target.json", "{}");
    let output = cli(&[
        "run-program",
        &fixture("registers"),
        "views",
        "--args",
        "",
        "--target",
        &target,
    ]);
    assert_eq!(output.status.code(), Some(1));
    assert!(output.stdout.is_empty(), "no partial JSON on a diagnostic");
    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
    assert!(stderr.contains("staged deliverable 9"), "{stderr}");
    assert!(stderr.contains("§8"), "{stderr}");
    // Even a missing target names the staged path rather than implying
    // that supplying an existing file could execute a §8 target.
    fails(
        &[
            "run-program",
            &fixture("registers"),
            "views",
            "--target",
            &format!("{target}/missing"),
        ],
        "staged deliverable 9",
    );
    // A schedule section needs verbatim scheduled execution: staged
    // deliverable 10 (§11 schedule consumer). The schedule JSON is the
    // valid inc8 schedule of tests/r1_certificates.rs.
    let schedule = Json::parse(&format!(
        r#"{{"bindings":{{"budget":[3,0,0,0],"closure_hash":"8ce5e64f15830d8e596ba9b4861def6565dd567b5804300f427d8b9566d5be93","epsilon":0,"expansion":{{"hash":"{}","name":"ref","version":"0.8"}},"inherited_controls":0,"params_hash":"{}","region":"inc8","scheduler":{{"name":"test","version":"1"}},"target_hash":"{}","variant":"forward"}},"entries":[{{"generated":"*","kind":"start","path":[{{"iteration":[],"point":"entry:0","symbol":"8ce5e64f15830d8e596ba9b4861def6565dd567b5804300f427d8b9566d5be93"}}],"phase":"fwd","start":{{"time":0}},"step":1}}]}}"#,
        "1".repeat(64),
        "2".repeat(64),
        "3".repeat(64)
    ))
    .unwrap()
    .canonical();
    let scheduled = tmp_file(
        "xam-scheduled.bisa",
        &format!(
            "{}\nsection schedule\n{schedule}\n",
            include_str!("fixtures/inc8.bisa")
        ),
    );
    let output = cli(&["run-program", &scheduled, "inc8", "--args", ""]);
    assert_eq!(output.status.code(), Some(1));
    assert!(output.stdout.is_empty(), "no partial JSON on a diagnostic");
    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
    assert!(stderr.contains("staged deliverable 10"), "{stderr}");
    assert!(stderr.contains("§11"), "{stderr}");
}

#[test]
fn run_action_mem_cells_wider_than_128_bits() {
    // A mem region of 2 cells of wire[300]: cell hex is 38 little-endian
    // bytes per cell. Cell 0 is 2^299 + 1 (byte 0 = 0x01, byte 37 = 0x08)
    // and cell 1 is zero; qexchm with a = 0 swaps it with t = 5, so t ends
    // at 2^299 + 1 and the cells are [5, 0]. Widths above 128 must not be
    // narrowed through u128 anywhere in the --mem path.
    let sig = r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[1],"kind":"perm_action","mem":[{"A":1,"W":300,"role":"mut"}],"mut":[300],"tier":"q"}"#;
    let body = "perm_action @wex (t:wire[300] mut) (a:wire in) (m:region[1,300] mut) () ()\n^entry():\nqexchm m a t";
    let layout = "\nsection layout\n{\"A_tab\":0,\"H\":4,\"S_cells\":0,\"globals\":{},\"heap_base\":1,\"heap_limit_max\":0,\"interface_regions\":{},\"null_size\":1,\"ptr_width\":32}\n";
    let text = support::rehash(&support::object(&[("wex", sig, body)], "{}", layout)).text;
    let path = tmp_file("xam-wide.bisa", &text);
    let mut cell0 = [0u8; 38];
    cell0[0] = 1;
    cell0[37] = 8;
    let mem: String = cell0
        .iter()
        .chain(&[0u8; 38])
        .map(|b| format!("{b:02x}"))
        .collect();
    let v = ok(&[
        "run-action",
        &path,
        "wex",
        "--mut",
        "5",
        "--in",
        "0",
        "--mem",
        &format!("m={mem}"),
    ]);
    // Decimal expansion of 2^299 + 1, independent of the interpreter.
    assert_eq!(array(&v, "mut")[0].string().unwrap(), "1018517988167243043134222844204689080525734196832968125318070224677190649881668353091698689");
    assert_eq!(
        field(field(&v, "mem"), "m")
            .array()
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .map(|c| c.uint().unwrap())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        [5, 0]
    );
}

#[test]
fn classical_commands_report_each_bound_budget_in_order() {
    // §10 positional binding: tk0 and tk1 are separated by an i8 argument.
    // The sole row returns x = 255; tokens consume no oracle steps because
    // this entry calls no oracle. §5.4 memoryless tokens have h=s=d=0.
    let sig =
        r#"{"abi":"0.8","kind":"cc","params":["token","i8","token"],"results":["i8"],"tier":"cc"}"#;
    let body = "fn cc @tokens (tk0:token, x:i8, tk1:token) (r:i8) () () ()\n^entry():\nret x";
    let object = support::rehash(&support::object(&[("tokens", sig, body)], "{}", ""));
    let path = tmp_file("xam-tokens.bisa", &object.text);
    let expected = Json::parse(
        r#"[{"depth":0,"heap":0,"stack":0,"steps":3},{"depth":0,"heap":0,"stack":0,"steps":7}]"#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    for command in ["run-cc", "reverse", "run-program"] {
        let v = ok(&[
            command, &path, "tokens", "--arg", "token:3", "--arg", "-1", "--arg", "token:7",
        ]);
        assert_eq!(field(&v, "budgets"), &expected);
        assert_eq!(
            field(&v, "results").canonical(),
            r#"[{"type":"i8","value":"255"}]"#
        );
        assert_eq!(uint(&v, "steps"), 1);
        if command == "reverse" {
            assert_eq!(field(&v, "equals_entry"), &Json::Bool(true));
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn measurement_json_preserves_the_high_bit_of_i128() {
    // §3.3/§14.2: measurement of a definite 128-wire register with only
    // wire 127 set returns 2^127 exactly. §9.1 encodes it as a decimal
    // string, both as an i128 result and as the measurement's value.
    let sig = r#"{"abi":"0.8","kind":"cc","params":["qreg[128]"],"results":["i128"],"tier":"cc"}"#;
    let body = "fn cc @wide (q:qreg[128]) (r:i128) () () ()\n^entry():\nr = measure q\nret r";
    let object = support::rehash(&support::object(&[("wide", sig, body)], "{}", ""));
    let path = tmp_file("xam-measure128.bisa", &object.text);
    let bits = format!("{}1", "0".repeat(127));
    for command in ["run-cc", "run-program"] {
        let v = ok(&[command, &path, "wide", "--arg", &format!("qreg:{bits}")]);
        assert_eq!(
            field(&v, "results").canonical(),
            r#"[{"type":"i128","value":"170141183460469231731687303715884105728"}]"#
        );
        let measurements = array(&v, "measurements");
        assert_eq!(measurements.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(text(&measurements[0], "bits"), bits);
        assert_eq!(
            text(&measurements[0], "value"),
            "170141183460469231731687303715884105728"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn r2_finite_rotations_render_when_the_combined_angle_exceeds_binary64() {
    for literal in [true, false] {
        let sig = if literal {
            r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}"#
        } else {
            r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":["f64"],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}"#
        };
        let angle = if literal { "1e+308" } else { "theta" };
        let params = if literal { "" } else { "theta:f64" };
        let body = format!("action @a (t:wire mut) () () ({params}) ()\n^entry():\nrz {angle} t\nrz {angle} t\nrz {angle} t\nrz {angle} t");
        let o = support::rehash(&support::object(&[("a", sig, &body)], "{}", ""));
        let path = tmp_file(
            if literal {
                "r2-large-literal.bisa"
            } else {
                "r2-large-arg.bisa"
            },
            &o.text,
        );
        for t in ["0", "1"] {
            let mut args = vec!["run-action", &path, "a", "--mut", t];
            if !literal {
                args.extend(["--arg", "f64:1e308"]);
            }
            let v = ok(&args);
            let state = field(&v, "state").object().unwrap();
            assert_eq!(state.len(), 1);
            let amp = state[t].array().unwrap();
            let re: f64 = amp[0].canonical().parse().unwrap();
            let im: f64 = amp[1].canonical().parse().unwrap();
            // theta is the EXACT binary64 1e308. Four single-gate phases
            // multiply to exp(-i*2*theta) on |0>, its conjugate on |1>.
            assert!((re - 0.588863244801576).abs() < 1e-12, "{re}");
            let sign = if t == "0" { 1.0 } else { -1.0 };
            assert!((im - sign * 0.8082326886001081).abs() < 1e-12, "{im}");
            assert!((re * re + im * im - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12);
            args[0] = "reverse";
            let v = ok(&args);
            assert_eq!(field(&v, "equals_entry"), &Json::Bool(true));
            assert_eq!(field(&v, "state").canonical(), format!("{{\"{t}\":[1,0]}}"));
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn r2_qinplace_identity_workspace_cleanup_runs_and_reverses() {
    let os =
        r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[1],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":1,"tier":"q"}"#;
    let ac = r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":["token"],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}"#;
    let text = support::object(&[("g", os, "oracle @g (x:wire in) (t:wire) (f:wire[4]) () ()\n^entry():\nlift.retval x"), ("a", ac, "action @a (t:wire mut) () () (tk:token) ()\n^entry():\nd = qalloc any 1\nqinplace @g @g tk d\nqinplace @g @g tk d\nqfree d")], "{}", "");
    let path = tmp_file("r2-qinplace-cli.bisa", &support::rehash(&text).text);
    for t in ["0", "1"] {
        for adj in [false, true] {
            let mut args = vec![
                "run-action",
                &path,
                "a",
                "--mut",
                t,
                "--arg",
                "token:1,0,0,0",
            ];
            if adj {
                args.push("--adjoint");
            }
            assert_eq!(
                field(&ok(&args), "state").canonical(),
                format!("{{\"{t}\":[1,0]}}")
            );
        }
        let v = ok(&["reverse", &path, "a", "--mut", t, "--arg", "token:1,0,0,0"]);
        assert_eq!(field(&v, "equals_entry"), &Json::Bool(true));
    }
    // Published sum_db's n=0 path: wrapper 4 + callee 6 = 10 rows;
    // 13 saved locations + 3 record cells = stack 16, payload and code zero.
    let v = ok(&[
        "run-oracle",
        &fixture("sum_db"),
        "sum_db",
        "--input",
        "0",
        "--budget",
        "10,4080,16,64",
    ]);
    assert_eq!(
        (uint(&v, "payload"), uint(&v, "code"), uint(&v, "steps")),
        (0, 0, 10)
    );
}

#[test]
fn r4_dynamic_region_aliases_report_failed_json_and_reverse_the_prefix() {
    for tier in ["cc", "r"] {
        for kind in ["interface", "control", "readonly-control", "oracle"] {
            let o = support::dynamic_region_alias_object(kind, tier);
            let path = tmp_file(&format!("r4-alias-{tier}-{kind}.bisa"), &o.text);
            for c in ["0", "1"] {
                for command in ["run-cc", "reverse", "run-program"] {
                    if command == "run-program" && tier == "r" {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let mut args = vec![
                        command, &path, "p", "--arg", c, "--arg", "qreg:0", "--arg", "qreg:1",
                    ];
                    if kind == "oracle" {
                        args.extend(["--arg", "qreg:0000", "--arg", "token:1"]);
                    }
                    let v = ok(&args);
                    // The faulting call is the second executed row. No ret or
                    // output delivery executes. §7.4 reversal undoes both frames.
                    assert_eq!(
                        text(&v, "status"),
                        if command == "reverse" {
                            "REVERSED"
                        } else if c == "1" {
                            "FAILED"
                        } else {
                            "COMPLETED"
                        }
                    );
                    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "steps"), if c == "1" { 2 } else { 3 });
                    assert_eq!(
                        field(&v, "fault"),
                        &if c == "1" {
                            Json::Number("4".into())
                        } else {
                            Json::Null
                        }
                    );
                    assert!(array(&v, "results").is_empty());
                    if c == "1" {
                        let faults = array(&v, "faults");
                        assert_eq!(faults.len(), 1);
                        assert_eq!(uint(&faults[0], "code"), 4);
                        assert_eq!(text(&faults[0], "name"), "FAULT_UB_TRAP");
                    }
                    if command == "reverse" {
                        assert_eq!(field(&v, "equals_entry"), &Json::Bool(true));
                        assert_eq!(field(&v, "first_difference"), &Json::Null);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn sol_r4_b01_tiny_born_branch_is_selectable() {
    // Rx(theta)|1> = -i sin(theta/2)|0> + cos(theta/2)|1>.
    // For nonzero theta, draw=0 selects the first supported outcome, even
    // when sin^2(theta/2) is below binary64's least positive number.
    let a = r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}"#;
    let p = r#"{"abi":"0.8","kind":"cc","params":["qreg[1]"],"results":["i1"],"tier":"cc"}"#;
    for angle in ["1e-100", "1e-161", "1e-162", "1e-200", "5e-324", "0.0"] {
        let action = format!("action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()\n^entry():\nrx {angle} t");
        let parent = "fn cc @p (q:qreg[1]) (r:i1) () () ()\n^entry():\naction_call @a (q) () () ()\nr = measure q\nret r";
        let o = support::rehash(&support::object(
            &[("a", a, &action), ("p", p, parent)],
            "{}",
            "",
        ));
        let path = tmp_file(&format!("sol-r4-b01-{angle}.bisa"), &o.text);
        ok(&["check", &path]);
        for draw in ["0", "0.5"] {
            let v = ok(&["run-cc", &path, "p", "--arg", "qreg:1", "--draws", draw]);
            let expected = if draw == "0" && angle != "0.0" {
                "0"
            } else {
                "1"
            };
            assert_eq!(text(&v, "status"), "COMPLETED");
            assert_eq!(uint(&v, "steps"), 3);
            assert_eq!(field(&v, "fault"), &Json::Null);
            assert_eq!(
                result(&array(&v, "results")[0]).1,
                expected,
                "angle={angle}, draw={draw}"
            );
            assert_eq!(text(&array(&v, "measurements")[0], "bits"), expected);
        }
        fails(
            &["reverse", &path, "p", "--arg", "qreg:1", "--draws", "0"],
            "measure",
        );
    }
}

fn r6_cli_map(case: &str) {
    let (body, h, oh) = support::r6_witness(case);
    let path = tmp_file(&format!("r6-{case}.bisa"), &body);
    let hashes = ok(&["hash", &path]);
    assert!(hashes.canonical().contains(h));
    assert!(hashes.canonical().contains(oh));
    ok(&["check", &path]);
    for (flag, input) in [
        ("--mut", "0"),
        ("--mut", "1"),
        ("--state", "0=0.6,0;1=0,0.8"),
    ] {
        for adj in [false, true] {
            let mut args = vec!["run-action", &path, "a", flag, input];
            if adj {
                args.push("--adjoint");
            }
            let v = ok(&args);
            assert_eq!(uint(&v, "wires"), 1);
            let state = field(&v, "state").object().unwrap();
            if case != "codex-boundary" {
                if flag == "--mut" {
                    assert_eq!(
                        field(&v, "state").canonical(),
                        format!("{{\"{input}\":[1,0]}}")
                    );
                } else {
                    let expected = [("0", (0.6, 0.0)), ("1", (0.0, 0.8))];
                    for (bits, (re, im)) in expected {
                        r6_amplitude(&state[bits], re, im);
                    }
                }
            } else {
                // H|0>, H|1>, and H(0.6|0>+0.8i|1>), derived directly.
                let s = std::f64::consts::FRAC_1_SQRT_2;
                let (a, b) = if flag == "--state" {
                    ((0.6 * s, 0.8 * s), (0.6 * s, -0.8 * s))
                } else {
                    ((s, 0.0), (if input == "0" { s } else { -s }, 0.0))
                };
                assert_eq!(state.len(), 2);
                r6_amplitude(&state["0"], a.0, a.1);
                r6_amplitude(&state["1"], b.0, b.1);
            }
        }
        let v = ok(&["reverse", &path, "a", flag, input]);
        assert_eq!(field(&v, "equals_entry"), &Json::Bool(true));
        assert_eq!(uint(&v, "wires"), 1);
    }
}
fn r6_amplitude(v: &Json, re: f64, im: f64) {
    let a = v.array().unwrap();
    for (n, expected) in a.iter().zip([re, im]) {
        let actual: f64 = n.canonical().parse().unwrap();
        assert!((actual - expected).abs() < 1e-12, "{actual} != {expected}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn r7_cli_restored() {
    r7_cli_identity("restored");
}

#[test]
fn r7_cli_loop_good() {
    r7_cli_identity("loop-good");
}

#[test]
fn r7_cli_diagonal() {
    r7_cli_identity("diagonal");
}

#[test]
fn r7_cli_control() {
    r7_cli_identity("control");
}

fn r7_cli_identity(case: &str) {
    let (body, h, oh) = support::r7_witness(case);
    let path = tmp_file(&format!("r7-{case}.bisa"), &body);
    let hashes = ok(&["hash", &path]);
    assert!(hashes.canonical().contains(h));
    if !oh.is_empty() {
        assert!(hashes.canonical().contains(oh));
    }
    ok(&["check", &path]);
    for (flag, input) in [
        ("--mut", "0"),
        ("--mut", "1"),
        ("--state", "0=0.6,0;1=0,0.8"),
    ] {
        for adj in [false, true] {
            let mut args = vec!["run-action", &path, "a", flag, input];
            if adj {
                args.push("--adjoint");
            }
            let v = ok(&args);
            assert_eq!(uint(&v, "wires"), 1);
            let state = field(&v, "state").object().unwrap();
            if flag == "--mut" {
                assert_eq!(
                    field(&v, "state").canonical(),
                    format!("{{\"{input}\":[1,0]}}")
                );
            } else {
                assert_eq!(state.len(), 2);
                r6_amplitude(&state["0"], 0.6, 0.0);
                r6_amplitude(&state["1"], 0.0, 0.8);
            }
        }
        let v = ok(&["reverse", &path, "a", flag, input]);
        assert_eq!(field(&v, "equals_entry"), &Json::Bool(true));
        assert_eq!(uint(&v, "wires"), 1);
    }
}

#[test]
fn r7_cli_bounded_5000_h_t_reports_finite_amplitudes() {
    let (body, h, oh) = support::r7_witness("float");
    let path = tmp_file("r7-float.bisa", &body);
    let hashes = ok(&["hash", &path]);
    assert!(hashes.canonical().contains(h));
    assert!(hashes.canonical().contains(oh));
    ok(&["check", &path]);
    // Independently evaluated (TH)^5000|0> at 100 decimal digits by the member.
    // The adjoint's first column is the conjugate first row; U_01=e^-iπ/4 U_10.
    for adj in [false, true] {
        let mut args = vec!["run-action", &path, "a", "--mut", "0"];
        if adj {
            args.push("--adjoint");
        }
        let v = ok(&args);
        assert_eq!(uint(&v, "wires"), 1);
        assert_eq!(field(&v, "mut").canonical(), "[null]");
        let state = field(&v, "state").object().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(state.len(), 2);
        r6_amplitude(
            &state["0"],
            -0.9438757756719142,
            if adj {
                -0.22414147502106144
            } else {
                0.22414147502106144
            },
        );
        r6_amplitude(
            &state["1"],
            if adj {
                0.09284243884403397
            } else {
                -0.09284243884403397
            },
            if adj {
                -0.22414147502106144
            } else {
                0.22414147502106144
            },
        );
        let norm: f64 = state
            .values()
            .flat_map(|x| x.array().unwrap())
            .map(|x| x.canonical().parse::<f64>().unwrap().powi(2))
            .sum();
        assert!((norm - 1.0).abs() < 1e-12);
    }
    let v = ok(&["reverse", &path, "a", "--mut", "0"]);
    assert_eq!(field(&v, "equals_entry"), &Json::Bool(true));
    assert_eq!(uint(&v, "wires"), 1);
}
````

````rust
mod support;
use bennett_isa_ref::Object;
use support::object;
const ACTION: &str =
    r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[1],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}"#;
const ORACLE: &str = r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":["token"],"fault":4,"in":[8],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":8,"tier":"q"}"#;
const INC: &str =
    r#"{"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[8],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":8,"tier":"q"}"#;
fn action(body: &str) -> String {
    object(
        &[(
            "a",
            ACTION,
            &format!("action @a (t:wire mut) (p:wire in) () () ()\n^entry():\n{body}"),
        )],
        "{}",
        "",
    )
}
fn reject(text: &str, rule: &str) {
    let error = match Object::parse(text) {
        Err(error) => error,
        Ok(_) => panic!("ill-formed cleanup accepted"),
    };
    assert!(error.to_string().contains(rule), "{error}");
}

#[test]
fn loop_cleanup_uses_all_iterations_and_lexical_bounds_once() {
    fn loop_action(body: &str, bounds: &[u64]) -> String {
        let mut text = action(body);
        let values = bounds
            .iter()
            .map(u64::to_string)
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join(",");
        text = text.replace("\"bounds\":[]", &format!("\"bounds\":[{values}]"));
        text.replace(
            "^entry():",
            &format!(
                "regs {{  }} bounds {{{}}}\n^entry():",
                values.replace(',', ", ")
            ),
        )
    }
    // X^(2^40) is identity. The verifier must not expand 2^40 iterations.
    Object::parse(&loop_action(
        "d = qalloc any 1\nqloop 1099511627776 {\nx d\n}\nqfree d",
        &[1099511627776],
    ))
    .unwrap();
    Object::parse(&loop_action(
        "qloop 3 {\nd = qalloc any 1\nqloop 2 {\nx d\n}\nqfree d\n}",
        &[3, 2],
    ))
    .unwrap();
    Object::parse(&loop_action(
        "d = qalloc any 1\nqloop 0 {\nx d\n}\nqfree d",
        &[0],
    ))
    .unwrap();
    reject(
        &loop_action("d = qalloc any 1\nqloop 3 {\nx d\n}\nqfree d", &[3]),
        "§6.2",
    );
    reject(
        &loop_action("qloop 2 {\nd = qalloc any 1\n}\nqfree d", &[2]),
        "§3.3",
    );
    reject(&loop_action("qloop 0 {\nmystery t\n}", &[0]), "§4.8");
}
````

## `tests/fixtures/actions.comments` (2 lines)

````
Hand derivations: flip computes d=p, XORs d into t and uncomputes d, so t XOR p with no garbage. memory has an all-zero 4x2-bit local image; load/unload cancels, two stores cancel and two memory exchanges cancel, so it is identity. loop flips t[0] three times, hence once. bell maps |00> to (|00>+|11>)/sqrt(2). Each adjoint composed after its action is identity including phase.
lifted starts r=1, then flip(r,x) computes r XOR x, so the oracle payload is x XOR 1 in three rows.
````

## `tests/fixtures/arithmetic.comments` (1 lines)

````
Hand-derived vectors: arithmetic is modulo 256. 255+2=1, 0-1=255, 128*3=128; 0xaa & 0xf0=0xa0, OR=0xfa, XOR=0x5a. Shifts >=8 give zero including signed right shift. Signed -7/2 truncates to -3 (253), remainder -1 (255). Signed -128/-1 faults 6, division by zero faults 5. sext(0x80) to 16 bits gives 0xff80; logical shift by 8 and trunc gives 255. parmov swaps 3 and 9, returns 9. jump(0,0) returns 42, jump(1,9) returns 9. badjump faults 4. fault0..fault10 XOR the named literal fault code and return no payload.
````

````
fn r @sum (n:i8) (answer:i8) () () ()
^entry():

one = const.i8 1

^loop(i:i8, acc:i8):

^more(ii:i8, aa:i8):
next = sub ii one
s = add aa ii
br ^loop(next, s)
^done(answer:i8):
ret answer
````

## `tests/fixtures/classical.comments` (2 lines)

````
Hand derivations: sum(n) accumulates n+(n-1)+...+1, hence n(n+1)/2 for n<=8. nested calls f, whose clock.read in g is cancelled by an inner uncall; uncalling f must skip those frames, leaving clock=0. effects copies entropy [11,22,33] to console, clock.read writes initial 0, then block.write/read sector 7; five tape entries, clock=1, return 0. Whole reversal removes the formerly absent sector. impure performs store after g, so uncall faults 4. entropy_short has live destination but empty tape and faults 10 atomically. Unknown device faults 8. Null load faults 7; 3/0 faults 5.
Host: request is a5 00 00 in a three-byte allocation. Reply 11 22 33 44 55 writes 11 22 33 and returns full length 5; reversal restores the original bytes and then allocation. Null host pointer faults 7 before making a request.
````

## `tests/fixtures/control_flow.comments` (14 lines)

````
Hand-derived expectations, recorded before execution:
while3: flag_i is AND of p[0] through p[i]. X flips t once per true flag.
Thus t is XORed with the parity of the initial consecutive ones in p, and p
is unchanged. At p=3 (011) it flips twice; at p=5 (101) it flips once.
Adjoint reverses those same enabled iterations and clears all three flags.
conditional: starting with t=0 and p=+ gives amplitudes [0,1/sqrt(2),1/2,1/2]
in allocation order (t low bit). Applying the adjoint restores t=0,p=+.
controlled_phase: Rz(2*pi) = -I on t. Controlled by p, it is Z on p;
H p; controlled_phase; H p therefore produces p=1 with probability one.
exchange: qexchm swaps t with m[a] and leaves the other cell unchanged.
image: data dead has cell0=0xde and cell1=0xad. With t initially0x35 the
result is0xeb or0x98 respectively. Scratch and local image are restored.
borrowed: CX x,b; CX b,t; CX x,b; CX b,t gives t XOR x, restores b,
and has no dependence on b, including when b is entangled externally.
````

## `tests/fixtures/heap.comments` (1 lines)

````
Hand-derived vectors: heap_base=32, heap_limit=32, initial pinned g=(16,1); table capacity=4. heap allocates two bytes at 32, stores 0x1234 little endian (34 12), loads 4660. heap_limit=1 faults 2. Two zero-sized allocations still consume one byte each, so returned pointers differ by 1. Freed, pinned, double-freed, null store accesses fault 7. Three new allocations fill the table; the fourth faults 2. faultif(true,9) gives (0,9).
````

## `tests/fixtures/nested.comments` (1 lines)

````
Hand derivation: inc8(8)=9 in three rows. nested calls it, compares fr to zero, and raises FAULT_CALLEE=9 on an unsuccessful inner budget. cancel calls then uncalls with identical ins/mem/token, so target and fr return to zero even for a callee fault. ignore returns a zero payload when the callee faults without automatic propagation. inc8(255)=0 by 8-bit wrap.
````

## `tests/fixtures/registers.comments` (1 lines)

````
Hand-derived vectors: allocation concatenates two clean one-wire qregs and frees the resulting clean two-wire qreg. views flips bit 0 through a view twice; each region call consumes that view and restores its parent to live, so free succeeds. unclean flips a one-wire qreg once, so free traps with code 4 before consuming it. measurement produces Bell amplitudes at 00 and 11, probabilities 1/2; draws 0.1 and 0.9 select 0 and 3 respectively. measuring (CC, since an R function may call only R functions, §3.1 / SPEC-QUESTIONS 19) wraps that call; bad_uncall must trap 4 because the uncalled CC segment contains a measure frame (§7.4). Reversal restores handle states and wire identities for reversible traces; measurement traces are ineligible.
````

## `tests/fixtures/tiny_memory.comments` (1 lines)

````
Hand derivation over full D (14 bits): input x is one bit, db is one caller-owned byte, target one bit, fault four bits. Rows: addr, zext x, load db, udiv(db,x), const one, and, icmp, retval. x=0 faults DIV0=5 at row 4. x=1 returns db&1 at row 8. Earlier prefixes give step-budget fault 1. B=9 has one idle HALT frame. Every target/fault entry value is checked by explicit commit and every internal location/frame/byte/pre-entry must restore.
````

## `tests/fixtures/wide.comments` (12 lines)

````
Hand expectations, recorded before execution:
x=2^200+3=1606938044258990275541962092341162602522202993782792835301379;
y=2^100+5=1267650600228229401496703205381.
div257 quotient=2^100-5=1267650600228229401496703205371, remainder28,
since (2^100-5)(2^100+5)=2^200-25. It finishes in2 rows; B1 faults1.
add257 computes (x+y) mod2^257 in2 rows.
call257 captures x into id257, returns x, then retval:3 rows. id257's frame
has3 metadata+1 parameter+1 result=5 cells. stack4 faults3 on the first row;
stack5 and depth1 suffice. Every complete prefix must reverse.
fault257 emits code2^200+3 in one row, no payload, high bit200 retained.
fault_small257 has the same wide fault but one input bit: both inputs yield
that fault in one row. Its small input domain permits exhaustive CLI checking.
````

mod support;
use bennett_isa_ref::{sha256_hex, Object};

#[test]
fn fips_180_4_sha256_vectors() {
    for (input, expected) in [
        ("", "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"),
        ("abc", "ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad"),
        ("abcdbcdecdefdefgefghfghighijhijkijkljklmklmnlmnomnopnopq", "248d6a61d20638b8e5c026930c3e6039a33ce45964ff2167f6ecedd419db06c1"),
        ("abcdefghbcdefghicdefghijdefghijkefghijklfghijklmghijklmnhijklmnoijklmnopjklmnopqklmnopqrlmnopqrsmnopqrstnopqrstu", "cf5b16a778af8380036ce59e7b0492370b249b11e8f07a51afac45037afee9d1"),
    ] { assert_eq!(sha256_hex(input.as_bytes()), expected); }
    assert_eq!(
        sha256_hex(&vec![b'a'; 1_000_000]),
        "cdc76e5c9914fb9281a1c7e284d73e67f1809a48a497200e046d39ccc7112cd0"
    );
}

#[test]
fn all_four_published_hashes_and_printed_envelopes() {
    let spec = include_str!("../../spec/Bennett-ISA-Spec.md");
    let mut hashes = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    let mut envelopes = Vec::new();
    for fixture in [
        include_str!("fixtures/inc8.bisa"),
        include_str!("fixtures/sum_db.bisa"),
    ] {
        let object = Object::parse(fixture).unwrap();
        let identity = object.identity().unwrap();
        object.check_hashes().unwrap();
        for (name, hash) in identity.interface_hashes {
            assert_eq!(
                identity.closure_hashes[&name].as_deref(),
                Some(hash.as_str())
            );
            hashes.insert(name, hash);
        }
        envelopes.extend(identity.envelopes.into_values());
    }
    for (name, expected) in [
        (
            "inc8",
            "8ce5e64f15830d8e596ba9b4861def6565dd567b5804300f427d8b9566d5be93",
        ),
        (
            "zero",
            "7002ed5ea010907a0ae99065663f22fb7d18ca1d6cb171fed57e2594bd9367e6",
        ),
        (
            "sum",
            "74f110bbafde68a4785025e7e571ef871ddd83a09465ab9c1604f653a0cfcd92",
        ),
        (
            "sum_db",
            "68225d213c44812fe844cd295d8821127c3cf31682be4eb19303cb53f9b147f7",
        ),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(hashes[name], expected);
    }
    let mut count = 0;
    for block in spec.split("```\n").skip(1) {
        if block.starts_with("isa=0.8\n") {
            let envelope = block.split("```").next().unwrap();
            assert!(
                envelopes.iter().any(|e| e == envelope),
                "printed envelope differs byte-for-byte"
            );
            count += 1;
        }
    }
    assert_eq!(count, 2);
}

#[test]
fn object_hash_excludes_only_the_three_nonsemantic_sections() {
    let raw = include_str!("fixtures/inc8.bisa");
    let base = Object::parse(raw).unwrap().identity().unwrap();
    let annotated = format!("{raw}\nsection coverage\n{{\"entries\":[]}}\n");
    let after = Object::parse(&annotated).unwrap().identity().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(base.object_hash, sha256_hex(raw.as_bytes()));
    assert_eq!(base.object_hash, after.object_hash);
    assert!(
        Object::parse(&raw.replace("lift.const.i8 1", "lift.const.i8 2"))
            .unwrap()
            .check_hashes()
            .is_err()
    );
}

#[test]
fn reference_order_and_self_scc_are_observable() {
    let raw = include_str!("fixtures/sum_db.bisa");
    let base = Object::parse(raw).unwrap().identity().unwrap();
    let env = &base.envelopes["sum"];
    assert!(env.contains("lift.call @$0"));
    assert_eq!(
        base.interface_hashes["sum"],
        sha256_hex(format!("{}:0", sha256_hex(env.as_bytes())).as_bytes())
    );
    let shifted = Object::parse(&raw.replace("\"base\":16,\"image\"", "\"base\":17,\"image\""))
        .unwrap()
        .identity()
        .unwrap();
    assert_ne!(
        base.interface_hashes["sum"],
        shifted.interface_hashes["sum"]
    );
    assert_ne!(
        base.interface_hashes["sum_db"],
        shifted.interface_hashes["sum_db"]
    );
    assert_eq!(
        base.interface_hashes["zero"],
        shifted.interface_hashes["zero"]
    );
}

#[test]
fn unmodelled_effect_is_hashable_and_keeps_its_fault_semantics() {
    let o = Object::parse(include_str!("fixtures/classical.bisa")).unwrap();
    let identity = o.identity().unwrap();
    assert!(identity.envelopes["g"].contains("device clock {\"version\":\"0.8\"}\n"));
    assert!(!identity.envelopes["unknown_effect"].contains("device missing"));
}

#[test]
fn mutual_scc_hashing_and_canonical_lproc_member_order() {
    use bennett_isa_ref::{Budget, OracleInput};
    let o = Object::parse(include_str!("fixtures/mutual.bisa")).unwrap();
    let id = o.identity().unwrap();
    assert!(
        id.interface_hashes["f"] > id.interface_hashes["g"],
        "fixture must expose sorting by member hashes"
    );
    let digest = sha256_hex(format!("{}{}", id.envelopes["f"], id.envelopes["g"]).as_bytes());
    assert_eq!(
        id.interface_hashes["f"],
        sha256_hex(format!("{digest}:0").as_bytes())
    );
    assert_eq!(
        id.interface_hashes["g"],
        sha256_hex(format!("{digest}:1").as_bytes())
    );
    assert!(id.envelopes["f"].contains("lift.call @$1"));
    assert!(id.envelopes["g"].contains("lift.call @$0"));
    let r = o
        .run_oracle(
            "main",
            &OracleInput::bits(&[]),
            Budget {
                steps: 20,
                heap: 0,
                stack: 32,
                depth: 8,
            },
        )
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!((r.payload, r.code), (4, 0));
}

fn every_committed_fixture_has_valid_identity() {
    // The complete fixture audit is tests/r1_fixtures.rs (directory enumeration).
    // Independently hand-assembled device/layout envelope, checked by Python hashlib.
    let o = Object::parse(include_str!("fixtures/classical.bisa")).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        o.identity().unwrap().interface_hashes["g"],
        "e8a3dc5429049b16559aa6a4262779e3dcd37a758967def4e08c371a5b765fff"
    );
}

#[test]
fn council_r4_mutual_scc_has_independent_literal_envelopes() {
    // §9.2: f < g bytewise; headers are definitions, calls are references;
    // lprocs without lift.addr globals have NO layout leaves or part-(6) lines.
    let f = concat!(
        "isa=0.8\nptr_width=16\n",
        "{\"abi\":\"0.8\",\"kind\":\"lproc\",\"params\":[],\"result\":16,\"tier\":\"q\"}\n",
        "lproc @f () (r:reg[16]) () () ()\n^entry():\nr = lift.call @$1 ()\nlift.ret r\n"
    );
    let g = concat!(
        "isa=0.8\nptr_width=16\n",
        "{\"abi\":\"0.8\",\"kind\":\"lproc\",\"params\":[],\"result\":16,\"tier\":\"q\"}\n",
        "lproc @g () (r:reg[16]) () () ()\nregs { p:reg[1] }\n^entry():\n",
        "p = lift.const.i1 1\nqbranch p ^done ^recurse\n^done():\nr = lift.label ^entry\nlift.ret r\n",
        "^recurse():\nr = lift.call @$0 ()\nlift.ret r\n"
    );
    let digest = sha256_hex(format!("{f}{g}").as_bytes());
    let id = Object::parse(include_str!("fixtures/mutual.bisa"))
        .unwrap()
        .identity()
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(id.envelopes["f"], f);
    assert_eq!(id.envelopes["g"], g);
    assert_eq!(id.scc_members["f"], ["f", "g"]);
    assert_eq!(id.scc_hashes["f"], digest);
    assert_eq!(
        sha256_hex(format!("{digest}:0").as_bytes()),
        "e4028cf7347c2779e19c8193ef1039837944acebd4784e9c3a42fbe236e737ec"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        sha256_hex(format!("{digest}:1").as_bytes()),
        "7dc9c25aff5230a46ae697edf187d34ba72a03f7a3c1a520c6fc6bf5462c6374"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        id.interface_hashes["f"],
        sha256_hex(format!("{digest}:0").as_bytes())
    );
    assert_eq!(
        id.interface_hashes["g"],
        sha256_hex(format!("{digest}:1").as_bytes())
    );
}

#[test]
fn council_r4_cc_envelope_includes_service_but_not_unused_model() {
    // §4.8: effect is R-only, hostcall CC-only. A CC envelope includes its
    // service but not an unused declared model; both cannot be used directly.
    let raw = support::object(
        &[("mix", r#"{"abi":"0.8","kind":"cc","params":["ptr","i32"],"results":[],"tier":"cc"}"#,
        "fn cc @mix (p:ptr, n:i32) () () () ()\n^entry():\nr = hostcall a.service p n\nret")], "{}",
        "\nsection devices\n{\"models\":{\"clock\":{\"version\":\"0.8\"}},\"services\":{\"a.service\":{\"version\":\"1\"}}}\n\nsection layout\n{\"A_tab\":0,\"H\":0,\"S_cells\":0,\"globals\":{},\"heap_base\":1,\"heap_limit_max\":0,\"interface_regions\":{},\"null_size\":1,\"ptr_width\":32}\n"
    );
    let expected = concat!(
        "isa=0.8\nptr_width=32\n",
        "{\"abi\":\"0.8\",\"kind\":\"cc\",\"params\":[\"ptr\",\"i32\"],\"results\":[],\"tier\":\"cc\"}\n",
        "fn cc @mix (p:ptr, n:i32) () () () ()\n^entry():\nr = hostcall a.service p n\nret\n",
        "layout A_tab 0\nlayout H 0\nlayout S_cells 0\nlayout heap_base 1\nlayout heap_limit_max 0\nlayout null_size 1\nlayout ptr_width 32\n",
        "device a.service {\"version\":\"1\"}\n"
    );
    let id = Object::parse(&raw).unwrap().identity().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(id.envelopes["mix"], expected);
    assert_eq!(id.interface_hashes["mix"], sha256_hex(expected.as_bytes()));
}
